```rust
//! Trace → SM replay driver: flattens one traced kernel launch into per-SM
//! block replays using the REAL hardware placement recorded in the trace
//! (per-instruction `sm_id` / `warpid_sm`), joins each dynamic record to
//! the issue schedule (and, when an L1 setup is supplied, to the cache-op
//! manifest + per-record unique-sector expansion), and runs the issue
//! model on every SM.
//!
//! Placement policy v0: the traced placement IS the model — each block
//! runs on the SM the hardware ran it on, each warp on its physical warp
//! slot. Traces without `sm_id` are a typed error (a synthetic placement
//! model is a future knob, not a silent fallback).
//!
//! Memory-record classification (L1 mode): a global-class record takes
//! the [`MemRole`] its pc's SIDECAR OPCODE was classified to at join
//! time (`sim_mem::cache_op` port of the Python token rules) — eligible
//! load → modeled L1 sectors; bypass load → counted bypass; store head →
//! hit-tested without allocating; everything else → unified-denominator
//! count only. Sector expansion follows the `l1_trace_adapter` contract:
//! per-lane `addr>>5 ..= (addr+width-1)>>5`, deduplicated per INSTRUCTION
//! in first-seen order (active lanes are the non-sentinel slots — the
//! canonical positional guarantee).
//!
//! v0 limitation (fail-closed, not silent): every dynamic record of a
//! launch must carry the launch's own `function_unique_id` — traced device
//! function CALLs would need per-segment schedules and are rejected typed
//! until a trace exercises them (none of the 17 M1 traces does).
//!
//! Memory discipline: blocks are decoded ONE at a time and compacted
//! immediately (12-byte records + a per-warp sector arena); the prost tree
//! is dropped before the next block loads.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::path::PathBuf;

use sim_mem::{L1Config, L1Counters, push_unique_sectors};
use sim_trace::lanes::LANE_INACTIVE_SENTINEL;
use sim_trace::pb;
use sim_trace::{
    KernelLoc, TraceDir, TraceError, block_launch_index, check_allocation_identity, kernel_grid,
    read_threadblock, visit_memory_access,
};

use sim_mem::{L2Config, L2Counters, L2Model, MemRole};

use crate::issue::{
    AccessKind, BlockReplay, IssueError, IssueModelParams, ReplayInst, SmSimResult, WarpReplay,
    simulate_sm,
};
use crate::program::FunctionSchedule;
use crate::system::{DramBw, DramStats, L2SourceSplit, SystemError, simulate_kernel_shared};

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum ReplayError {
    #[error(transparent)]
    Trace(#[from] TraceError),
    #[error(transparent)]
    Issue(#[from] IssueError),
    #[error(transparent)]
    System(#[from] SystemError),
    #[error("L2 config invalid: {0}")]
    L2Config(#[from] sim_mem::L2ConfigError),
    #[error("no issue schedule for function_unique_id {function_unique_id}")]
    ScheduleMissing { function_unique_id: i32 },
    #[error(
        "{path}: warp {warp_id} record {record_ix} carries function_unique_id {found}, launch \
         kernel is {expected} — multi-function replay is not supported in v0"
    )]
    MultiFunctionUnsupported {
        path: PathBuf,
        warp_id: i32,
        record_ix: usize,
        expected: i32,
        found: i32,
    },
    #[error("{path}: no instruction record carries sm_id — v0 replay requires traced placement")]
    SmIdMissing { path: PathBuf },
    #[error(
        "{path}: sm_id changes within the block ({first} then {second}) — blocks never migrate"
    )]
    SmIdInconsistent {
        path: PathBuf,
        first: i32,
        second: i32,
    },
    #[error("{path}: warp {warp_id} warpid_sm changes within the warp ({first} then {second})")]
    WarpSlotInconsistent {
        path: PathBuf,
        warp_id: i32,
        first: i32,
        second: i32,
    },
    #[error(
        "{path}: warp {warp_id} has no warpid_sm on any record — v0 replay requires the traced \
         physical warp slot (sub-core assignment), like sm_id"
    )]
    WarpSlotMissing { path: PathBuf, warp_id: i32 },
    #[error(
        "{path}: warp {warp_id} record {record_ix}: {sectors} unique sectors in one record \
         overflows the u16 arena index"
    )]
    SectorCountOverflow {
        path: PathBuf,
        warp_id: i32,
        record_ix: usize,
        sectors: usize,
    },
    #[error("duplicate block launch index {index} across threadblock files")]
    DuplicateLaunchIndex { index: i64 },
    #[error(
        "issued {issued} != records {records} — replay invariant broken (every traced record \
         must issue exactly once)"
    )]
    CountMismatch { issued: u64, records: u64 },
    #[error(
        "E_INCOMPLETE_TRACE: {seen}/{grid_total} launch blocks present and no \
         trace_sampling.json sidecar — an incomplete trace must carry a sampling sidecar"
    )]
    IncompleteTrace { seen: u64, grid_total: u64 },
    #[error(
        "trace_sampling sidecar original_grid {sidecar:?} != launch gridDim {launch:?} \
         (a subset must NEVER rewrite gridDim)"
    )]
    GridDimRewritten {
        launch: (u32, u32, u32),
        sidecar: (u32, u32, u32),
    },
    #[error("records_seen {records_seen} != trace_sampling sidecar records.captured {captured}")]
    RecordsCapturedMismatch { records_seen: u64, captured: u64 },
    #[error(
        "trace_sampling sidecar selected block membership does not match replayed threadblocks \
         ({seen} seen, {declared} declared)"
    )]
    SelectedBlockMembershipMismatch { seen: u64, declared: u64 },
    #[error("trace_sampling sidecar kernel {sidecar:?} != launch kernel {launch:?}")]
    SamplingKernelMismatch { launch: String, sidecar: String },
    #[error("kernel launch block_dim is absent or degenerate")]
    BlockDimMissing,
    #[error("trace_sampling sidecar original_block {sidecar:?} != launch blockDim {launch:?}")]
    BlockDimRewritten {
        launch: (u32, u32, u32),
        sidecar: (u32, u32, u32),
    },
}

/// Replay outcome for one kernel launch.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct KernelReplayResult {
    /// Exact by construction: one issue per traced record (invariant-checked
    /// against `records_seen`).
    pub instructions_issued: u64,
    pub records_seen: u64,
    /// Per traced SM id.
    pub per_sm: BTreeMap<i32, SmSimResult>,
    /// Directional v0 proxy for `gpc__cycles_elapsed.max`.
    pub max_cycles: u64,
    /// Kernel-level L1 counters (sum over per-SM caches) in L1 mode.
    pub l1: Option<L1Counters>,
    /// Shared-L2 counters (the `replay_kernel_shared` path only).
    pub l2: Option<L2Counters>,
    /// Per-source L2 split from the driver-side emission observer.
    pub l2_by_source: Option<L2SourceSplit>,
    /// DRAM read-traffic observer (shared mode only).
    pub dram: Option<DramStats>,
}

/// Decode one launch into per-SM block replays on the traced placement.
/// `decode_sectors` selects the L1-mode classification (lane decode +
/// unique-sector expansion) over the flat-mode class check.
fn extract_per_sm_blocks(
    td: &TraceDir,
    loc: &KernelLoc<'_>,
    schedule: &FunctionSchedule,
    decode_sectors: bool,
) -> Result<(BTreeMap<i32, Vec<BlockReplay>>, u64), ReplayError> {
    let expected_fuid = schedule.function_unique_id;
    // sm_id → blocks (launch index kept for in-SM ordering).
    let mut per_sm_blocks: BTreeMap<i32, Vec<BlockReplay>> = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut seen_indices: BTreeSet<i64> = BTreeSet::new();
    let mut records_seen: u64 = 0;

    for path in td.threadblock_paths(loc)? {
        let tb = read_threadblock(&path)?;
        let launch_index = block_launch_index(loc.kernel, &tb, &path)?;
        if !seen_indices.insert(launch_index) {
            return Err(ReplayError::DuplicateLaunchIndex {
                index: launch_index,
            });
        }

        let mut block_sm: Option<i32> = None;
        let mut warps = Vec::with_capacity(tb.warps.len());
        for (&warp_id, warp) in &tb.warps {
            let mut warp_slot: Option<i32> = None;
            let mut insts = Vec::with_capacity(warp.instructions.len());
            let mut sectors: Vec<i64> = Vec::new();
            for (record_ix, inst) in warp.instructions.iter().enumerate() {
                records_seen += 1;
                // Allocation-identity gate on the path the simulator actually
                // consumes: a GLOBAL/GENERIC-space active record (ordinary global,
                // global atomic, LDGSTS source) must carry a resolvable, in-range
                // allocation id — parity with the Python validator and the
                // TraceDir reader. Fail-closed BEFORE classification so a
                // malformed record never reaches the L1/L2 model.
                check_allocation_identity(inst, td.allocations(), || {
                    format!("{} warp={warp_id} inst={record_ix}", path.display())
                })?;
                if inst.function_unique_id != expected_fuid {
                    return Err(ReplayError::MultiFunctionUnsupported {
                        path,
                        warp_id,
                        record_ix,
                        expected: expected_fuid,
                        found: inst.function_unique_id,
                    });
                }
                if let Some(sm) = inst.sm_id {
                    match block_sm {
                        None => block_sm = Some(sm),
                        Some(first) if first != sm => {
                            return Err(ReplayError::SmIdInconsistent {
                                path,
                                first,
                                second: sm,
                            });
                        }
                        Some(_) => {}
                    }
                }
                if let Some(slot) = inst.warpid_sm {
                    match warp_slot {
                        None => warp_slot = Some(slot),
                        Some(first) if first != slot => {
                            return Err(ReplayError::WarpSlotInconsistent {
                                path,
                                warp_id,
                                first,
                                second: slot,
                            });
                        }
                        Some(_) => {}
                    }
                }
                let kind = if decode_sectors {
                    classify_with_l1(inst, schedule, &mut sectors, &path, warp_id, record_ix)?
                } else {
                    classify_flat(inst, &path, warp_id, record_ix)?
                };
                insts.push(ReplayInst { pc: inst.pc, kind });
            }
            // Fail-closed traced placement: a warp that issued records
            // without ever exposing its physical slot is a typed error,
            // exactly like a block without sm_id (a synthetic placement
            // model is a future knob, never a silent fallback). Warps
            // with NO records carry no placement and issue nothing.
            let warp_slot = match warp_slot {
                Some(slot) => slot,
                None if insts.is_empty() => warp_id,
                None => {
                    return Err(ReplayError::WarpSlotMissing { path, warp_id });
                }
            };
            warps.push(WarpReplay {
                warp_slot,
                insts,
                sectors,
            });
        }
        let Some(sm) = block_sm else {
            return Err(ReplayError::SmIdMissing { path });
        };
        per_sm_blocks.entry(sm).or_default().push(BlockReplay {
            launch_index,
            warps,
        });
    }
    // Completeness gate (fail-closed) on the path replay ACTUALLY consumes: a
    // subset trace (coverage < grid) is admissible ONLY with a valid
    // trace_sampling.json sidecar whose original_grid matches the launch record
    // (gridDim is never rewritten) and whose captured record count matches
    // records_seen. Absent/non-sampling sidecars never waive full coverage.
    let (gx, gy, gz) = kernel_grid(loc.kernel)?;
    let grid_total = u64::from(gx) * u64::from(gy) * u64::from(gz);
    let seen = seen_indices.len() as u64;
    match td.sampling_sidecar() {
        None => {
            if seen < grid_total {
                return Err(ReplayError::IncompleteTrace { seen, grid_total });
            }
        }
        Some(sc) => {
            let block = loc
                .kernel
                .block_dim
                .as_ref()
                .filter(|dim| dim.x > 0 && dim.y > 0 && dim.z > 0)
                .ok_or(ReplayError::BlockDimMissing)?;
            let launch_block = (block.x as u32, block.y as u32, block.z as u32);
            if sc.kernel_mangled_name != loc.kernel.name {
                return Err(ReplayError::SamplingKernelMismatch {
                    launch: loc.kernel.name.clone(),
                    sidecar: sc.kernel_mangled_name.clone(),
                });
            }
            if sc.original_grid != (gx, gy, gz) {
                return Err(ReplayError::GridDimRewritten {
                    launch: (gx, gy, gz),
                    sidecar: sc.original_grid,
                });
            }
            if sc.original_block != launch_block {
                return Err(ReplayError::BlockDimRewritten {
                    launch: launch_block,
                    sidecar: sc.original_block,
                });
            }
            if sc.sanctions_incomplete && sc.selected_block_ids.as_ref() != Some(&seen_indices) {
                return Err(ReplayError::SelectedBlockMembershipMismatch {
                    seen,
                    declared: sc
                        .selected_block_ids
                        .as_ref()
                        .map_or(0, |blocks| blocks.len() as u64),
                });
            }
            if seen < grid_total && !sc.sanctions_incomplete {
                return Err(ReplayError::IncompleteTrace { seen, grid_total });
            }
            if records_seen != sc.captured_records {
                return Err(ReplayError::RecordsCapturedMismatch {
                    records_seen,
                    captured: sc.captured_records,
                });
            }
        }
    }
    for blocks in per_sm_blocks.values_mut() {
        blocks.sort_by_key(|b| b.launch_index);
    }
    Ok((per_sm_blocks, records_seen))
}

/// Fold per-SM results into the kernel-level view, enforcing the
/// one-issue-per-record invariant.
fn fold_kernel_result(
    per_sm: BTreeMap<i32, SmSimResult>,
    records_seen: u64,
    l2: Option<(L2Counters, L2SourceSplit, DramStats)>,
) -> Result<KernelReplayResult, ReplayError> {
    let mut instructions_issued: u64 = 0;
    let mut max_cycles: u64 = 0;
    let mut l1_totals: Option<L1Counters> = None;
    for result in per_sm.values() {
        instructions_issued += result.instructions_issued;
        max_cycles = max_cycles.max(result.cycles);
        if let Some(c) = &result.l1 {
            l1_totals.get_or_insert_with(L1Counters::default).add(c);
        }
    }
    if instructions_issued != records_seen {
        return Err(ReplayError::CountMismatch {
            issued: instructions_issued,
            records: records_seen,
        });
    }
    let (l2, l2_by_source, dram) = match l2 {
        Some((counters, split, dram)) => (Some(counters), Some(split), Some(dram)),
        None => (None, None, None),
    };
    Ok(KernelReplayResult {
        instructions_issued,
        records_seen,
        per_sm,
        max_cycles,
        l1: l1_totals,
        l2,
        l2_by_source,
        dram,
    })
}

fn lookup_schedule<'a>(
    schedules: &'a BTreeMap<i32, FunctionSchedule>,
    loc: &KernelLoc<'_>,
) -> Result<&'a FunctionSchedule, ReplayError> {
    let expected_fuid = loc.kernel.function_unique_id;
    schedules
        .get(&expected_fuid)
        .ok_or(ReplayError::ScheduleMissing {
            function_unique_id: expected_fuid,
        })
}

/// Memory-hierarchy mode for one kernel replay — the ONE typed selector
/// every harness goes through (a pair of optional configs would let a
/// plumbing slip degrade a cell to the wrong mode silently).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub enum ReplayMemMode {
    /// No cache model (flat global latency).
    Flat,
    /// Per-SM L1s with constant fill latency below them (the pre-L2
    /// lockstep/ablation surface).
    L1Const(L1Config),
    /// Per-SM L1s over ONE shared L2 (the full hierarchy): L1 misses
    /// priced L2-hit vs DRAM by the shared state through the event
    /// system.
    L1SharedL2 {
        l1: L1Config,
        l2: L2Config,
        dram: DramBw,
    },
}

/// Replay one kernel launch on its traced placement under `mode`.
/// Caches are FRESH per kernel (cold, NCU `--cache-control all` parity).
pub fn replay_kernel(
    td: &TraceDir,
    loc: &KernelLoc<'_>,
    schedules: &BTreeMap<i32, FunctionSchedule>,
    params: &IssueModelParams,
    mode: ReplayMemMode,
) -> Result<KernelReplayResult, ReplayError> {
    let schedule = lookup_schedule(schedules, loc)?;
    let decode_sectors = !matches!(mode, ReplayMemMode::Flat);
    let (per_sm_blocks, records_seen) = extract_per_sm_blocks(td, loc, schedule, decode_sectors)?;
    match mode {
        ReplayMemMode::Flat | ReplayMemMode::L1Const(_) => {
            let l1_config = match mode {
                ReplayMemMode::L1Const(cfg) => Some(cfg),
                _ => None,
            };
            let mut per_sm = BTreeMap::new();
            for (sm, blocks) in &per_sm_blocks {
                per_sm.insert(*sm, simulate_sm(blocks, schedule, params, l1_config)?);
            }
            fold_kernel_result(per_sm, records_seen, None)
        }
        ReplayMemMode::L1SharedL2 { l1, l2, dram } => {
            let mut l2 = L2Model::new(l2)?;
            let sys = simulate_kernel_shared(&per_sm_blocks, schedule, params, l1, &mut l2, dram)?;
            fold_kernel_result(
                sys.per_sm,
                records_seen,
                Some((sys.l2, sys.l2_by_source, sys.dram)),
            )
        }
    }
}

/// Fast-path classification when no L1 model is attached: memory class
/// only, no lane decode — but the SAME wire-contract violations the L1
/// path rejects via `visit_memory_access` are rejected here with the
/// SAME typed diagnoses (a malformed record must never pass one mode
/// and fail the other).
///
/// Note: flat mode reuses `GlobalUntagged { off: 0, len: 0 }` as its
/// "global-class, sectors not decoded" encoding; `AccessKind` consumers
/// must not read flat-mode replays as untagged-pc statistics (no L1
/// counters exist in this mode).
fn classify_flat(
    inst: &pb::Instruction,
    path: &std::path::Path,
    warp_id: i32,
    record_ix: usize,
) -> Result<AccessKind, ReplayError> {
    let record = || format!("{} warp={warp_id} inst={record_ix}", path.display());
    let Some(raw) = inst.memory_op_class else {
        // Memory-ness contract: address payloads without a memory class
        // are a typed violation (mirrors the reader).
        if inst.addresses.is_empty() {
            return Ok(AccessKind::NonMemory);
        }
        return Err(TraceError::MemoryOpClassMissing {
            record: record(),
            n_addresses: inst.addresses.len(),
        }
        .into());
    };
    match pb::MemoryOpClass::try_from(raw) {
        Ok(pb::MemoryOpClass::Shared) => Ok(AccessKind::Shared),
        Ok(pb::MemoryOpClass::Unspecified) => {
            // Contract violation, NOT schema skew — same diagnosis as
            // the reader path.
            Err(TraceError::MemoryOpClassUnspecified { record: record() }.into())
        }
        Err(_) => Err(TraceError::UnknownEnumValue {
            record: record(),
            field: "memory_op_class",
            raw,
        }
        .into()),
        Ok(_) => {
            // Route a shared-space record (a shared atomic ATOMS carries
            // op_class=ATOMIC but address_space=SHARED) out of the global path,
            // even in flat mode where sectors are not decoded. Per-address
            // space is authoritative; absent falls back to global.
            let shared_space = inst.addresses.iter().any(|a| {
                matches!(
                    a.address_space
                        .and_then(|r| pb::MemorySpace::try_from(r).ok()),
                    Some(pb::MemorySpace::Shared) | Some(pb::MemorySpace::Local)
                )
            });
            if shared_space {
                Ok(AccessKind::Shared)
            } else {
                Ok(AccessKind::GlobalUntagged { off: 0, len: 0 })
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Full classification in L1 mode: wire-contract decode (streaming form),
/// per-instruction unique-sector expansion into the warp arena, and the
/// join-time [`MemRole`] split.
fn classify_with_l1(
    inst: &pb::Instruction,
    schedule: &FunctionSchedule,
    sectors: &mut Vec<i64>,
    path: &std::path::Path,
    warp_id: i32,
    record_ix: usize,
) -> Result<AccessKind, ReplayError> {
    let start = sectors.len();
    let record = || format!("{} warp={warp_id} inst={record_ix}", path.display());
    let mut effective_space: Option<pb::MemorySpace> = None;
    let meta = visit_memory_access(inst, record, |a| {
        if effective_space.is_none() {
            effective_space = a.address_space;
        }
        push_unique_sectors(
            &a.lane_vector,
            (0..a.lane_vector.len()).filter(|&i| a.lane_vector[i] != LANE_INACTIVE_SENTINEL),
            a.data_width_bytes,
            sectors,
            start,
        );
    })?;
    let Some(meta) = meta else {
        return Ok(AccessKind::NonMemory);
    };
    // Route by EFFECTIVE per-address space, not the instruction-level op_class:
    // a shared atomic (ATOMS) carries op_class=ATOMIC but address_space=SHARED,
    // and must not enter the global L1TEX/L2 sector stream. The per-address
    // space is authoritative when present; absent (legacy traces) falls back to
    // the instruction-level Shared class.
    let shared_space = matches!(
        effective_space,
        Some(pb::MemorySpace::Shared) | Some(pb::MemorySpace::Local)
    );
    if meta.op_class == pb::MemoryOpClass::Shared || shared_space {
        // Shared-window addresses never enter the L1TEX sector stream.
        sectors.truncate(start);
        return Ok(AccessKind::Shared);
    }
    let count = sectors.len() - start;
    let overflow = |sectors: usize| ReplayError::SectorCountOverflow {
        path: path.to_path_buf(),
        warp_id,
        record_ix,
        sectors,
    };
    let off = u32::try_from(start).map_err(|_| overflow(start))?;
    let len = u16::try_from(count).map_err(|_| overflow(count))?;
    // A pc absent from the schedule surfaces as the issue loop's typed
    // PcNotInSchedule; classify neutrally here.
    let role = schedule
        .by_pc
        .get(&u64::from(inst.pc))
        .map_or(MemRole::None, |slot| slot.mem_role);
    Ok(match role {
        MemRole::EligibleLoad(token) => AccessKind::GlobalEligible { off, len, token },
        MemRole::BypassLoad(token) => AccessKind::GlobalBypass { off, len, token },
        MemRole::Store => AccessKind::GlobalStore { off, len },
        MemRole::None => AccessKind::GlobalUntagged { off, len },
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod space_routing_tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::path::Path;

    /// An ATOMIC-class instruction carrying a single address record whose
    /// per-address space is `space` (None = legacy, no address_space).
    fn atomic_inst(space: Option<pb::MemorySpace>) -> pb::Instruction {
        let mut a = pb::Address::default();
        a.addrs = vec![0x1000];
        a.address_space = space.map(|s| s as i32);
        pb::Instruction {
            memory_op_class: Some(pb::MemoryOpClass::Atomic as i32),
            addresses: vec![a],
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn flat_shared_atomic_routes_to_shared_not_global() {
        // The blocking corruption: a shared atomic (op_class=ATOMIC,
        // address_space=SHARED) must NOT reach the global path.
        let k = classify_flat(
            &atomic_inst(Some(pb::MemorySpace::Shared)),
            Path::new("t"),
            0,
            0,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(k, AccessKind::Shared));
    }

    #[test]
    fn flat_global_atomic_routes_to_global() {
        let k = classify_flat(
            &atomic_inst(Some(pb::MemorySpace::Global)),
            Path::new("t"),
            0,
            0,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(k, AccessKind::GlobalUntagged { .. }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn flat_legacy_atomic_without_space_falls_back_to_global() {
        let k = classify_flat(&atomic_inst(None), Path::new("t"), 0, 0).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(k, AccessKind::GlobalUntagged { .. }));
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod replay_identity_tests {
    //! The allocation-identity gate is enforced on the path the simulator
    //! actually consumes (extract_per_sm_blocks), not only in a helper: a
    //! malformed GLOBAL-space global-atomic or LDGSTS-source record fails closed
    //! BEFORE replay classification.
    use super::*;
    use crate::program::FunctionSchedule;
    use prost::Message;
    use std::collections::BTreeMap as StdMap;

    /// A GLOBAL-space memory instruction of `op_class` with NO allocation_id —
    /// malformed under the address-carrying contract's identity rule.
    fn malformed_global_inst(op_class: pb::MemoryOpClass) -> pb::Instruction {
        let mut addrs = vec![0x7000_0000i64];
        addrs.extend(std::iter::repeat(LANE_INACTIVE_SENTINEL).take(31));
        pb::Instruction {
            pc: 16,
            active_mask: Some(0b1),
            predicate_mask: Some(0b1),
            function_unique_id: 1,
            vpc: Some(16),
            sm_id: Some(0),
            warpid_sm: Some(0),
            warpid_tb: Some(0),
            data_width: Some(4),
            memory_op_class: Some(op_class as i32),
            memory_op_access_kind: Some(pb::MemoryOpAccessKind::Atomic as i32),
            addresses: vec![pb::Address {
                data_width: 4,
                compression_format: 0, // list_all
                addrs,
                allocation_id: None, // malformed: GLOBAL active record, no id
                address_space: Some(pb::MemorySpace::Global as i32),
                ..Default::default()
            }],
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    fn write_trace_with(dir: &std::path::Path, inst: pb::Instruction) {
        let kernel = pb::Kernel {
            id: 1,
            name: "k".into(),
            function_unique_id: 1,
            size_shared_memory: 0,
            number_of_registers: 32,
            shared_memory_base_address: 0,
            local_memory_base_address: 0,
            grid_dim: Some(pb::Dim3d { x: 1, y: 1, z: 1 }),
            block_dim: Some(pb::Dim3d { x: 32, y: 1, z: 1 }),
            cluster_dim: Some(pb::Dim3d { x: 1, y: 1, z: 1 }),
        };
        let stream = pb::CudaStream {
            id: 0,
            kernels: vec![kernel],
            ordered_cuda_events: vec![],
        };
        let device = pb::GpuDevice {
            id: 0,
            streams: [(0i64, stream)].into_iter().collect(),
        };
        let trace = pb::Trace {
            name: "m".into(),
            binary_version: 1,
            nvbit_version: "1.8".into(),
            accelsim_version: 0,
            is_gathered_registers_values: false,
            gpu_device: [(0i64, device)].into_iter().collect(),
            trace_contract_id: String::new(),
            memory_payload_classes: vec![],
        };
        std::fs::write(dir.join("dynamic_trace.pb"), trace.encode_to_vec()).unwrap();
        // A VALID sidecar, so a missing id is AllocationIdMissing (not
        // AllocationsSidecarMissing) — the record itself is what is malformed.
        let extra = dir.join("extra_info");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&extra).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(
            extra.join("allocations.json"),
            r#"[{"allocation_id":1,"context_id":1,"device_id":0,"base_address":"0x70000000","size_bytes":4096,"alive":true}]"#,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let tb_dir = dir.join("threadblocks/device_0/stream_0/kernel_1");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&tb_dir).unwrap();
        let warp = pb::Warp {
            id: 0,
            instructions: vec![inst],
        };
        let tb = pb::Threadblock {
            block_id: Some(pb::Dim3d { x: 0, y: 0, z: 0 }),
            warps: [(0i32, warp)].into_iter().collect(),
        };
        std::fs::write(tb_dir.join("d_0_s_0_k_1_0,0,0.pb"), tb.encode_to_vec()).unwrap();
    }

    fn assert_replay_rejects_identity(inst: pb::Instruction) {
        let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        write_trace_with(tmp.path(), inst);
        let td = TraceDir::open(tmp.path()).unwrap();
        let loc = td.kernels().next().unwrap();
        let sched = FunctionSchedule {
            function_unique_id: 1,
            kernel_name: "k".into(),
            function_name: "f".into(),
            by_pc: StdMap::new(),
        };
        let err = extract_per_sm_blocks(&td, &loc, &sched, true).unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            matches!(
                err,
                ReplayError::Trace(TraceError::AllocationIdMissing { .. })
            ),
            "expected AllocationIdMissing, got {err:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn replay_rejects_malformed_global_atomic() {
        assert_replay_rejects_identity(malformed_global_inst(pb::MemoryOpClass::Atomic));
    }

    #[test]
    fn replay_rejects_malformed_ldgsts_source() {
        assert_replay_rejects_identity(malformed_global_inst(pb::MemoryOpClass::AsyncCopy));
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod completeness_tests {
    //! Reader/replay completeness fail-closed on the path replay ACTUALLY
    //! consumes: an incomplete trace lacking a trace_sampling.json sidecar is
    //! E_INCOMPLETE_TRACE; a subset trace passes iff the sidecar's original_grid
    //! matches the launch gridDim (never rewritten) and records.captured matches
    //! records_seen. A lossless-full sidecar may be present, but never sanctions
    //! incomplete coverage.
    use super::*;
    use crate::program::FunctionSchedule;
    use prost::Message;
    use std::collections::BTreeMap as StdMap;

    /// A minimal non-memory record (no memory_op_class) carrying placement, so it
    /// increments records_seen without engaging the allocation-identity gate.
    fn simple_inst() -> pb::Instruction {
        pb::Instruction {
            pc: 16,
            active_mask: Some(0b1),
            predicate_mask: Some(0b1),
            function_unique_id: 1,
            vpc: Some(16),
            sm_id: Some(0),
            warpid_sm: Some(0),
            warpid_tb: Some(0),
            data_width: Some(4),
            memory_op_class: None,
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    fn write_grid_trace(
        dir: &std::path::Path,
        grid_x: i32,
        grid_y: i32,
        block_xs: &[i32],
        sidecar: Option<&str>,
    ) {
        let kernel = pb::Kernel {
            id: 1,
            name: "_Z1kv".into(),
            function_unique_id: 1,
            size_shared_memory: 0,
            number_of_registers: 32,
            shared_memory_base_address: 0,
            local_memory_base_address: 0,
            grid_dim: Some(pb::Dim3d {
                x: grid_x,
                y: grid_y,
                z: 1,
            }),
            block_dim: Some(pb::Dim3d { x: 32, y: 1, z: 1 }),
            cluster_dim: Some(pb::Dim3d { x: 1, y: 1, z: 1 }),
        };
        let stream = pb::CudaStream {
            id: 0,
            kernels: vec![kernel],
            ordered_cuda_events: vec![],
        };
        let device = pb::GpuDevice {
            id: 0,
            streams: [(0i64, stream)].into_iter().collect(),
        };
        let trace = pb::Trace {
            name: "m".into(),
            binary_version: 1,
            nvbit_version: "1.8".into(),
            accelsim_version: 0,
            is_gathered_registers_values: false,
            gpu_device: [(0i64, device)].into_iter().collect(),
            trace_contract_id: String::new(),
            memory_payload_classes: vec![],
        };
        std::fs::write(dir.join("dynamic_trace.pb"), trace.encode_to_vec()).unwrap();
        let tb_dir = dir.join("threadblocks/device_0/stream_0/kernel_1");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&tb_dir).unwrap();
        for &bx in block_xs {
            let warp = pb::Warp {
                id: 0,
                instructions: vec![simple_inst()],
            };
            let tb = pb::Threadblock {
                block_id: Some(pb::Dim3d { x: bx, y: 0, z: 0 }),
                warps: [(0i32, warp)].into_iter().collect(),
            };
            std::fs::write(
                tb_dir.join(format!("d_0_s_0_k_1_{bx},0,0.pb")),
                tb.encode_to_vec(),
            )
            .unwrap();
        }
        if let Some(json) = sidecar {
            std::fs::write(dir.join("trace_sampling.json"), json).unwrap();
        }
    }

    // Literal producer fixtures generated and sealed by Python's sidecar
    // implementation.  Consumer tests therefore exercise the real canonical
    // contract instead of manufacturing a Rust-only approximation.
    const PYTHON_SEALED_SUBSET: &str =     fn rewrite_launch_metadata(
        dir: &std::path::Path,
        kernel_name: Option<&str>,
        block_x: Option<i32>,
    ) {
        let path = dir.join("dynamic_trace.pb");
        let mut trace = pb::Trace::decode(std::fs::read(&path).unwrap().as_slice()).unwrap();
        let kernel = &mut trace
            .gpu_device
            .get_mut(&0)
            .unwrap()
            .streams
            .get_mut(&0)
            .unwrap()
            .kernels[0];
        if let Some(name) = kernel_name {
            kernel.name = name.to_string();
        }
        if let Some(x) = block_x {
            kernel.block_dim.as_mut().unwrap().x = x;
        }
        std::fs::write(path, trace.encode_to_vec()).unwrap();
    }

    fn run(dir: &std::path::Path) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
        let td = TraceDir::open(dir)?;
        let loc = td.kernels().next().unwrap();
        let sched = FunctionSchedule {
            function_unique_id: 1,
            kernel_name: "_Z1kv".into(),
            function_name: "f".into(),
            by_pc: StdMap::new(),
        };
        extract_per_sm_blocks(&td, &loc, &sched, true).map(|_| ())
    }
```

```rust
//! Memory-record classification shared by the SM issue model and the
//! memory hierarchy. Lives in sim-mem (not sim-sm) because the token is
//! MEMORY semantics: which level a record stages into, whether it
//! allocates, and (next increments) per-token L2 behavior — the
//! `CacheOpToken → MemRole → AccessKind` chain keeps the token instead of
//! flattening it away, so bypass/untagged/store sectors can take
//! token-specific hierarchy paths without re-joining the sidecar.

use crate::cache_op::{CacheOpToken, classify_opcode, derive_l1_eligible, opcode_head};

/// How the memory hierarchy treats a global-class record at a static pc,
/// classified from the sidecar's SASS text (see `cache_op` for why the
/// Python classifier's own manifests are not consumed).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MemRole {
    /// Load-class opcode staging into the modeled L1.
    EligibleLoad(CacheOpToken),
    /// Load-class opcode bypassing the modeled L1 (`.cg`/`.cs`/strong
    /// scopes/LDGSTS/ATOM/TEX/OTHER).
    BypassLoad(CacheOpToken),
    /// Global-class store head (STG / RED): sectors hit-tested against
    /// the L1 without allocating; write-allocate at the L2.
    Store,
    /// Not load-class and not a store head (LD.E, LDC, LDSM, non-memory
    /// opcodes): counted in the unified sector denominator only when the
    /// dynamic record is global-class.
    None,
}

/// Is this opcode a global-class STORE head (STG / reduction)? STS/STL
/// are not global stores (shared / local — STL is L1-eligible via its
/// token).
pub fn is_global_store_opcode(opcode_text: &str) -> bool {
    matches!(opcode_head(opcode_text), "STG" | "RED")
}

/// Classify one static pc's SASS text into its [`MemRole`].
pub fn mem_role_of(opcode_text: &str, arch_token: &str) -> MemRole {
    match classify_opcode(opcode_text, arch_token) {
        Some(token) if derive_l1_eligible(token) => MemRole::EligibleLoad(token),
        Some(token) => MemRole::BypassLoad(token),
        None if is_global_store_opcode(opcode_text) => MemRole::Store,
        None => MemRole::None,
    }
}

/// How one DYNAMIC traced record interacts with the memory model: the
/// static [`MemRole`] of its pc joined with the record's decoded unique
/// sectors. Sector payloads (`off`/`len`) index the owning warp's sector
/// arena.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AccessKind {
    NonMemory,
    /// Shared-memory class: no L1TEX sector traffic; fixed shared latency.
    Shared,
    /// Manifest-eligible global-class record: modeled L1 sectors.
    GlobalEligible {
        off: u32,
        len: u16,
        token: CacheOpToken,
    },
    /// Sidecar-tagged INELIGIBLE record (`.cg`/`.cs`/LDGSTS/ATOM/...):
    /// bypasses the modeled L1 straight to the L2.
    GlobalBypass {
        off: u32,
        len: u16,
        token: CacheOpToken,
    },
    /// Global-class record whose pc the classifier did not tag and whose
    /// opcode is not a store: counted in the unified denominator only.
    GlobalUntagged {
        off: u32,
        len: u16,
    },
    /// Global-class STORE (STG/RED...): sectors hit-tested against the
    /// L1 without allocating (v0 write-through no-allocate); allocate at
    /// the L2 (card policy `write_allocate_non_inclusive`).
    GlobalStore {
        off: u32,
        len: u16,
    },
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn mem_roles_classified_from_sidecar_text() {
        assert_eq!(
            mem_role_of("LDG.E.U16.CONSTANT R0, [R2.64]", "sm_86"),
            MemRole::EligibleLoad(CacheOpToken::LdgECa)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mem_role_of("LDGSTS.E.128 [R1], [R2.64]", "sm_86"),
            MemRole::BypassLoad(CacheOpToken::Ldgsts)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mem_role_of("ATOMG.E.CAS.STRONG.GPU PT, R4, [R2.64], R6, R7", "sm_86"),
            MemRole::BypassLoad(CacheOpToken::Atom)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mem_role_of("STG.E.U16 [R2.64], R0", "sm_86"),
            MemRole::Store
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mem_role_of("RED.E.ADD.STRONG.GPU [R2.64], R0", "sm_86"),
            MemRole::Store
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mem_role_of("STL [R1], R0", "sm_86"),
            MemRole::EligibleLoad(CacheOpToken::Stl)
        );
        assert_eq!(mem_role_of("IADD3 R0, R1, R2, RZ", "sm_86"), MemRole::None);
        assert_eq!(mem_role_of("LD.E R0, [R2.64]", "sm_86"), MemRole::None);
        // Bare LDG.E off sm_86: conservative bypass (OTHER).
        assert_eq!(
            mem_role_of("LDG.E R0, [R2.64]", "sm_120"),
            MemRole::BypassLoad(CacheOpToken::Other)
        );
        // STS is a shared store, never a global store head.
        assert_eq!(mem_role_of("STS [R1], R0", "sm_86"), MemRole::None);
    }
}
```

```rust
//! sim-calib: loader for the per-arch calibration cards
//! (`arch_profiles/cards/*.json`).
//!
//! The simulator's latencies, geometries, and clock anchors come from these
//! cards — which are filled from microbenchmarks (pchase) and vendor
//! documentation, never from NCU labels (Rule 1: targets-never-features).
//!
//! Fail-closed discipline: a card field recorded as a `research_gap` is a
//! typed error when the simulator requires it — there are no silent default
//! latencies. The schema's `objOrGap` pattern applies at BLOCK level too
//! (the sm_120-laptop card ships `l1_geometry` itself as a research_gap
//! object), so gap-able blocks deserialize through [`Carded`]. An object
//! carrying BOTH a payload and a `status` key is rejected outright rather
//! than silently admitted as either arm. The Python side enforces
//! card↔evidence lockstep (`arch_profiles/tests/test_arch_profile_lockstep.py`);
//! this crate's own lockstep test asserts the Rust loader sees the identical
//! sm_86 values.

use std::path::Path;

use serde::Deserialize;
use serde::de::DeserializeOwned;

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum CalibError {
    #[error("could not read card {path}: {source}")]
    Io {
        path: String,
        #[source]
        source: std::io::Error,
    },
    #[error("could not parse card {path}: {source}")]
    Parse {
        path: String,
        #[source]
        source: serde_json::Error,
    },
    #[error("card {arch_id} has no latencies_cycles block (pre-Phase-1 card?)")]
    LatenciesMissing { arch_id: String },
    #[error(
        "card {arch_id}: latency '{kind}' is a research_gap ({reason}); the simulator must not \
         invent a default — close the gap with a microbenchmark or type-exclude the consumer"
    )]
    ResearchGap {
        arch_id: String,
        kind: LatencyKind,
        reason: String,
    },
    #[error(
        "card {arch_id}: block '{block}' is a research_gap ({reason}); the consumer must \
         type-exclude, never guess geometry"
    )]
    BlockResearchGap {
        arch_id: String,
        block: &'static str,
        reason: String,
    },
    #[error("card field {field} = {value} violates '{requirement}' — fail closed, never clamp")]
    InvalidCardValue {
        field: &'static str,
        value: String,
        requirement: &'static str,
    },
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum LatencyKind {
    L1Hit,
    L2Hit,
    Dram,
    Shared,
    MshrOutstandingMisses,
}

impl std::fmt::Display for LatencyKind {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        let s = match self {
            Self::L1Hit => "l1_hit",
            Self::L2Hit => "l2_hit",
            Self::Dram => "dram",
            Self::Shared => "shared",
            Self::MshrOutstandingMisses => "mshr_outstanding_misses",
        };
        f.write_str(s)
    }
}

/// Closed enum so a typo'd status never deserializes into a gap arm.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum GapStatus {
    #[serde(rename = "research_gap")]
    ResearchGap,
}

/// A measured scalar card property: value + dispersion + unit.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct MeasuredValue {
    pub value: f64,
    pub dispersion: Option<f64>,
    pub unit: Option<String>,
}

/// A scalar property that is either measured or a typed research gap.
/// Mirrors the ArchProfile schema's `objOrGap` shape. Deserialization is
/// manual (NOT `#[serde(untagged)]`): an object with BOTH `value` and
/// `status` keys — a half-migrated card — must fail parsing, not silently
/// win whichever untagged arm matches first.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Measured {
    Value(MeasuredValue),
    Gap { reason: Option<String> },
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct RawObjOrGap {
    #[serde(default)]
    value: Option<f64>,
    #[serde(default)]
    dispersion: Option<f64>,
    #[serde(default)]
    unit: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    status: Option<GapStatus>,
    #[serde(default)]
    reason: Option<String>,
}

impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Measured {
    fn deserialize<D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error>
    where
        D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,
    {
        let raw = RawObjOrGap::deserialize(deserializer)?;
        match (raw.value, raw.status) {
            (Some(value), None) => Ok(Measured::Value(MeasuredValue {
                value,
                dispersion: raw.dispersion,
                unit: raw.unit,
            })),
            (None, Some(GapStatus::ResearchGap)) => Ok(Measured::Gap { reason: raw.reason }),
            (Some(_), Some(_)) => Err(serde::de::Error::custom(
                "objOrGap entry carries BOTH `value` and `status: research_gap` — \
                 half-migrated card, refusing to pick an arm",
            )),
            (None, None) => Err(serde::de::Error::custom(
                "objOrGap entry carries NEITHER `value` nor `status: research_gap`",
            )),
        }
    }
}

/// A whole card block (object payload) that may instead be a typed
/// research-gap object — the block-level `objOrGap` pattern used by the
/// partial sm_120-laptop card for `l1_geometry` and
/// `nvml_reference_operating_point`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Carded<T> {
    Present(T),
    Gap { reason: Option<String> },
}

impl<T> Carded<T> {
    pub fn require(&self, arch_id: &str, block: &'static str) -> Result<&T, CalibError> {
        match self {
            Carded::Present(t) => Ok(t),
            Carded::Gap { reason } => Err(CalibError::BlockResearchGap {
                arch_id: arch_id.to_string(),
                block,
                reason: reason.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
            }),
        }
    }

    /// Serde default for blocks newer than a card: a field the card
    /// never carried is a GAP (fail closed at `require`), never a value.
    /// The reason names BOTH causes — cards ignore unknown keys, so a
    /// misspelled block key lands here too, and the diagnosis must not
    /// claim the card simply predates the block (gate finding
    /// 2026-07-07).
    pub fn absent_gap() -> Self {
        Carded::Gap {
            reason: Some(
                "field absent from this card (card predates the block, OR the card's key is \
                 misspelled — unknown keys are ignored on parse)"
                    .to_owned(),
            ),
        }
    }
}

impl<'de, T> Deserialize<'de> for Carded<T>
where
    T: DeserializeOwned,
{
    fn deserialize<D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error>
    where
        D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,
    {
        let raw = serde_json::Value::deserialize(deserializer)?;
        let status = raw.get("status");
        if let Some(status) = status {
            let gap: GapStatus = serde_json::from_value(status.clone())
                .map_err(|e| serde::de::Error::custom(format!("bad gap status: {e}")))?;
            let GapStatus::ResearchGap = gap;
            let reason = raw
                .get("reason")
                .and_then(|r| r.as_str())
                .map(str::to_string);
            return Ok(Carded::Gap { reason });
        }
        serde_json::from_value(raw)
            .map(Carded::Present)
            .map_err(|e| serde::de::Error::custom(format!("block payload: {e}")))
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct LatenciesCycles {
    pub l1_hit: Measured,
    pub l2_hit: Measured,
    pub dram: Measured,
    pub shared: Measured,
    pub mshr_outstanding_misses: Measured,
    pub provenance: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct L1Geometry {
    pub l1tex_bytes: u64,
    pub ways: u32,
    pub default_l1_bytes: u64,
    pub max_shared_bytes: u64,
    pub sets: u32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct L2Geometry {
    pub capacity_bytes: u64,
    pub sector_bytes: u32,
    pub num_slices: u32,
    pub line_bytes: u32,
    /// `null` on partial cards (sm_120-laptop ships capacity/slices with the
    /// write policy still unmeasured) — consumers requiring the policy must
    /// treat `None` as a typed gap, never assume write-allocate.
    pub policy: Option<String>,
    pub provenance: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct NvmlReferenceOperatingPoint {
    pub sm_clock_ref_mhz: f64,
    pub max_sm_clock_mhz: f64,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub short_burst_sm_clock_ref_mhz: Option<f64>,
}

/// Aggregate DRAM read-bandwidth covariate at the card-declared model
/// operating point. On the retained sm_86 card this combines the vendor
/// bus-width × data-rate spec with legacy numeric core/memory clock fields;
/// schema-v1 pchase provenance does not prove those clocks were locked during
/// latency capture. Vendor-documented simulator INPUT, never an NCU value;
/// `peak_bytes_per_second` remains a service-rate hypothesis until verified
/// schema-v2 protocol evidence supersedes it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct DramBandwidth {
    pub peak_bytes_per_second: u64,
    pub locked_sm_clock_mhz: f64,
    pub locked_mem_clock_mhz: f64,
    pub provenance: String,
}

impl DramBandwidth {
    /// The card-declared SM model clock in Hz as an exact integer (the legacy
    /// JSON field is named `locked_sm_clock_mhz`; that name is not proof of the
    /// retained capture protocol). The fixed-point DRAM server divides by this
    /// value. VALIDATED: a non-finite, non-positive
    /// or non-whole-MHz value is a typed error — a float→int saturating
    /// cast of a bad card value would otherwise produce a 0 Hz clock and
    /// a silently inert bandwidth server (gate finding, 2026-07-07).
    pub fn locked_sm_clock_hz(&self) -> Result<u64, CalibError> {
        let mhz = self.locked_sm_clock_mhz;
        if !mhz.is_finite() || mhz <= 0.0 || mhz.fract() != 0.0 {
            return Err(CalibError::InvalidCardValue {
                field: "dram_bandwidth.locked_sm_clock_mhz",
                value: mhz.to_string(),
                requirement: "positive finite whole MHz",
            });
        }
        Ok((mhz as u64) * 1_000_000)
    }

    /// The carded peak rate, validated non-zero (a 0 B/s rate must be a
    /// typed configuration error, never a clamped 1 B/s server).
    pub fn validated_peak_bytes_per_second(&self) -> Result<u64, CalibError> {
        if self.peak_bytes_per_second == 0 {
            return Err(CalibError::InvalidCardValue {
                field: "dram_bandwidth.peak_bytes_per_second",
                value: "0".to_owned(),
                requirement: "positive bytes/second",
            });
        }
        Ok(self.peak_bytes_per_second)
    }
}

/// Typed bundle of the latencies every current consumer requires (MSHR is
/// deliberately NOT here: it is still a research gap on sm_86 and consumers
/// must confront that via [`ArchCard::require_latency`]).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub struct RequiredLatencies {
    pub l1_hit: f64,
    pub l2_hit: f64,
    pub dram: f64,
    pub shared: f64,
}

/// The subset of an ArchProfile card the simulator consumes. Unknown fields
/// are ignored on purpose: cards carry label-side bookkeeping (predictor
/// state, crosswalk gates) that must never leak into simulator inputs.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct ArchCard {
    pub arch_id: String,
    pub sku: String,
    pub compute_capability: (u32, u32),
    pub sm_count: u32,
    pub l1_geometry: Carded<L1Geometry>,
    pub l2_geometry: Carded<L2Geometry>,
    pub nvml_reference_operating_point: Carded<NvmlReferenceOperatingPoint>,
    /// DRAM read-bandwidth covariate; research_gap on cards without a
    /// locked operating point (sm_120-laptop). Absent on legacy cards →
    /// treated as a gap, never a default.
    #[serde(default = "Carded::absent_gap")]
    pub dram_bandwidth: Carded<DramBandwidth>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub latencies_cycles: Option<LatenciesCycles>,
    /// Load classifier default for bare LDG.E (per-arch measured fact).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub bare_ldg_e_default: Option<String>,
}

impl ArchCard {
    pub fn load(path: &Path) -> Result<Self, CalibError> {
        let raw = std::fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|source| CalibError::Io {
            path: path.display().to_string(),
            source,
        })?;
        serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|source| CalibError::Parse {
            path: path.display().to_string(),
            source,
        })
    }

    /// The latency table, or a typed error if the card predates Phase 1D.
    pub fn latencies(&self) -> Result<&LatenciesCycles, CalibError> {
        self.latencies_cycles
            .as_ref()
            .ok_or_else(|| CalibError::LatenciesMissing {
                arch_id: self.arch_id.clone(),
            })
    }

    /// A required latency in cycles. `research_gap` → typed error, never a
    /// default.
    pub fn require_latency(&self, kind: LatencyKind) -> Result<f64, CalibError> {
        let lat = self.latencies()?;
        let entry = match kind {
            LatencyKind::L1Hit => &lat.l1_hit,
            LatencyKind::L2Hit => &lat.l2_hit,
            LatencyKind::Dram => &lat.dram,
            LatencyKind::Shared => &lat.shared,
            LatencyKind::MshrOutstandingMisses => &lat.mshr_outstanding_misses,
        };
        match entry {
            Measured::Value(v) => Ok(v.value),
            Measured::Gap { reason } => Err(CalibError::ResearchGap {
                arch_id: self.arch_id.clone(),
                kind,
                reason: reason.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
            }),
        }
    }

    /// The four simulator-required latencies resolved at once, so a consumer
    /// can fail-close at construction instead of mid-simulation.
    pub fn required_latencies(&self) -> Result<RequiredLatencies, CalibError> {
        Ok(RequiredLatencies {
            l1_hit: self.require_latency(LatencyKind::L1Hit)?,
            l2_hit: self.require_latency(LatencyKind::L2Hit)?,
            dram: self.require_latency(LatencyKind::Dram)?,
            shared: self.require_latency(LatencyKind::Shared)?,
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
#[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)] // unwrap in tests is an assertion, not error handling
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::path::PathBuf;

    fn card_path(name: &str) -> PathBuf {
        PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
            .join("../../arch_profiles/cards")
            .join(name)
            .canonicalize()
            .expect("card exists in-repo")
    }

    /// Cross-language lockstep: the Rust loader must see the exact retained
    /// values the Python lockstep test pins against the legacy schema-v1
    /// pchase observation. The v1 card does not establish a locked protocol.
    #[test]
    fn sm86_card_lockstep() {
        let card = ArchCard::load(&card_path("sm_86.json")).expect("load sm_86 card");
        assert_eq!(card.arch_id, "sm_86");
        assert_eq!(card.compute_capability, (8, 6));
        assert_eq!(card.sm_count, 84);
        let l2 = card.l2_geometry.require("sm_86", "l2_geometry").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(l2.capacity_bytes, 6_291_456);
        assert_eq!(l2.num_slices, 6);
        assert_eq!(l2.sector_bytes, 32);
        assert_eq!(l2.line_bytes, 128);
        let l1 = card.l1_geometry.require("sm_86", "l1_geometry").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(l1.l1tex_bytes, 131_072);
        assert_eq!(l1.default_l1_bytes, 32_768);
        assert_eq!(card.bare_ldg_e_default.as_deref(), Some("ca"));

        // Retained legacy pchase-v1 observations. They are scoped to the
        // recorded operating state; successor values require verified v2
        // recapture metadata for the core:memory clock relationship.
        let l = card.required_latencies().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(l.l1_hit, 33.0016);
        assert_eq!(l.l2_hit, 243.6152);
        assert_eq!(l.dram, 422.6486);
        assert_eq!(l.shared, 23.0016);

        // Retained DRAM service-rate hypothesis: vendor 21 Gbps × 384-bit
        // combined with the card's existing 1350/10501 MHz model point. The
        // legacy pchase-v1 card does not prove those clocks were locked during
        // latency capture.
        let bw = card
            .dram_bandwidth
            .require("sm_86", "dram_bandwidth")
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(bw.peak_bytes_per_second, 1_008_000_000_000);
        assert_eq!(bw.locked_sm_clock_mhz, 1350.0);
        assert_eq!(bw.locked_mem_clock_mhz, 10501.0);
        assert_eq!(bw.locked_sm_clock_hz().unwrap(), 1_350_000_000);
        assert_eq!(
            bw.validated_peak_bytes_per_second().unwrap(),
            1_008_000_000_000
        );
        // INTERNAL-CONSISTENCY PIN: the card carries the same numeric SM-clock
        // model point in its NVML and DRAM blocks. Keep those numeric hypotheses
        // aligned so the latency arm and byte server do not silently use
        // different clock domains. Equality is not evidence that the legacy v1
        // pchase capture ran under a locked protocol.
        let nvml = card
            .nvml_reference_operating_point
            .require("sm_86", "nvml_reference_operating_point")
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            bw.locked_sm_clock_mhz, nvml.sm_clock_ref_mhz,
            "dram_bandwidth.locked_sm_clock_mhz must equal the NVML reference SM clock"
        );
        // Bad-value validation is typed, never a clamp/saturating cast.
        let bad = DramBandwidth {
            peak_bytes_per_second: 0,
            locked_sm_clock_mhz: -1.0,
            locked_mem_clock_mhz: 10501.0,
            provenance: String::new(),
        };
        assert!(matches!(
            bad.locked_sm_clock_hz(),
            Err(CalibError::InvalidCardValue { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            bad.validated_peak_bytes_per_second(),
            Err(CalibError::InvalidCardValue { .. })
        ));

        // Ordering sanity mirrors the Python lockstep test.
        assert!(l.shared < l.l1_hit);
        assert!(l.l1_hit < l.l2_hit);
        assert!(l.l2_hit < l.dram);
    }

    /// The PARTIAL sm_120-laptop card must load: its gap blocks surface as
    /// typed BlockResearchGap on access, never as an opaque parse failure.
    #[test]
    fn sm120_partial_card_loads_with_typed_block_gaps() {
        let card = ArchCard::load(&card_path("sm_120-laptop.json")).expect("load sm_120 card");
        assert_eq!(card.arch_id, "sm_120");
        // l2_geometry is populated on this card.
        let l2 = card.l2_geometry.require("sm_120", "l2_geometry").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(l2.capacity_bytes, 33_554_432);
        // l1_geometry + NVML op point are research gaps → typed errors.
        match card.l1_geometry.require("sm_120", "l1_geometry") {
            Err(CalibError::BlockResearchGap { block, reason, .. }) => {
                assert_eq!(block, "l1_geometry");
                assert!(!reason.is_empty());
            }
            other => panic!("expected typed BlockResearchGap, got {other:?}"),
        }
        assert!(matches!(
            card.nvml_reference_operating_point
                .require("sm_120", "nvml_reference_operating_point"),
            Err(CalibError::BlockResearchGap { .. })
        ));
        // No latency table yet → typed LatenciesMissing.
        assert!(matches!(
            card.require_latency(LatencyKind::L1Hit),
            Err(CalibError::LatenciesMissing { .. })
        ));
        // DRAM bandwidth is a research gap (no locked operating point on
        // the DVFS-spanning laptop part) → typed, never inherited.
        assert!(matches!(
            card.dram_bandwidth.require("sm_120", "dram_bandwidth"),
            Err(CalibError::BlockResearchGap { .. })
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn sm86_mshr_is_research_gap_typed() {
        let card = ArchCard::load(&card_path("sm_86.json")).expect("load sm_86 card");
        match card.require_latency(LatencyKind::MshrOutstandingMisses) {
            Err(CalibError::ResearchGap { kind, reason, .. }) => {
                assert_eq!(kind, LatencyKind::MshrOutstandingMisses);
                assert!(!reason.is_empty(), "gap must carry its reason");
            }
            other => panic!("expected typed ResearchGap, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_latency_block_is_typed() {
        let card_json = r#"{
            "arch_id": "sm_test", "sku": "test",
            "compute_capability": [8, 6], "sm_count": 1,
            "l1_geometry": {"l1tex_bytes": 1, "ways": 1, "default_l1_bytes": 1,
                             "max_shared_bytes": 1, "sets": 1},
            "l2_geometry": {"capacity_bytes": 1, "sector_bytes": 32, "num_slices": 1,
                             "line_bytes": 128, "policy": "p", "provenance": "test"},
            "nvml_reference_operating_point": {"sm_clock_ref_mhz": 1.0, "max_sm_clock_mhz": 1.0}
        }"#;
        let card: ArchCard = serde_json::from_str(card_json).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            card.require_latency(LatencyKind::L1Hit),
            Err(CalibError::LatenciesMissing { .. })
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn typo_gap_status_never_deserializes() {
        let bad = r#"{"status": "reseach_gap", "reason": "typo"}"#;
        assert!(serde_json::from_str::<Measured>(bad).is_err());
    }

    /// The half-migrated collision case: an entry carrying BOTH a value and
    /// a research_gap status must fail parsing outright — under the old
    /// untagged representation it silently deserialized as Value(0.0).
    #[test]
    fn value_and_status_collision_rejected() {
        let bad = r#"{"status": "research_gap", "reason": "pending", "value": 0.0}"#;
        let err = serde_json::from_str::<Measured>(bad).expect_err("collision must fail");
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("BOTH"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_entry_rejected() {
        assert!(serde_json::from_str::<Measured>(r#"{"unit": "cycles"}"#).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn carded_typo_status_rejected() {
        let bad = r#"{"status": "reseach_gap", "reason": "typo"}"#;
        assert!(serde_json::from_str::<Carded<L1Geometry>>(bad).is_err());
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Loader for `extra_info/enhanced_execution_info.json` — the NVBit
//! tracer's static per-kernel metadata that ships alongside every trace dir.
//!
//! The simulator consumes ONLY the join surface:
//! `unique_function_id` → kernel name / sidecar function name + the static
//! pc table. This is the key that connects a dynamic trace record
//! (`instruction.function_unique_id`, `instruction.pc`) to the Phase-1E
//! control-bits sidecar (`sim_sm::ControlSidecar`, keyed by function name
//! and pc).
//!
//! Join facts, verified on all 17 M1 traces (2026-07-06):
//! - every traced instruction's `function_unique_id` matches a kernel's
//!   `unique_function_id` here;
//! - `kernel_name` minus its trailing `___<digits>` instance suffix equals
//!   the sidecar's function key BYTE-EXACTLY (C++ mangled names included);
//! - the static pc set here equals the sidecar's pc set exactly, and every
//!   dynamic traced pc is a member (pcs are function-relative; `vpc - pc`
//!   is the constant function base address).
//!
//! Deliberately NOT parsed: the per-instruction `control_bits` block and
//! `op_code`. The embedded control bits are untrustworthy — compared against
//! the Phase-1E sidecars (which re-decode the binary's actual encoding under
//! a transcription guard), only 88 of 5,736 static instructions agreed
//! (stall counts mostly 0, yield never set; NVBit records
//! `encoded_instruction: []`, so it never saw the raw words). The sidecar is
//! the ONLY admissible control-bits source. `op_code` is NVBit's own
//! normalization and disagrees with nvdisasm's head (e.g. NVBit "MOV" where
//! SASS reads "IMAD.MOV.U32"), so opcode classification must come from the
//! sidecar's `opcode_text`, never from here.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::collections::BTreeSet;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use serde::Deserialize;

/// Path of the exec-info file inside a trace dir.
const EXEC_INFO_RELPATH: &str = "extra_info/enhanced_execution_info.json";

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum ExecInfoError {
    #[error("failed to read {path}: {source}")]
    Io {
        path: PathBuf,
        #[source]
        source: std::io::Error,
    },
    #[error("failed to parse {path}: {source}")]
    Parse {
        path: PathBuf,
        #[source]
        source: serde_json::Error,
    },
    #[error("exec info has no kernels")]
    EmptyKernels,
    #[error("kernel {kernel_name:?}: empty static instruction table")]
    EmptyInstructions { kernel_name: String },
    #[error("duplicate unique_function_id {id} (kernels {first:?} and {second:?})")]
    DuplicateFunctionId {
        id: i32,
        first: String,
        second: String,
    },
    #[error("kernel {kernel_name:?}: duplicate static pc {pc}")]
    DuplicatePc { kernel_name: String, pc: u64 },
    #[error(
        "kernel {kernel_name:?}: pc transcription mismatch: \
         pc_string_hex {hex:?} != pc_num_dec {dec}"
    )]
    PcTranscriptionMismatch {
        kernel_name: String,
        hex: String,
        dec: u64,
    },
}

/// Static metadata for one kernel: the (function id → name, pc table) join
/// surface.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct KernelStaticInfo {
    /// Raw NVBit kernel name, including the trailing `___<digits>` instance
    /// suffix (e.g. `layernorm_fwd_bf16_sm80_kernel___0`).
    pub kernel_name: String,
    /// `kernel_name` with the trailing `___<digits>` suffix stripped — the
    /// control-bits sidecar's function key. Equal to `kernel_name` when no
    /// suffix is present.
    pub function_name: String,
    /// SM architecture version as NVBit reports it (86 for sm_86).
    pub architecture_version: u32,
    /// Function-relative pcs of every static instruction.
    pub static_pcs: BTreeSet<u64>,
}

/// Parsed exec info: `unique_function_id` → static kernel metadata.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ExecInfo {
    pub benchmark_name: String,
    pub kernels: BTreeMap<i32, KernelStaticInfo>,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct RawExecInfo {
    benchmark_name: String,
    kernels: Vec<RawKernel>,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct RawKernel {
    kernel_name: String,
    unique_function_id: i32,
    architecture_version: u32,
    instructions: Vec<RawInst>,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct RawInst {
    pc_string_hex: String,
    pc_num_dec: u64,
}

/// Strip a trailing `___<digits>` NVBit instance suffix, if present.
///
/// Only a suffix where every character after the final `___` is a digit is
/// stripped — mangled C++ names may legitimately contain `___` elsewhere.
fn strip_instance_suffix(kernel_name: &str) -> &str {
    if let Some(pos) = kernel_name.rfind("___") {
        let tail = &kernel_name[pos + 3..];
        if !tail.is_empty() && tail.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) {
            return &kernel_name[..pos];
        }
    }
    kernel_name
}

impl ExecInfo {
    /// Load and validate `<trace_dir>/extra_info/enhanced_execution_info.json`.
    pub fn load_from_trace_dir(trace_dir: &Path) -> Result<Self, ExecInfoError> {
        let path = trace_dir.join(EXEC_INFO_RELPATH);
        let raw = std::fs::read(&path).map_err(|source| ExecInfoError::Io {
            path: path.clone(),
            source,
        })?;
        let parsed: RawExecInfo =
            serde_json::from_slice(&raw).map_err(|source| ExecInfoError::Parse { path, source })?;
        Self::from_raw(parsed)
    }

    fn from_raw(raw: RawExecInfo) -> Result<Self, ExecInfoError> {
        if raw.kernels.is_empty() {
            return Err(ExecInfoError::EmptyKernels);
        }
        let mut kernels: BTreeMap<i32, KernelStaticInfo> = BTreeMap::new();
        for k in raw.kernels {
            if k.instructions.is_empty() {
                return Err(ExecInfoError::EmptyInstructions {
                    kernel_name: k.kernel_name,
                });
            }
            let mut static_pcs = BTreeSet::new();
            for inst in &k.instructions {
                let hex_value = u64::from_str_radix(&inst.pc_string_hex, 16);
                if hex_value != Ok(inst.pc_num_dec) {
                    return Err(ExecInfoError::PcTranscriptionMismatch {
                        kernel_name: k.kernel_name,
                        hex: inst.pc_string_hex.clone(),
                        dec: inst.pc_num_dec,
                    });
                }
                if !static_pcs.insert(inst.pc_num_dec) {
                    return Err(ExecInfoError::DuplicatePc {
                        kernel_name: k.kernel_name,
                        pc: inst.pc_num_dec,
                    });
                }
            }
            let function_name = strip_instance_suffix(&k.kernel_name).to_owned();
            let info = KernelStaticInfo {
                function_name,
                architecture_version: k.architecture_version,
                static_pcs,
                kernel_name: k.kernel_name,
            };
            match kernels.entry(k.unique_function_id) {
                std::collections::btree_map::Entry::Occupied(e) => {
                    return Err(ExecInfoError::DuplicateFunctionId {
                        id: k.unique_function_id,
                        first: e.get().kernel_name.clone(),
                        second: info.kernel_name,
                    });
                }
                std::collections::btree_map::Entry::Vacant(v) => {
                    v.insert(info);
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(Self {
            benchmark_name: raw.benchmark_name,
            kernels,
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
#[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn raw(kernels: &str) -> RawExecInfo {
        serde_json::from_str(&format!(
            r#"{{"benchmark_name": "bench_run", "kernels": [{kernels}]}}"#
        ))
        .unwrap()
    }

    fn kernel_json(name: &str, id: i32, pcs: &[u64]) -> String {
        let insts: Vec<String> = pcs
            .iter()
            .map(|pc| format!(r#"{{"pc_string_hex": "{pc:x}", "pc_num_dec": {pc}}}"#))
            .collect();
        format!(
            r#"{{"kernel_name": "{name}", "unique_function_id": {id},
                 "architecture_version": 86, "instructions": [{}]}}"#,
            insts.join(",")
        )
    }

    #[test]
    fn loads_minimal_exec_info() {
        let info = ExecInfo::from_raw(raw(&kernel_json("my_kernel___0", 1, &[0, 16, 32]))).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(info.benchmark_name, "bench_run");
        let k = &info.kernels[&1];
        assert_eq!(k.kernel_name, "my_kernel___0");
        assert_eq!(k.function_name, "my_kernel");
        assert_eq!(k.architecture_version, 86);
        assert_eq!(
            k.static_pcs.iter().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            [0, 16, 32]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn suffix_strip_requires_all_digit_tail() {
        // Mangled names may contain ___ that is NOT an instance suffix.
        assert_eq!(strip_instance_suffix("k___0"), "k");
        assert_eq!(strip_instance_suffix("k___12"), "k");
        assert_eq!(strip_instance_suffix("k___0x"), "k___0x");
        assert_eq!(strip_instance_suffix("k___"), "k___");
        assert_eq!(strip_instance_suffix("plain_kernel"), "plain_kernel");
        // Only the FINAL ___<digits> run is stripped.
        assert_eq!(strip_instance_suffix("a___1___2"), "a___1");
    }

    #[test]
    fn hex_dec_transcription_mismatch_is_typed() {
        let bad = r#"{"kernel_name": "k___0", "unique_function_id": 1,
                      "architecture_version": 86,
                      "instructions": [{"pc_string_hex": "10", "pc_num_dec": 10}]}"#;
        let err = ExecInfo::from_raw(raw(bad)).unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(
            err,
            ExecInfoError::PcTranscriptionMismatch { dec: 10, .. }
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn duplicate_pc_rejected() {
        let err = ExecInfo::from_raw(raw(&kernel_json("k___0", 1, &[0, 0]))).unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(err, ExecInfoError::DuplicatePc { pc: 0, .. }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn duplicate_function_id_rejected() {
        let two = format!(
            "{},{}",
            kernel_json("a___0", 1, &[0]),
            kernel_json("b___0", 1, &[0])
        );
        let err = ExecInfo::from_raw(raw(&two)).unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(
            err,
            ExecInfoError::DuplicateFunctionId { id: 1, .. }
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_kernels_and_empty_instructions_rejected() {
        let err = ExecInfo::from_raw(raw("")).unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(err, ExecInfoError::EmptyKernels));
        let err = ExecInfo::from_raw(raw(r#"{"kernel_name": "k___0", "unique_function_id": 1,
                "architecture_version": 86, "instructions": []}"#))
        .unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(err, ExecInfoError::EmptyInstructions { .. }));
    }
}
```

```text
import "gpu_device.proto";
import "instruction.proto";

message Trace {
  string name = 1;
  int32 binary_version = 2;
  string nvbit_version = 3;
  int32 accelsim_version = 4;
  bool is_gathered_registers_values = 5;

  // address-carrying contract transition (additive, per the CLAUDE.md wire-
  // extension policy). `trace_contract_id` names the emitted contract so an
  // old exclusion-semantics trace (field absent/empty) is never silently
  // cross-compared with a new address-carrying one. `memory_payload_classes`
  // lists the MemoryOpClass values for which this trace emits address records
  // under the contract (e.g. [GLOBAL, SHARED, LOCAL, ATOMIC, ASYNC_COPY] post-
  // flip); its ABSENCE is the legacy signal the consumer identity gates use to
```
