```text
syntax = "proto3";

package dynamic_trace;

import "address.proto";

// AC4 enum: memory operation class for each emitted instruction.
// MEMORY_OP_CLASS_UNSPECIFIED is the proto3 default zero value and
// must NEVER be emitted by the tracer; readers treat it as a
// contract violation. The nine original plan classes follow; the
// tenth value MEMORY_OP_CLASS_TMEM was added for Blackwell
// (sm_100) tensor-memory accesses via the `tcgen05.{ld,st}`
// family (mnemonics `LDT` / `STT`). Per the CLAUDE.md wire-
// extension policy this is an additive enum extension: producer
// emits the new value, consumer accepts it; old readers that
// only knew 0-9 either route the new value through their
// catch-all path or REJECT (a closed-enum validator that
// hard-codes the prior 10 cases as a frozenset is the only place
// readers would break, and the consumer-side widening lands in
// the same commit as this producer-side enum addition per
// BL-20260507-multi-surface-lockstep-changes).
enum MemoryOpClass {
  MEMORY_OP_CLASS_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  MEMORY_OP_CLASS_GLOBAL = 1;
  MEMORY_OP_CLASS_SHARED = 2;
  MEMORY_OP_CLASS_LOCAL = 3;
  MEMORY_OP_CLASS_TEXTURE = 4;
  MEMORY_OP_CLASS_SURFACE = 5;
  MEMORY_OP_CLASS_ATOMIC = 6;
  MEMORY_OP_CLASS_TMA = 7;
  MEMORY_OP_CLASS_ASYNC_COPY = 8;
  MEMORY_OP_CLASS_CLUSTER_DSMEM = 9;
  MEMORY_OP_CLASS_TMEM = 10;
}

// Write-policy classification dimension orthogonal to
// MemoryOpClass. MemoryOpClass tags the memory space (global,
// shared, local, etc.); MemoryOpAccessKind tags the direction
// (load, store, atomic / read-modify-write, async-copy). Together
// the two enums let consumers distinguish write-allocate paths
// (global / local / texture loads + stores; atomic; texture
// loads) from no-write-allocate paths (shared, async-copy
// destination side). The classifier is the producer's job: the
// SASS opcode head determines which kind the access falls into.
// New optional field at tag 12; legacy traces leave it absent,
// and consumers fall back to UNSPECIFIED so the additive widening
// is wire-compatible with pre-tag-12 readers.
enum MemoryOpAccessKind {
  MEMORY_OP_ACCESS_KIND_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  MEMORY_OP_ACCESS_KIND_LOAD = 1;
  MEMORY_OP_ACCESS_KIND_STORE = 2;
  MEMORY_OP_ACCESS_KIND_ATOMIC = 3;
  MEMORY_OP_ACCESS_KIND_ASYNC_COPY = 4;
}

message instruction {
  // Existing fields (tags 1-5) are unchanged so older readers can
  // still parse new traces and silently ignore the new tags >= 6.
  uint32 pc = 1;
  // Tag numbers preserved when `optional` is added so older
  // readers can still parse new traces. The change here is
  // observability: proto3 explicit-presence lets the validator
  // distinguish "tracer did not emit this field" (HasField false)
  // from "tracer emitted value 0" (HasField true with the proto3
  // default value). Without explicit-presence, a regression that
  // dropped the producer's `inst->set_active_mask(...)` /
  // `inst->set_predicate_mask(...)` calls would be silently
  // admitted because the proto3 default 0 is a valid lane-mask
  // value (predicated-off all-lanes-inactive case). Setters on
  // the producer side are wire-compatible; no producer-code
  // change is required.
  optional uint32 active_mask = 2;
  optional uint32 predicate_mask = 3;
  int32 function_unique_id = 4;
  repeated address addresses = 5;

  // AC4 per-record fields.

  // Operation class. Marked `optional` so a non-memory instruction
  // (ALU, branch, control flow) can leave the field absent on the
  // wire. The downstream contract validator interprets:
  //   - field absent: this is not a memory instruction; addresses
  //     list is also expected to be empty.
  //   - field present and != UNSPECIFIED: a memory instruction whose
  //     op-class the tracer determined.
  //   - field present and == UNSPECIFIED: contract violation; the
  //     tracer encountered a memory instruction it could not
  //     classify and should have emitted a typed
  //     `unsupported_memory_path` exclusion sidecar instead.
  optional MemoryOpClass memory_op_class = 6;

  // Width of the per-lane access in bytes (e.g. 4 for an int32
  // load, 16 for a 128-bit load). Mirrors the per-warp-instruction
  // data width that already appears on `address.data_width`, but is
  // promoted to instruction level so consumers do not have to walk
  // the address list to discover the width when no addresses are
  // emitted (e.g. predicated-off warps with all-lanes-inactive).
  // Marked `optional` for proto3 explicit presence so consumers can
  // distinguish "tracer did not emit data_width" from "data_width
  // value 0" (which is a contract violation analogous to
  // MEMORY_OP_CLASS_UNSPECIFIED — the loss-of-diagnostic Codex
  // flagged in R8 v2 review).
  optional int32 data_width = 7;

  // Warp index inside the threadblock (0 <= warpid_tb < blockDim
  // total / 32). This is the lane-grouping the SIMT scheduler uses
  // and the one downstream coalescer needs. Marked `optional` so
  // proto3 explicit presence distinguishes "warp 0" (valid) from
  // "tracer did not emit this field" (absent on the wire). Required
  // because SM/warp 0 is a perfectly valid ID and a plain int32
  // scalar would collapse it to the proto3 zero default.
  optional int32 warpid_tb = 8;

  // Warp index on the SM, where exposed by NVBit. Marked `optional`
  // so absence on the wire ("not exposed by the NVBit runtime
  // present at trace time") is observationally distinct from value
  // 0 (warp 0 on the SM). The AC4 plan permits this so traces
  // from older NVBit releases stay admissible.
  optional int32 warpid_sm = 9;

  // SM id, where exposed by NVBit. Marked `optional` for the same
  // reason: SM 0 is a valid id and must be distinguishable from
  // "tracer did not emit this field". When the NVBit runtime does
  // not expose the SM id, the field is simply omitted (has_sm_id()
  // returns false on the C++ side; the field is absent on the
  // wire); when it is exposed, the actual value is written
  // including 0.
  optional int32 sm_id = 10;

  // Virtual program counter. Widens the existing `pc` field
  // (uint32) to uint64 because PC ranges on post-Hopper
  // architectures may exceed 32 bits when the code lives in a
  // long-running kernel module mapped at a high virtual address.
  // The legacy `pc` field stays so older readers continue to work;
  // new emitters should populate both `pc` (low 32 bits) and `vpc`
  // (full 64-bit virtual PC). Marked `optional` for proto3
  // explicit-presence so the validator can distinguish "tracer
  // did not emit vpc" (HasField false) from "vpc=0" (HasField
  // true with a value that legitimately equals pc=0 for the
  // first instruction in a kernel). Tag number unchanged.
  optional uint64 vpc = 11;

  // Access-kind dimension orthogonal to memory_op_class. The
  // producer-side SASS classifier maps the opcode head to one of
  // {load, store, atomic, async-copy}; downstream consumers use
  // the kind to distinguish write-allocate paths (global stores
  // fetch the line on miss, just like loads) from
  // no-write-allocate paths (shared stores do not touch L2;
  // async-copy destination side flows into shared without an L2
  // write-allocate). Marked `optional` so legacy traces emitted
  // before this field landed remain admissible (HasField false
  // routes to UNSPECIFIED on the consumer side). Tag 12 is the
  // next available after the existing tags 1-11. Producer-side
  // C++ classifier lands in a future round; this tag reserves
  // the wire slot and the consumer reads it when present.
  optional MemoryOpAccessKind memory_op_access_kind = 12;

  // Cache-operator dimension orthogonal to both memory_op_class
  // (memory space) AND memory_op_access_kind (load/store/atomic/
  // async-copy direction). The producer-side SASS classifier at
  // tools/cache_predictor/l1_cache_op_classifier.py maps the
  // opcode head (LDG.E.CA / LDG.E.STRONG.SM / LDGSTS / LDL /
  // STL / ATOM / TEX / etc.) to one of the closed 12-token
  // underscore-vocabulary InstructionCacheOp values. The
  // downstream L1 predictor head's per-SM walker filters
  // l1_eligible accesses by this field; it answers "how does the
  // cache operator decide whether this access touches the modeled
  // L1 line state".
  //
  // Per CLAUDE.md "Two-Device Local Development Model" and
  // BL-20260505, the classifier records the actual SASS encoding
  // (Ampere LDG.E.CA -> LDG_E_CA; Blackwell LDG.E.STRONG.SM ->
  // LDG_E_STRONG_SM), NOT the semantic equivalent class. The
  // two arches' cache-operator behavior is per-architecture
  // distinct.
  //
  // Marked `optional` so legacy traces emitted before this field
  // landed remain admissible (HasField false routes to
  // INSTRUCTION_CACHE_OP_UNSPECIFIED on the consumer side); the
  // L1 predictor head treats absent or unspecified values as
  // `predictor_l1_sass_provenance_missing`. Tag 13 is the next
  // available after the existing tags 1-12.
  //
  // Three-surface lockstep with the JSON classifier manifest
  // schema (tools/cache_predictor/cache_op_map.schema.json) +
  // the cache_predictor._TYPED_REASONS frozenset + the
  // comparison_runner module-level constants is enforced by the
  // structural lockstep test at
  // workloads/simbench_bw/tests/test_predictor_l1_sass_provenance_missing_lockstep.py
  // per BL-20260507-arch-token-multi-surface-lockstep.
  optional InstructionCacheOp instruction_cache_op = 13;
}

// Closed 12-token cache-operator vocabulary. The
// INSTRUCTION_CACHE_OP_UNSPECIFIED zero value is the proto3
// default and is what an absent-on-the-wire instruction_cache_op
// resolves to on the consumer side; the L1 predictor head treats
// it as `predictor_l1_sass_provenance_missing` (the tracer did
// not classify the cache operator for this instruction).
//
// Per CLAUDE.md wire-extension policy, this is an additive enum
// extension: producer emits the new values, consumer accepts them;
// old readers that only know the enum entries at producer-side
// build time route unknown values through their catch-all path.
// The 12 named values mirror the JSON schema's
// `instruction_cache_op` enum at
// tools/cache_predictor/cache_op_map.schema.json (closed-set
// lockstep enforced by a structural cross-surface parity test).
enum InstructionCacheOp {
  INSTRUCTION_CACHE_OP_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  INSTRUCTION_CACHE_OP_LDG_E_CA = 1;
  INSTRUCTION_CACHE_OP_LDG_E_CG = 2;
  INSTRUCTION_CACHE_OP_LDG_E_CS = 3;
  INSTRUCTION_CACHE_OP_LDG_E_EF = 4;
  INSTRUCTION_CACHE_OP_LDG_E_STRONG_SM = 5;
  INSTRUCTION_CACHE_OP_LDG_E_STRONG_GPU = 6;
  INSTRUCTION_CACHE_OP_LDL = 7;
  INSTRUCTION_CACHE_OP_STL = 8;
  INSTRUCTION_CACHE_OP_LDGSTS = 9;
  INSTRUCTION_CACHE_OP_ATOM = 10;
  INSTRUCTION_CACHE_OP_TEX = 11;
  INSTRUCTION_CACHE_OP_OTHER = 12;
}
```

```python
"""Fail-closed admission for a completed forward NVBit trace capture.

Historical M1 payload authorities are verified by their dedicated manifest
gate and must never be dispatched through this forward-capture consumer.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import io
import json
import os
import stat
import sys
from contextlib import contextmanager
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Iterator, NoReturn

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
if str(REPO_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))

from tools.nvbit_tracer.import_trace_contract import (
    TraceContractRuntimePrerequisiteMissing,
    TraceContractTrackedBindingsCorrupt,
    TraceDirValidationSnapshot,
    TraceThreadblockBytes,
    _import_pb_modules,
    validate_trace_dir,
)


PB_GENERATED = REPO_ROOT / "workloads" / "simbench_bw" / "_pb_generated"
EXPECTED_TRACE_CONTRACT_ID = "sm86_addr_carry_v1"
EXPECTED_MEMORY_PAYLOAD_CLASSES = frozenset({1, 2, 3, 6, 8})
TRACE_ADMISSION_SCOPE = "forward_capture_only"


class TraceAdmissionError(RuntimeError):
    """A capture exists but is not safe to publish or consume."""

    def __init__(self, typed_reason: str, detail: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"{typed_reason}: {detail}")
        self.typed_reason = typed_reason
        self.detail = detail


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TraceAdmission:
    launch_count: int
    threadblock_count: int
    instruction_count: int
    expected_record_count: int
    admitted_record_count: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _StatState:
    device: int
    inode: int
    mode: int
    links: int
    uid: int
    gid: int
    size: int
    mtime_ns: int
    ctime_ns: int

    @classmethod
    def capture(cls, value: os.stat_result) -> "_StatState":
        return cls(
            device=value.st_dev,
            inode=value.st_ino,
            mode=value.st_mode,
            links=value.st_nlink,
            uid=value.st_uid,
            gid=value.st_gid,
            size=value.st_size,
            mtime_ns=value.st_mtime_ns,
            ctime_ns=value.st_ctime_ns,
        )

    @property
    def identity(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        return self.device, self.inode

    @property
    def file_type(self) -> int:
        return stat.S_IFMT(self.mode)


@dataclass
class _DescriptorRecord:
    fd: int
    path: Path
    parent_fd: int | None
    name: str | None
    initial: _StatState
    typed_reason: str
    strict_state: bool
    payload: bytes | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _InventoryEntry:
    name: str
    state: _StatState


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _DirectoryInventory:
    directory: _DescriptorRecord
    entries: tuple[_InventoryEntry, ...]
    typed_reason: str


class _TraceSnapshotTransaction:
    """Anchored no-follow snapshot of one completed trace directory."""

    _READ_SIZE = 1024 * 1024

    def __init__(self, trace_dir: Path) -> None:
        self.trace_dir = self._lexical_absolute_path(trace_dir)
        self._descriptors: list[_DescriptorRecord] = []
        self._inventories: list[_DirectoryInventory] = []
        self._identity_paths: dict[tuple[int, int], Path] = {}
        self._root: _DescriptorRecord | None = None
        self._root_file: _DescriptorRecord | None = None
        self._stats_file: _DescriptorRecord | None = None
        self._allocation_file: _DescriptorRecord | None = None
        self._threadblocks: list[_DescriptorRecord] = []

    @staticmethod
    def _lexical_absolute_path(trace_dir: Path) -> Path:
        supplied = Path(trace_dir)
        raw = os.fspath(supplied)
        if "\x00" in raw:
            raise TraceAdmissionError(
                "trace_root_unreadable",
                "trace directory path contains a NUL byte",
            )
        if ".." in supplied.parts:
            raise TraceAdmissionError(
                "trace_root_unreadable",
                f"trace directory path aliases an ancestor via '..': {supplied}",
            )
        absolute = Path(os.path.abspath(raw))
        if absolute.anchor != os.sep:
            raise TraceAdmissionError(
                "trace_root_unreadable",
                f"trace directory uses a non-canonical root alias: {absolute}",
            )
        return absolute

    @staticmethod
    def _directory_flags() -> int:
        required = ("O_DIRECTORY", "O_NOFOLLOW")
        missing = [name for name in required if not hasattr(os, name)]
        if missing or not hasattr(os, "pread"):
            unavailable = missing + ([] if hasattr(os, "pread") else ["pread"])
            raise TraceAdmissionError(
                "trace_root_unreadable",
                "platform lacks required anchored no-follow primitives: "
                + ", ".join(unavailable),
            )
        return (
            os.O_RDONLY
            | os.O_DIRECTORY
            | os.O_NOFOLLOW
            | getattr(os, "O_CLOEXEC", 0)
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _file_flags() -> int:
        return (
            os.O_RDONLY
            | os.O_NOFOLLOW
            | getattr(os, "O_CLOEXEC", 0)
            | getattr(os, "O_NONBLOCK", 0)
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _same_object(left: _StatState, right: _StatState) -> bool:
        return (
            left.identity == right.identity
            and left.file_type == right.file_type
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _raise(typed_reason: str, path: Path, detail: str) -> NoReturn:
        raise TraceAdmissionError(typed_reason, f"{path}: {detail}")

    def _register_identity(
        self,
        path: Path,
        state: _StatState,
        typed_reason: str,
    ) -> None:
        prior = self._identity_paths.get(state.identity)
        if prior is not None and prior != path:
            self._raise(
                typed_reason,
                path,
                f"aliases {prior}; duplicate filesystem identity "
                f"device={state.device} inode={state.inode}",
            )
        self._identity_paths[state.identity] = path
        if stat.S_ISREG(state.mode) and state.links != 1:
            self._raise(
                typed_reason,
                path,
                f"regular input has st_nlink={state.links}; hard-link aliases "
                "are not admissible",
            )

    def _lstat_at(
        self,
        parent_fd: int,
        name: str,
        path: Path,
        typed_reason: str,
    ) -> _StatState:
        try:
            value = os.stat(name, dir_fd=parent_fd, follow_symlinks=False)
        except OSError as exc:
            self._raise(typed_reason, path, f"anchored lstat failed: {exc}")
        state = _StatState.capture(value)
        if stat.S_ISLNK(state.mode):
            self._raise(typed_reason, path, "symbolic links are not admissible")
        return state

    def _fstat(
        self,
        fd: int,
        path: Path,
        typed_reason: str,
        action: str,
    ) -> _StatState:
        try:
            return _StatState.capture(os.fstat(fd))
        except OSError as exc:
            self._raise(typed_reason, path, f"{action} failed: {exc}")

    def _append_descriptor(
        self,
        *,
        fd: int,
        path: Path,
        parent_fd: int | None,
        name: str | None,
        initial: _StatState,
        typed_reason: str,
        strict_state: bool,
    ) -> _DescriptorRecord:
        record = _DescriptorRecord(
            fd=fd,
            path=path,
            parent_fd=parent_fd,
            name=name,
            initial=initial,
            typed_reason=typed_reason,
            strict_state=strict_state,
        )
        self._descriptors.append(record)
        self._register_identity(path, initial, typed_reason)
        return record

    def _open_root_chain(self) -> _DescriptorRecord:
        flags = self._directory_flags()
        try:
            slash_fd = os.open("/", flags)
        except OSError as exc:
            self._raise(
                "trace_root_unreadable",
                Path("/"),
                f"could not establish filesystem anchor: {exc}",
            )
        try:
            slash_state = self._fstat(
                slash_fd,
                Path("/"),
                "trace_root_unreadable",
                "filesystem-anchor fstat",
            )
        except BaseException:
            os.close(slash_fd)
            raise
        current = self._append_descriptor(
            fd=slash_fd,
            path=Path("/"),
            parent_fd=None,
            name=None,
            initial=slash_state,
            typed_reason="trace_root_unreadable",
            strict_state=False,
        )

        current_path = Path("/")
        for component in self.trace_dir.parts[1:]:
            next_path = current_path / component
            before = self._lstat_at(
                current.fd,
                component,
                next_path,
                "trace_root_unreadable",
            )
            if not stat.S_ISDIR(before.mode):
                self._raise(
                    "trace_root_unreadable",
                    next_path,
                    "path component is not a directory",
                )
            try:
                next_fd = os.open(component, flags, dir_fd=current.fd)
            except OSError as exc:
                self._raise(
                    "trace_root_unreadable",
                    next_path,
                    f"anchored no-follow directory open failed: {exc}",
                )
            try:
                opened = self._fstat(
                    next_fd,
                    next_path,
                    "trace_root_unreadable",
                    "opened-directory fstat",
                )
                after = self._lstat_at(
                    current.fd,
                    component,
                    next_path,
                    "trace_root_unreadable",
                )
            except BaseException:
                os.close(next_fd)
                raise
            if not (
                self._same_object(before, opened)
                and self._same_object(opened, after)
            ):
                try:
                    os.close(next_fd)
                finally:
                    self._raise(
                        "trace_root_unreadable",
                        next_path,
                        "path identity changed while opening ancestor/root",
                    )
            current = self._append_descriptor(
                fd=next_fd,
                path=next_path,
                parent_fd=current.fd,
                name=component,
                initial=opened,
                typed_reason="trace_root_unreadable",
                strict_state=False,
            )
            current_path = next_path

        current.strict_state = True
        self._root = current
        return current

    def _scan_directory(
        self,
        directory: _DescriptorRecord,
        typed_reason: str,
    ) -> tuple[_InventoryEntry, ...]:
        try:
            names = sorted(os.listdir(directory.fd))
        except OSError as exc:
            self._raise(
                typed_reason,
                directory.path,
                f"anchored inventory read failed: {exc}",
            )
        entries: list[_InventoryEntry] = []
        for name in names:
            path = directory.path / name
            state = self._lstat_at(directory.fd, name, path, typed_reason)
            if not (stat.S_ISDIR(state.mode) or stat.S_ISREG(state.mode)):
                self._raise(
                    typed_reason,
                    path,
                    f"unsupported inventory entry type mode=0o{state.mode:o}",
                )
            self._register_identity(path, state, typed_reason)
            entries.append(_InventoryEntry(name=name, state=state))
        return tuple(entries)

    def _capture_inventory(
        self,
        directory: _DescriptorRecord,
        typed_reason: str,
    ) -> tuple[_InventoryEntry, ...]:
        entries = self._scan_directory(directory, typed_reason)
        self._inventories.append(
            _DirectoryInventory(
                directory=directory,
                entries=entries,
                typed_reason=typed_reason,
            )
        )
        return entries

    def _open_child(
        self,
        parent: _DescriptorRecord,
        entry: _InventoryEntry,
        *,
        expect_directory: bool,
        typed_reason: str,
    ) -> _DescriptorRecord:
        path = parent.path / entry.name
        before = self._lstat_at(parent.fd, entry.name, path, typed_reason)
        if before != entry.state:
            self._raise(
                typed_reason,
                path,
                "path metadata changed between inventory and open",
            )
        expected_type = stat.S_ISDIR if expect_directory else stat.S_ISREG
        if not expected_type(before.mode):
            expected_name = "directory" if expect_directory else "regular file"
            self._raise(typed_reason, path, f"expected {expected_name}")
        flags = self._directory_flags() if expect_directory else self._file_flags()
        try:
            fd = os.open(entry.name, flags, dir_fd=parent.fd)
        except OSError as exc:
            self._raise(
                typed_reason,
                path,
                f"anchored no-follow open failed: {exc}",
            )
        try:
            opened = self._fstat(
                fd,
                path,
                typed_reason,
                "opened-child fstat",
            )
            after = self._lstat_at(parent.fd, entry.name, path, typed_reason)
        except BaseException:
            os.close(fd)
            raise
        if opened != before or after != before:
            try:
                os.close(fd)
            finally:
                self._raise(
                    typed_reason,
                    path,
                    "descriptor/path identity or metadata changed while opening",
                )
        return self._append_descriptor(
            fd=fd,
            path=path,
            parent_fd=parent.fd,
            name=entry.name,
            initial=opened,
            typed_reason=typed_reason,
            strict_state=True,
        )

    def _required_entry(
        self,
        entries: tuple[_InventoryEntry, ...],
        name: str,
        path: Path,
        typed_reason: str,
    ) -> _InventoryEntry:
        for entry in entries:
            if entry.name == name:
                return entry
        self._raise(typed_reason, path, "required trace artifact is missing")

    def _read_exact_descriptor(self, record: _DescriptorRecord) -> bytes:
        before = self._fstat(
            record.fd,
            record.path,
            record.typed_reason,
            "pre-read descriptor fstat",
        )
        if before != record.initial:
            self._raise(
                record.typed_reason,
                record.path,
                "descriptor metadata changed before stable read",
            )
        chunks: list[bytes] = []
        offset = 0
        while offset < before.size:
            try:
                chunk = os.pread(
                    record.fd,
                    min(self._READ_SIZE, before.size - offset),
                    offset,
                )
            except OSError as exc:
                self._raise(
                    record.typed_reason,
                    record.path,
                    f"descriptor read failed: {exc}",
                )
            if not chunk:
                self._raise(
                    record.typed_reason,
                    record.path,
                    "descriptor reached EOF before snapshotted size",
                )
            chunks.append(chunk)
            offset += len(chunk)
        try:
            extra = os.pread(record.fd, 1, offset)
        except OSError as exc:
            self._raise(
                record.typed_reason,
                record.path,
                f"descriptor EOF verification failed: {exc}",
            )
        after = self._fstat(
            record.fd,
            record.path,
            record.typed_reason,
            "post-read descriptor fstat",
        )
        if extra or after != before:
            self._raise(
                record.typed_reason,
                record.path,
                "descriptor mutated during stable read",
            )
        return b"".join(chunks)

    def _capture_payload(self, record: _DescriptorRecord) -> bytes:
        payload = self._read_exact_descriptor(record)
        record.payload = payload
        return payload

    def _capture_threadblocks(
        self,
        threadblocks_root: _DescriptorRecord,
    ) -> None:
        pending = [threadblocks_root]
        while pending:
            directory = pending.pop()
            entries = self._capture_inventory(
                directory,
                "trace_threadblock_unreadable",
            )
            children: list[_DescriptorRecord] = []
            for entry in entries:
                if stat.S_ISDIR(entry.state.mode):
                    children.append(
                        self._open_child(
                            directory,
                            entry,
                            expect_directory=True,
                            typed_reason="trace_threadblock_unreadable",
                        )
                    )
                elif entry.name.endswith(".pb"):
                    record = self._open_child(
                        directory,
                        entry,
                        expect_directory=False,
                        typed_reason="trace_threadblock_unreadable",
                    )
                    self._capture_payload(record)
                    self._threadblocks.append(record)
            pending.extend(reversed(children))
        self._threadblocks.sort(key=lambda record: str(record.path))

    def capture(self) -> None:
        root = self._open_root_chain()
        root_entries = self._capture_inventory(root, "trace_root_unreadable")

        root_entry = self._required_entry(
            root_entries,
            "dynamic_trace.pb",
            root.path / "dynamic_trace.pb",
            "trace_root_unreadable",
        )
        self._root_file = self._open_child(
            root,
            root_entry,
            expect_directory=False,
            typed_reason="trace_root_unreadable",
        )
        self._capture_payload(self._root_file)

        stats_entry = self._required_entry(
            root_entries,
            "stats.csv",
            root.path / "stats.csv",
            "stats_unreadable",
        )
        self._stats_file = self._open_child(
            root,
            stats_entry,
            expect_directory=False,
            typed_reason="stats_unreadable",
        )
        self._capture_payload(self._stats_file)

        threadblocks_entry = self._required_entry(
            root_entries,
            "threadblocks",
            root.path / "threadblocks",
            "trace_unreadable",
        )
        threadblocks_root = self._open_child(
            root,
            threadblocks_entry,
            expect_directory=True,
            typed_reason="trace_threadblock_unreadable",
        )
        self._capture_threadblocks(threadblocks_root)

        extra_info_entry = next(
            (entry for entry in root_entries if entry.name == "extra_info"),
            None,
        )
        if extra_info_entry is not None:
            if not stat.S_ISDIR(extra_info_entry.state.mode):
                self._raise(
                    "allocations_sidecar_malformed",
                    root.path / "extra_info",
                    "extra_info exists but is not a directory",
                )
            extra_info = self._open_child(
                root,
                extra_info_entry,
                expect_directory=True,
                typed_reason="allocations_sidecar_malformed",
            )
            extra_entries = self._capture_inventory(
                extra_info,
                "allocations_sidecar_malformed",
            )
            allocation_entry = next(
                (
                    entry
                    for entry in extra_entries
                    if entry.name == "allocations.json"
                ),
                None,
            )
            if allocation_entry is not None:
                if not stat.S_ISREG(allocation_entry.state.mode):
                    self._raise(
                        "allocations_sidecar_malformed",
                        extra_info.path / "allocations.json",
                        "allocations sidecar is not a regular file",
                    )
                self._allocation_file = self._open_child(
                    extra_info,
                    allocation_entry,
                    expect_directory=False,
                    typed_reason="allocations_sidecar_malformed",
                )
                self._capture_payload(self._allocation_file)

    @property
    def root_bytes(self) -> bytes:
        assert self._root_file is not None
        assert self._root_file.payload is not None
        return self._root_file.payload

    @property
    def stats_bytes(self) -> bytes:
        assert self._stats_file is not None
        assert self._stats_file.payload is not None
        return self._stats_file.payload

    @property
    def threadblock_bytes(self) -> tuple[TraceThreadblockBytes, ...]:
        payloads: list[TraceThreadblockBytes] = []
        for record in self._threadblocks:
            assert record.payload is not None
            payloads.append(
                TraceThreadblockBytes(path=record.path, data=record.payload)
            )
        return tuple(payloads)

    @property
    def validation_snapshot(self) -> TraceDirValidationSnapshot:
        allocation_bytes: bytes | None = None
        if self._allocation_file is not None:
            assert self._allocation_file.payload is not None
            allocation_bytes = self._allocation_file.payload
        return TraceDirValidationSnapshot(
            threadblocks=self.threadblock_bytes,
            allocations_sidecar=allocation_bytes,
        )

    def _verify_descriptors(self) -> None:
        for record in self._descriptors:
            try:
                descriptor_state = _StatState.capture(os.fstat(record.fd))
            except OSError as exc:
                self._raise(
                    record.typed_reason,
                    record.path,
                    f"descriptor post-verification failed: {exc}",
                )
            if record.strict_state:
                descriptor_matches = descriptor_state == record.initial
            else:
                descriptor_matches = self._same_object(
                    descriptor_state,
                    record.initial,
                )
            if not descriptor_matches:
                self._raise(
                    record.typed_reason,
                    record.path,
                    "descriptor identity or metadata changed after snapshot",
                )
            if record.parent_fd is None or record.name is None:
                continue
            path_state = self._lstat_at(
                record.parent_fd,
                record.name,
                record.path,
                record.typed_reason,
            )
            if record.strict_state:
                path_matches = path_state == record.initial
            else:
                path_matches = self._same_object(path_state, record.initial)
            if not path_matches:
                self._raise(
                    record.typed_reason,
                    record.path,
                    "anchored path no longer names the snapshotted descriptor",
                )

    def _verify_inventories(self) -> None:
        for inventory in self._inventories:
            current = self._scan_directory(
                inventory.directory,
                inventory.typed_reason,
            )
            if current != inventory.entries:
                self._raise(
                    inventory.typed_reason,
                    inventory.directory.path,
                    "exact directory inventory changed after snapshot",
                )

    def verify(self) -> None:
        self._verify_descriptors()
        self._verify_inventories()
        for record in self._descriptors:
            if record.payload is None:
                continue
            current = self._read_exact_descriptor(record)
            if current != record.payload:
                self._raise(
                    record.typed_reason,
                    record.path,
                    "descriptor bytes changed after snapshot",
                )
        # Bracket byte re-reads with another identity/inventory pass so a
        # mutation during verification cannot escape merely because its entry
        # was checked earlier in the walk.
        self._verify_descriptors()
        self._verify_inventories()

    def close(self) -> None:
        while self._descriptors:
            record = self._descriptors.pop()
            try:
                os.close(record.fd)
            except OSError:
                pass


@contextmanager
def _stable_trace_snapshot(
    trace_dir: Path,
) -> Iterator[_TraceSnapshotTransaction]:
    snapshot = _TraceSnapshotTransaction(trace_dir)
    try:
        snapshot.capture()
        snapshot.verify()
        yield snapshot
    finally:
        snapshot.close()


def _raise_admission_prerequisite(
    exc: TraceContractTrackedBindingsCorrupt | TraceContractRuntimePrerequisiteMissing,
) -> NoReturn:
    if isinstance(exc, TraceContractTrackedBindingsCorrupt):
        raise TraceAdmissionError("tracked_protobuf_corrupt", str(exc)) from exc
    raise TraceAdmissionError(
        "protobuf_runtime_prerequisite_missing", str(exc)
    ) from exc


def _import_trace_pb2() -> Any:
    # The shared loader verifies the runtime, all nine tracked authorities, and
    # module provenance before the root Trace binding is imported.
    _import_pb_modules()
    if str(PB_GENERATED) not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, str(PB_GENERATED))
    try:
        import trace_pb2  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
    except Exception as exc:
        if exc.__class__.__module__.startswith("google.protobuf"):
            raise TraceContractRuntimePrerequisiteMissing(
                "protobuf runtime prerequisite is incompatible with the "
                f"tracked trace binding: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
            ) from exc
        raise TraceContractTrackedBindingsCorrupt(
            "tracked protobuf authority trace_pb2.py is unusable; restore "
            "its byte-exact committed content with `git restore "
            "--source=HEAD --worktree -- "
            "workloads/simbench_bw/_pb_generated/trace_pb2.py`; do not "
            f"regenerate bindings in the canonical checkout: {exc}"
        ) from exc
    try:
        Path(trace_pb2.__file__).resolve().relative_to(PB_GENERATED.resolve())
    except (AttributeError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise TraceAdmissionError(
            "protobuf_bindings_mismatch",
            f"trace_pb2 resolved outside {PB_GENERATED}: "
            f"{getattr(trace_pb2, '__file__', None)}",
        ) from exc
    return trace_pb2


def _parse_stats_bytes(raw: bytes, stats_path: Path) -> tuple[int, int]:
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
        rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(text, newline="")))
    except (UnicodeError, csv.Error) as exc:
        raise TraceAdmissionError(
            "stats_unreadable",
            f"{stats_path}: {exc}",
        ) from exc
    if not rows:
        raise TraceAdmissionError("stats_empty", str(stats_path))
    header = [cell.strip() for cell in rows[0]]
    try:
        expected_index = header.index("total_insts")
        admitted_index = header.index("total_reported_insts")
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise TraceAdmissionError(
            "stats_schema_invalid",
            "stats.csv lacks total_insts/total_reported_insts",
        ) from exc

    expected = admitted = row_count = 0
    for line_number, row in enumerate(rows[1:], start=2):
        cells = [cell.strip() for cell in row]
        if not any(cells):
            continue
        if len(cells) <= max(expected_index, admitted_index):
            raise TraceAdmissionError(
                "stats_schema_invalid", f"row {line_number} is truncated"
            )
        try:
            row_expected = int(cells[expected_index])
            row_admitted = int(cells[admitted_index])
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise TraceAdmissionError(
                "stats_schema_invalid", f"row {line_number} has non-integer counters"
            ) from exc
        if row_expected < 0 or row_admitted < 0 or row_admitted > row_expected:
            raise TraceAdmissionError(
                "stats_counters_invalid",
                f"row {line_number}: expected={row_expected} admitted={row_admitted}",
            )
        expected += row_expected
        admitted += row_admitted
        row_count += 1
    if row_count == 0 or expected <= 0 or admitted <= 0:
        raise TraceAdmissionError(
            "trace_payload_empty",
            f"stats rows={row_count} expected={expected} admitted={admitted}",
        )
    return expected, admitted


def _parse_stats(stats_path: Path) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Compatibility path reader; admission itself uses snapshot bytes."""

    try:
        raw = stats_path.read_bytes()
    except OSError as exc:
        raise TraceAdmissionError("stats_unreadable", str(exc)) from exc
    return _parse_stats_bytes(raw, stats_path)


def _admit_snapshot(snapshot: _TraceSnapshotTransaction) -> TraceAdmission:
    root_path = snapshot.trace_dir / "dynamic_trace.pb"
    root_bytes = snapshot.root_bytes
    if not root_bytes:
        raise TraceAdmissionError("trace_root_empty", str(root_path))

    try:
        trace_pb2 = _import_trace_pb2()
    except (
        TraceContractTrackedBindingsCorrupt,
        TraceContractRuntimePrerequisiteMissing,
    ) as exc:
        _raise_admission_prerequisite(exc)
    root = trace_pb2.Trace()
    try:
        root.ParseFromString(root_bytes)
    except Exception as exc:  # protobuf raises version-specific decode classes
        raise TraceAdmissionError("trace_root_unparseable", str(exc)) from exc
    if root.trace_contract_id != EXPECTED_TRACE_CONTRACT_ID:
        raise TraceAdmissionError(
            "trace_contract_mismatch",
            f"got {root.trace_contract_id!r}, expected {EXPECTED_TRACE_CONTRACT_ID!r}",
        )
    missing_classes = sorted(
        EXPECTED_MEMORY_PAYLOAD_CLASSES - set(root.memory_payload_classes)
    )
    if missing_classes:
        raise TraceAdmissionError(
            "trace_capabilities_incomplete", f"missing classes {missing_classes}"
        )

    launches = []
    launch_identities: set[tuple[int, int, int]] = set()
    for device_key, device in root.gpu_device.items():
        device_id = int(device.id)
        if int(device_key) != device_id or device_id < 0:
            raise TraceAdmissionError(
                "trace_launch_identity_invalid",
                f"device map key/id mismatch: {int(device_key)}/{device_id}",
            )
        for stream_key, stream in device.streams.items():
            stream_id = int(stream.id)
            if int(stream_key) != stream_id or stream_id < 0:
                raise TraceAdmissionError(
                    "trace_launch_identity_invalid",
                    f"stream map key/id mismatch: {int(stream_key)}/{stream_id}",
                )
            for kernel in stream.kernels:
                kernel_id = int(kernel.id)
                identity = (device_id, stream_id, kernel_id)
                if (
                    kernel_id <= 0
                    or not kernel.name
                    or identity in launch_identities
                ):
                    raise TraceAdmissionError(
                        "trace_launch_identity_invalid",
                        f"invalid or duplicate launch identity {identity}: "
                        f"name={kernel.name!r}",
                    )
                launch_identities.add(identity)
                launches.append(kernel)
    if not launches:
        raise TraceAdmissionError(
            "trace_launches_empty", "root Trace has zero launches"
        )
    for index, kernel in enumerate(launches):
        geometry = (
            int(kernel.grid_dim.x),
            int(kernel.grid_dim.y),
            int(kernel.grid_dim.z),
            int(kernel.block_dim.x),
            int(kernel.block_dim.y),
            int(kernel.block_dim.z),
        )
        if any(value <= 0 for value in geometry):
            raise TraceAdmissionError(
                "trace_launch_geometry_invalid",
                f"launch {index} has grid/block geometry {geometry}",
            )

    validation_snapshot = snapshot.validation_snapshot
    try:
        contract = validate_trace_dir(
            snapshot.trace_dir,
            snapshot=validation_snapshot,
        )
    except (
        TraceContractTrackedBindingsCorrupt,
        TraceContractRuntimePrerequisiteMissing,
    ) as exc:
        _raise_admission_prerequisite(exc)
    if not contract.ok:
        raise TraceAdmissionError(
            contract.typed_reason or "trace_contract_invalid",
            contract.detail or "threadblock contract validation failed",
        )

    threadblocks = validation_snapshot.threadblocks
    if not threadblocks:
        raise TraceAdmissionError(
            "trace_threadblocks_empty",
            "threadblocks/ contains zero protobuf files",
        )
    try:
        threadblock_pb2, _instruction_pb2, _address_pb2 = _import_pb_modules()
    except (
        TraceContractTrackedBindingsCorrupt,
        TraceContractRuntimePrerequisiteMissing,
    ) as exc:
        _raise_admission_prerequisite(exc)
    try:
        Path(threadblock_pb2.__file__).resolve().relative_to(
            PB_GENERATED.resolve()
        )
    except (AttributeError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise TraceAdmissionError(
            "protobuf_bindings_mismatch",
            f"threadblock_pb2 resolved outside {PB_GENERATED}: "
            f"{getattr(threadblock_pb2, '__file__', None)}",
        ) from exc
    instruction_count = 0
    for threadblock in threadblocks:
        raw = threadblock.data
        path = threadblock.path
        if not raw:
            raise TraceAdmissionError("trace_threadblock_empty", str(path))
        message = threadblock_pb2.threadblock()
        try:
            message.ParseFromString(raw)
        except Exception as exc:
            raise TraceAdmissionError(
                "trace_threadblock_unparseable", f"{path}: {exc}"
            ) from exc
        block_records = sum(
            len(warp.instructions) for warp in message.warps.values()
        )
        if block_records <= 0:
            raise TraceAdmissionError(
                "trace_threadblock_empty",
                f"{path} has zero instruction records",
            )
        instruction_count += block_records

    expected, admitted = _parse_stats_bytes(
        snapshot.stats_bytes,
        snapshot.trace_dir / "stats.csv",
    )
    return TraceAdmission(
        launch_count=len(launches),
        threadblock_count=len(threadblocks),
        instruction_count=instruction_count,
        expected_record_count=expected,
        admitted_record_count=admitted,
    )


def require_trace_admission(trace_dir: Path) -> TraceAdmission:
    """Admit one trace from a single anchored stable-snapshot transaction."""

    with _stable_trace_snapshot(trace_dir) as snapshot:
        admission = _admit_snapshot(snapshot)
        snapshot.verify()
        return admission


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description=__doc__,
        epilog=f"authority scope: {TRACE_ADMISSION_SCOPE}",
    )
    parser.add_argument("trace_dir", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        result = require_trace_admission(args.trace_dir)
    except TraceAdmissionError as exc:
        print(f"trace_admission: FAIL {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(json.dumps(asdict(result), sort_keys=True))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

import tools.nvbit_tracer.import_trace_contract as import_trace_contract
import tools.nvbit_tracer.trace_admission as trace_admission
from tools.nvbit_tracer.trace_admission import (
    PB_GENERATED,
    TRACE_ADMISSION_SCOPE,
    TraceAdmissionError,
    _raise_admission_prerequisite,
    require_trace_admission,

from tools.nvbit_tracer.import_trace_contract import (
    TraceContractRuntimePrerequisiteMissing,
    TraceContractTrackedBindingsCorrupt,
)


def _pb_modules():
    required = (
        "address_pb2.py", "cuda_stream_pb2.py", "dim3d_pb2.py",
        "gpu_device_pb2.py", "instruction_pb2.py", "kernel_pb2.py",
        "threadblock_pb2.py", "trace_pb2.py", "warp_pb2.py",
    )
    missing = [
        name
        for name in required
        if not (PB_GENERATED / name).is_file()
        or (PB_GENERATED / name).is_symlink()
    ]
    assert not missing, (
        "tracked protobuf authority is missing; restore byte-exact committed "
        "content with `git restore --source=HEAD --worktree -- "
        + " ".join(
            f"workloads/simbench_bw/_pb_generated/{name}" for name in missing
        )
        + "`"
    )
    if str(PB_GENERATED) not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, str(PB_GENERATED))
    try:
        import threadblock_pb2  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
        import trace_pb2  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
    except ImportError as exc:
        pytest.fail(f"tracked dynamic-trace authorities are unusable: {exc}")
    return trace_pb2, threadblock_pb2


def _write_trace(root: Path, *, launch: bool = True, instruction: bool = True,
                 expected: int = 1, admitted: int = 1) -> Path:
    trace_pb2, threadblock_pb2 = _pb_modules()
    root.mkdir()

    trace = trace_pb2.Trace()
    trace.trace_contract_id = "sm86_addr_carry_v1"
    trace.memory_payload_classes.extend([1, 2, 3, 6, 8])
    if launch:
        device = trace.gpu_device[0]
        device.id = 0
        stream = device.streams[0]
        stream.id = 0
        kernel = stream.kernels.add()
        kernel.id = 1
        kernel.name = "fixture_kernel"
        kernel.grid_dim.x = kernel.grid_dim.y = kernel.grid_dim.z = 1
        kernel.block_dim.x = 32
        kernel.block_dim.y = kernel.block_dim.z = 1
    (root / "dynamic_trace.pb").write_bytes(trace.SerializeToString())

    tb = threadblock_pb2.threadblock()
    tb.block_id.x = tb.block_id.y = tb.block_id.z = 0
    if instruction:
        warp = tb.warps[0]
        warp.id = 0
        inst = warp.instructions.add()
        inst.pc = inst.vpc = 0x1000
        inst.active_mask = inst.predicate_mask = 1
        inst.function_unique_id = 1
        inst.data_width = 4
        inst.warpid_tb = 0
    tb_path = root / "threadblocks" / "device_0" / "stream_0" / "kernel_1" / "0.pb"
    tb_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    tb_path.write_bytes(tb.SerializeToString())
    (root / "stats.csv").write_text(
        "kernel_id,total_insts,total_reported_insts\n"
        f"1,{expected},{admitted}\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    return root


def _threadblock_path(trace_dir: Path) -> Path:
    paths = sorted((trace_dir / "threadblocks").rglob("*.pb"))
    assert len(paths) == 1
    return paths[0]


def _mutate_after_contract_validation(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    mutation: Callable[[], None],
) -> None:
    original = trace_admission.validate_trace_dir

    def validating_then_mutating(traces_dir: Path, *, snapshot):
        result = original(traces_dir, snapshot=snapshot)
        assert result.ok
        mutation()
        return result

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        trace_admission,
        "validate_trace_dir",
        validating_then_mutating,
    )


def test_require_trace_admission_accepts_nonvacuous_capture(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    result = require_trace_admission(_write_trace(tmp_path / "trace"))
    assert result.launch_count == 1
    assert result.threadblock_count == 1
    assert result.instruction_count == 1
    assert result.expected_record_count == 1
    assert result.admitted_record_count == 1


def test_validation_consumes_snapshotted_threadblock_bytes_without_path_reopen(
    tmp_path: Path,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    trace_dir = _write_trace(tmp_path / "trace")
    allocation_bytes = b"[]\n"
    allocation_path = trace_dir / "extra_info" / "allocations.json"
    allocation_path.parent.mkdir()
    allocation_path.write_bytes(allocation_bytes)
    expected_path = _threadblock_path(trace_dir)
    expected_bytes = expected_path.read_bytes()
    original = trace_admission.validate_trace_dir
    seen = False

    def spy(traces_dir: Path, *, snapshot):
        nonlocal seen
        seen = True
        assert traces_dir == trace_dir
        assert len(snapshot.threadblocks) == 1
        assert snapshot.threadblocks[0].path == expected_path
        assert snapshot.threadblocks[0].data == expected_bytes
        assert snapshot.allocations_sidecar == allocation_bytes
        return original(traces_dir, snapshot=snapshot)

    def forbidden_path_reader(*_args, **_kwargs):
        raise AssertionError("snapshot validation reopened a threadblock path")

    monkeypatch.setattr(trace_admission, "validate_trace_dir", spy)
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        import_trace_contract,
        "validate_threadblock_path",
        forbidden_path_reader,
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(Path, "read_bytes", forbidden_path_reader)
    monkeypatch.setattr(Path, "open", forbidden_path_reader)

    require_trace_admission(trace_dir)
    assert seen


def test_require_trace_admission_rejects_symlinked_ancestor(
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    real_parent = tmp_path / "real_parent"
    real_parent.mkdir()
    _write_trace(real_parent / "trace")
    linked_parent = tmp_path / "linked_parent"
    linked_parent.symlink_to(real_parent, target_is_directory=True)

    with pytest.raises(TraceAdmissionError) as caught:
        require_trace_admission(linked_parent / "trace")
    assert caught.value.typed_reason == "trace_root_unreadable"
    assert "symbolic links are not admissible" in caught.value.detail


def test_require_trace_admission_rejects_symlinked_root(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    real_trace = _write_trace(tmp_path / "real_trace")
    linked_trace = tmp_path / "linked_trace"
    linked_trace.symlink_to(real_trace, target_is_directory=True)

    with pytest.raises(TraceAdmissionError) as caught:
        require_trace_admission(linked_trace)
    assert caught.value.typed_reason == "trace_root_unreadable"
    assert "symbolic links are not admissible" in caught.value.detail


@pytest.mark.parametrize("leaf", ["dynamic_trace.pb", "stats.csv", "threadblock"])
def test_require_trace_admission_rejects_symlinked_leaf(
    tmp_path: Path,
    leaf: str,
) -> None:
    trace_dir = _write_trace(tmp_path / "trace")
    victim = (
        _threadblock_path(trace_dir)
        if leaf == "threadblock"
        else trace_dir / leaf
    )
    target = tmp_path / f"real-{victim.name}"
    victim.rename(target)
    victim.symlink_to(target)

    with pytest.raises(TraceAdmissionError) as caught:
        require_trace_admission(trace_dir)
    assert caught.value.typed_reason in {
        "trace_root_unreadable",
        "trace_threadblock_unreadable",
    }
    assert "symbolic links are not admissible" in caught.value.detail


def test_require_trace_admission_rejects_symlinked_threadblock_ancestor(

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("artifact", "expected_reason"),
    (
        ("dynamic_trace.pb", "trace_root_unreadable"),
        ("stats.csv", "trace_root_unreadable"),
        ("threadblock", "trace_threadblock_unreadable"),
    ),
)
def test_require_trace_admission_rejects_replacement_between_phases(
    tmp_path: Path,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    artifact: str,
    expected_reason: str,
) -> None:
    trace_dir = _write_trace(tmp_path / "trace")
    victim = (
        _threadblock_path(trace_dir)
        if artifact == "threadblock"
        else trace_dir / artifact
    )
    original_bytes = victim.read_bytes()
    original_identity = (victim.stat().st_dev, victim.stat().st_ino)

    def replace() -> None:
        replacement = victim.with_name(f"{victim.name}.replacement")
        replacement.write_bytes(original_bytes)
        os.replace(replacement, victim)
        assert (victim.stat().st_dev, victim.stat().st_ino) != original_identity

    _mutate_after_contract_validation(monkeypatch, replace)

    with pytest.raises(TraceAdmissionError) as caught:
        require_trace_admission(trace_dir)
    assert caught.value.typed_reason == expected_reason
    assert "changed after snapshot" in caught.value.detail


def test_require_trace_admission_rejects_in_place_same_size_mutation(
    tmp_path: Path,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    trace_dir = _write_trace(tmp_path / "trace")
    stats_path = trace_dir / "stats.csv"
    before = stats_path.read_bytes()
    after = before.replace(b"1,1,1\n", b"1,2,1\n")
    assert after != before
    assert len(after) == len(before)
    original_identity = (stats_path.stat().st_dev, stats_path.stat().st_ino)

    def mutate_in_place() -> None:
        stats_path.write_bytes(after)
        current = stats_path.stat()
        assert (current.st_dev, current.st_ino) == original_identity
        assert current.st_size == len(before)

    _mutate_after_contract_validation(monkeypatch, mutate_in_place)

    with pytest.raises(TraceAdmissionError) as caught:
        require_trace_admission(trace_dir)
    assert caught.value.typed_reason == "stats_unreadable"
    assert "changed after snapshot" in caught.value.detail

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "identity_drift",
    ["zero_kernel", "empty_name", "device_key", "stream_key", "duplicate"],
)
def test_require_trace_admission_rejects_invalid_launch_identity(
    tmp_path: Path, identity_drift: str,
) -> None:
    trace_dir = _write_trace(tmp_path / "trace")
    trace_pb2, _threadblock_pb2 = _pb_modules()
    root_path = trace_dir / "dynamic_trace.pb"
    root = trace_pb2.Trace()
    root.ParseFromString(root_path.read_bytes())
    device = root.gpu_device[0]
    stream = device.streams[0]
    kernel = stream.kernels[0]
    if identity_drift == "zero_kernel":
        kernel.id = 0
    elif identity_drift == "empty_name":
        kernel.name = ""
    elif identity_drift == "device_key":
        device.id = 1
    elif identity_drift == "stream_key":
        stream.id = 1
    else:
        stream.kernels.add().CopyFrom(kernel)
    root_path.write_bytes(root.SerializeToString())

    with pytest.raises(TraceAdmissionError) as caught:
        require_trace_admission(trace_dir)
    assert caught.value.typed_reason == "trace_launch_identity_invalid"
```

```rust
// This file is @generated by prost-build.
/// Per-instruction memory address record. The contents of `addrs`
/// depend on `compression_format`:
///
///    * compression_format == 0 (list_all): `addrs` carries exactly
///      32 entries, one per warp lane. Active+predicated lanes hold
///      the real per-lane address; inactive lanes hold the sentinel
///      value -1 (declared in tracer_tool.cu as LANE_INACTIVE_SENTINEL).
///      Real GPU virtual addresses are non-negative uint64 values, so
///      -1 (cast through int64) is unambiguous and cannot collide
///      with a real address. Consumers reading list_all records can
///      skip sentinel entries; the count of non-sentinel entries
///      equals popcount(active_mask & predicate_mask).
///    * compression_format == 1 (base_stride): `addrs` is empty;
///      `base_address + stride` defines the address sequence.
///    * compression_format == 2 (base_delta): `addrs` carries deltas
///      relative to `base_address`, length up to 31 (the base lane
///      is implicit). Compressed formats are an optimization; consumers
///      reconstruct them into 32 lane slots downstream.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, ::prost::Message)]
pub struct Address {
    #[prost(int32, tag = "1")]
    pub data_width: i32,
    #[prost(uint32, tag = "2")]
    pub udesc_value: u32,
    #[prost(int32, tag = "3")]
    pub compression_format: i32,
    #[prost(uint64, tag = "4")]
    pub base_address: u64,
    #[prost(int32, tag = "5")]
    pub stride: i32,
    #[prost(int64, repeated, tag = "6")]
    pub addrs: ::prost::alloc::vec::Vec<i64>,
    /// Monotonic allocation id from the tracer's per-context
    /// allocator registry (see `nvbit_at_cuda_event` hooks for
    /// cuMemAlloc_v2 / cuMemFree_v2 in tracer_tool.cu). Allocation
    /// ids start at 1, so proto3 default 0 stays distinct as the
    /// "unresolved" sentinel; HasField=false means the producer's
    /// registry lookup did not resolve this record's address to
    /// any registered allocation. That distinction is the wire
    /// signal a future `unmapped_memory_range` sidecar (task11b)
    /// will use. The field carries the id of the allocation
    /// containing the lowest active+predicated-lane address; for
    /// gather/scatter patterns where active lanes touch different
    /// allocations, the out-of-range lanes will surface separately
    /// through the typed-exclusion sidecar path. The full
    /// allocation registry is also serialized to
    /// `traces/extra_info/allocations.json` so consumers can
    /// resolve `allocation_id` -> {base, size, alive} without
    /// re-instrumenting.
    #[prost(uint32, optional, tag = "7")]
    pub allocation_id: ::core::option::Option<u32>,
    /// Effective memory space of this address record's operand (see MemorySpace).
    /// Net-new with the address-carrying contract; absent on pre-transition traces
    /// (HasField=false → legacy fallback: consumers treat the instruction-level
    /// MemoryOpClass as the space, as before the transition). For a global-source /
    /// shared-destination instruction (LDGSTS) each address record carries its own
    /// space so the identity gate applies allocation resolution to the global side
    /// only. See plans/sm86_ldgsts_atoms_operand_adjudication.md.
    #[prost(enumeration = "MemorySpace", optional, tag = "8")]
    pub address_space: ::core::option::Option<i32>,
}
/// Effective memory space of an address record's operand. Net-new with the
/// ASYNC_COPY+ATOM address-carrying contract transition: a single instruction can
/// carry operands in different spaces (LDGSTS reads GLOBAL, writes SHARED), so the
/// space is a per-ADDRESS property, not the instruction-level MemoryOpClass. This
/// is the discriminator the allocation-identity gate keys on — only
/// MEMORY_SPACE_GLOBAL (and generic that resolves global) requires an
/// allocation_id; MEMORY_SPACE_SHARED/LOCAL are exempt (allocation_id 0 legit). A
/// dedicated enum (not MemoryOpClass) because instruction.proto imports
/// address.proto — reusing MemoryOpClass here would be a circular import — and
/// because a space is semantically distinct from an op class. Additive per the
/// CLAUDE.md wire-extension policy; absent on pre-transition traces.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, ::prost::Enumeration)]
#[repr(i32)]
pub enum MemorySpace {
    Unspecified = 0,
    Global = 1,
    Shared = 2,
    Local = 3,
    Generic = 4,
}
impl MemorySpace {
    /// String value of the enum field names used in the ProtoBuf definition.
    ///
    /// The values are not transformed in any way and thus are considered stable
    /// (if the ProtoBuf definition does not change) and safe for programmatic use.
    pub fn as_str_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Unspecified => "MEMORY_SPACE_UNSPECIFIED",
            Self::Global => "MEMORY_SPACE_GLOBAL",
            Self::Shared => "MEMORY_SPACE_SHARED",
            Self::Local => "MEMORY_SPACE_LOCAL",
            Self::Generic => "MEMORY_SPACE_GENERIC",
        }
    }
    /// Creates an enum from field names used in the ProtoBuf definition.
    pub fn from_str_name(value: &str) -> ::core::option::Option<Self> {
        match value {
            "MEMORY_SPACE_UNSPECIFIED" => Some(Self::Unspecified),
            "MEMORY_SPACE_GLOBAL" => Some(Self::Global),
            "MEMORY_SPACE_SHARED" => Some(Self::Shared),
            "MEMORY_SPACE_LOCAL" => Some(Self::Local),
            "MEMORY_SPACE_GENERIC" => Some(Self::Generic),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, ::prost::Message)]
pub struct Instruction {
    /// Existing fields (tags 1-5) are unchanged so older readers can
    /// still parse new traces and silently ignore the new tags >= 6.
    #[prost(uint32, tag = "1")]
    pub pc: u32,
    /// Tag numbers preserved when `optional` is added so older
    /// readers can still parse new traces. The change here is
    /// observability: proto3 explicit-presence lets the validator
    /// distinguish "tracer did not emit this field" (HasField false)
    /// from "tracer emitted value 0" (HasField true with the proto3
    /// default value). Without explicit-presence, a regression that
    /// dropped the producer's `inst->set_active_mask(...)` /
    /// `inst->set_predicate_mask(...)` calls would be silently
    /// admitted because the proto3 default 0 is a valid lane-mask
    /// value (predicated-off all-lanes-inactive case). Setters on
    /// the producer side are wire-compatible; no producer-code
    /// change is required.
    #[prost(uint32, optional, tag = "2")]
    pub active_mask: ::core::option::Option<u32>,
    #[prost(uint32, optional, tag = "3")]
    pub predicate_mask: ::core::option::Option<u32>,
    #[prost(int32, tag = "4")]
    pub function_unique_id: i32,
    #[prost(message, repeated, tag = "5")]
    pub addresses: ::prost::alloc::vec::Vec<Address>,
    /// Operation class. Marked `optional` so a non-memory instruction
    /// (ALU, branch, control flow) can leave the field absent on the
    /// wire. The downstream contract validator interprets:
    ///    - field absent: this is not a memory instruction; addresses
    ///      list is also expected to be empty.
    ///    - field present and != UNSPECIFIED: a memory instruction whose
    ///      op-class the tracer determined.
    ///    - field present and == UNSPECIFIED: contract violation; the
    ///      tracer encountered a memory instruction it could not
    ///      classify and should have emitted a typed
    ///      `unsupported_memory_path` exclusion sidecar instead.
    #[prost(enumeration = "MemoryOpClass", optional, tag = "6")]
    pub memory_op_class: ::core::option::Option<i32>,
    /// Width of the per-lane access in bytes (e.g. 4 for an int32
    /// load, 16 for a 128-bit load). Mirrors the per-warp-instruction
    /// data width that already appears on `address.data_width`, but is
    /// promoted to instruction level so consumers do not have to walk
    /// the address list to discover the width when no addresses are
    /// emitted (e.g. predicated-off warps with all-lanes-inactive).
    /// Marked `optional` for proto3 explicit presence so consumers can
    /// distinguish "tracer did not emit data_width" from "data_width
    /// value 0" (which is a contract violation analogous to
    /// MEMORY_OP_CLASS_UNSPECIFIED — the loss-of-diagnostic Codex
    /// flagged in R8 v2 review).
    #[prost(int32, optional, tag = "7")]
    pub data_width: ::core::option::Option<i32>,
    /// Warp index inside the threadblock (0 <= warpid_tb < blockDim
    /// total / 32). This is the lane-grouping the SIMT scheduler uses
    /// and the one downstream coalescer needs. Marked `optional` so
    /// proto3 explicit presence distinguishes "warp 0" (valid) from
    /// "tracer did not emit this field" (absent on the wire). Required
    /// because SM/warp 0 is a perfectly valid ID and a plain int32
    /// scalar would collapse it to the proto3 zero default.
    #[prost(int32, optional, tag = "8")]
    pub warpid_tb: ::core::option::Option<i32>,
    /// Warp index on the SM, where exposed by NVBit. Marked `optional`
    /// so absence on the wire ("not exposed by the NVBit runtime
    /// present at trace time") is observationally distinct from value
    /// 0 (warp 0 on the SM). The AC4 plan permits this so traces
    /// from older NVBit releases stay admissible.
    #[prost(int32, optional, tag = "9")]
    pub warpid_sm: ::core::option::Option<i32>,
    /// SM id, where exposed by NVBit. Marked `optional` for the same
    /// reason: SM 0 is a valid id and must be distinguishable from
    /// "tracer did not emit this field". When the NVBit runtime does
    /// not expose the SM id, the field is simply omitted (has_sm_id()
    /// returns false on the C++ side; the field is absent on the
    /// wire); when it is exposed, the actual value is written
    /// including 0.
    #[prost(int32, optional, tag = "10")]
    pub sm_id: ::core::option::Option<i32>,
    /// Virtual program counter. Widens the existing `pc` field
    /// (uint32) to uint64 because PC ranges on post-Hopper
    /// architectures may exceed 32 bits when the code lives in a
    /// long-running kernel module mapped at a high virtual address.
    /// The legacy `pc` field stays so older readers continue to work;
    /// new emitters should populate both `pc` (low 32 bits) and `vpc`
    /// (full 64-bit virtual PC). Marked `optional` for proto3
    /// explicit-presence so the validator can distinguish "tracer
    /// did not emit vpc" (HasField false) from "vpc=0" (HasField
    /// true with a value that legitimately equals pc=0 for the
    /// first instruction in a kernel). Tag number unchanged.
    #[prost(uint64, optional, tag = "11")]
    pub vpc: ::core::option::Option<u64>,
    /// Access-kind dimension orthogonal to memory_op_class. The
    /// producer-side SASS classifier maps the opcode head to one of
    /// {load, store, atomic, async-copy}; downstream consumers use
    /// the kind to distinguish write-allocate paths (global stores
    /// fetch the line on miss, just like loads) from
    /// no-write-allocate paths (shared stores do not touch L2;
    /// async-copy destination side flows into shared without an L2
    /// write-allocate). Marked `optional` so legacy traces emitted
    /// before this field landed remain admissible (HasField false
    /// routes to UNSPECIFIED on the consumer side). Tag 12 is the
    /// next available after the existing tags 1-11. Producer-side
    /// C++ classifier lands in a future round; this tag reserves
    /// the wire slot and the consumer reads it when present.
    #[prost(enumeration = "MemoryOpAccessKind", optional, tag = "12")]
    pub memory_op_access_kind: ::core::option::Option<i32>,
    /// Cache-operator dimension orthogonal to both memory_op_class
    /// (memory space) AND memory_op_access_kind (load/store/atomic/
    /// async-copy direction). The producer-side SASS classifier at
    /// tools/cache_predictor/l1_cache_op_classifier.py maps the
    /// opcode head (LDG.E.CA / LDG.E.STRONG.SM / LDGSTS / LDL /
    /// STL / ATOM / TEX / etc.) to one of the closed 12-token
    /// underscore-vocabulary InstructionCacheOp values. The
    /// downstream L1 predictor head's per-SM walker filters
    /// l1_eligible accesses by this field; it answers "how does the
    /// cache operator decide whether this access touches the modeled
    /// L1 line state".
    ///
    /// Per CLAUDE.md "Two-Device Local Development Model" and
    /// BL-20260505, the classifier records the actual SASS encoding
    /// (Ampere LDG.E.CA -> LDG_E_CA; Blackwell LDG.E.STRONG.SM ->
    /// LDG_E_STRONG_SM), NOT the semantic equivalent class. The
    /// two arches' cache-operator behavior is per-architecture
    /// distinct.
    ///
    /// Marked `optional` so legacy traces emitted before this field
    /// landed remain admissible (HasField false routes to
    /// INSTRUCTION_CACHE_OP_UNSPECIFIED on the consumer side); the
    /// L1 predictor head treats absent or unspecified values as
    /// `predictor_l1_sass_provenance_missing`. Tag 13 is the next
    /// available after the existing tags 1-12.
    ///
    /// Three-surface lockstep with the JSON classifier manifest
    /// schema (tools/cache_predictor/cache_op_map.schema.json) +
    /// the cache_predictor._TYPED_REASONS frozenset + the
    /// comparison_runner module-level constants is enforced by the
    /// structural lockstep test at
    /// workloads/simbench_bw/tests/test_predictor_l1_sass_provenance_missing_lockstep.py
    /// per BL-20260507-arch-token-multi-surface-lockstep.
    #[prost(enumeration = "InstructionCacheOp", optional, tag = "13")]
    pub instruction_cache_op: ::core::option::Option<i32>,
}
/// AC4 enum: memory operation class for each emitted instruction.
/// MEMORY_OP_CLASS_UNSPECIFIED is the proto3 default zero value and
/// must NEVER be emitted by the tracer; readers treat it as a
/// contract violation. The nine original plan classes follow; the
/// tenth value MEMORY_OP_CLASS_TMEM was added for Blackwell
/// (sm_100) tensor-memory accesses via the `tcgen05.{ld,st}`
/// family (mnemonics `LDT` / `STT`). Per the CLAUDE.md wire-
/// extension policy this is an additive enum extension: producer
/// emits the new value, consumer accepts it; old readers that
/// only knew 0-9 either route the new value through their
/// catch-all path or REJECT (a closed-enum validator that
/// hard-codes the prior 10 cases as a frozenset is the only place
/// readers would break, and the consumer-side widening lands in
/// the same commit as this producer-side enum addition per
/// BL-20260507-multi-surface-lockstep-changes).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, ::prost::Enumeration)]
#[repr(i32)]
pub enum MemoryOpClass {
    Unspecified = 0,
    Global = 1,
    Shared = 2,
    Local = 3,
    Texture = 4,
    Surface = 5,
    Atomic = 6,
    Tma = 7,
    AsyncCopy = 8,
    ClusterDsmem = 9,
    Tmem = 10,
}
impl MemoryOpClass {
    /// String value of the enum field names used in the ProtoBuf definition.
    ///
    /// The values are not transformed in any way and thus are considered stable
    /// (if the ProtoBuf definition does not change) and safe for programmatic use.
    pub fn as_str_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Unspecified => "MEMORY_OP_CLASS_UNSPECIFIED",
            Self::Global => "MEMORY_OP_CLASS_GLOBAL",
            Self::Shared => "MEMORY_OP_CLASS_SHARED",
            Self::Local => "MEMORY_OP_CLASS_LOCAL",
            Self::Texture => "MEMORY_OP_CLASS_TEXTURE",
            Self::Surface => "MEMORY_OP_CLASS_SURFACE",
            Self::Atomic => "MEMORY_OP_CLASS_ATOMIC",
            Self::Tma => "MEMORY_OP_CLASS_TMA",
            Self::AsyncCopy => "MEMORY_OP_CLASS_ASYNC_COPY",
            Self::ClusterDsmem => "MEMORY_OP_CLASS_CLUSTER_DSMEM",

    }
    /// Creates an enum from field names used in the ProtoBuf definition.

            "MEMORY_OP_CLASS_GLOBAL" => Some(Self::Global),

            "MEMORY_OP_CLASS_LOCAL" => Some(Self::Local),
            "MEMORY_OP_CLASS_TEXTURE" => Some(Self::Texture),

/// Write-policy classification dimension orthogonal to
/// MemoryOpClass. MemoryOpClass tags the memory space (global,
/// shared, local, etc.); MemoryOpAccessKind tags the direction
/// (load, store, atomic / read-modify-write, async-copy). Together
/// the two enums let consumers distinguish write-allocate paths
/// (global / local / texture loads + stores; atomic; texture
/// loads) from no-write-allocate paths (shared, async-copy
/// destination side). The classifier is the producer's job: the
/// SASS opcode head determines which kind the access falls into.
/// New optional field at tag 12; legacy traces leave it absent,
/// and consumers fall back to UNSPECIFIED so the additive widening
/// is wire-compatible with pre-tag-12 readers.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, ::prost::Enumeration)]
#[repr(i32)]
pub enum MemoryOpAccessKind {
    Unspecified = 0,
    Load = 1,
    Store = 2,
    Atomic = 3,
    AsyncCopy = 4,
}

            Self::Load => "MEMORY_OP_ACCESS_KIND_LOAD",
            Self::Store => "MEMORY_OP_ACCESS_KIND_STORE",
            Self::Atomic => "MEMORY_OP_ACCESS_KIND_ATOMIC",
            Self::AsyncCopy => "MEMORY_OP_ACCESS_KIND_ASYNC_COPY",
        }

    /// address-carrying contract transition (additive, per the CLAUDE.md wire-
    /// extension policy). `trace_contract_id` names the emitted contract so an
    /// old exclusion-semantics trace (field absent/empty) is never silently
    /// cross-compared with a new address-carrying one. `memory_payload_classes`
    /// lists the MemoryOpClass values for which this trace emits address records
    /// under the contract (e.g. \[GLOBAL, SHARED, LOCAL, ATOMIC, ASYNC_COPY\] post-
    /// flip); its ABSENCE is the legacy signal the consumer identity gates use to
    /// skip the widened ATOMIC/ASYNC enforcement on pre-transition traces.
    #[prost(string, tag = "7")]
    pub trace_contract_id: ::prost::alloc::string::String,
    #[prost(enumeration = "MemoryOpClass", repeated, tag = "8")]
    pub memory_payload_classes: ::prost::alloc::vec::Vec<i32>,
}
```

```rust
//! Committed-gencode drift guard.
//!
//! sim/trace/src/pb/dynamic_trace.rs is COMMITTED (generated by
//! `sim/trace/regen_pb.sh` with the pinned protoc). This test pins an
//! FNV-1a-64 hash of every .proto input so a schema change that lands
//! WITHOUT regenerating + committing the Rust bindings fails loudly in
//! `cargo test` instead of silently skewing the wire format.
//!
//! On failure: run `sim/trace/regen_pb.sh`, commit the regenerated
//! `dynamic_trace.rs`, and update the pins below — all in the SAME commit
//! as the .proto change (multi-surface lockstep rule).

use std::path::PathBuf;

const PROTO_PINS: &[(&str, u64)] = &[
    ("address.proto", 0xb768cd17c42a1788),
    ("cuda_stream.proto", 0xad1565c52bd75656),
    ("dim3d.proto", 0x13d2f3d8144e1420),
    ("gpu_device.proto", 0x456a3472a1018842),
    ("instruction.proto", 0xa387ffa3c65bcb44),
    ("kernel.proto", 0x2d6ee7fc080ec4ad),
    ("threadblock.proto", 0x0424145b630ec29a),
    ("trace.proto", 0xc7577e6647181017),
    ("warp.proto", 0xf6568d1a9c8bdf7b),
];

fn fnv1a64(bytes: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    let mut h: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
    for &b in bytes {
        h ^= u64::from(b);
        h = h.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01b3);
    }
    h
}

fn proto_dir() -> PathBuf {
    PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
        .join("../../tools/nvbit_tracer/traces_enhanced/dynamic_trace")
        .canonicalize()
        .expect("proto schema dir exists in-repo")
}

#[test]
fn committed_gencode_matches_proto_schema() {
    let dir = proto_dir();
    let mut mismatches = Vec::new();
    for (name, pin) in PROTO_PINS {
        let bytes = std::fs::read(dir.join(name))
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{name}: {e} — .proto removed without updating the pins?"));
        let got = fnv1a64(&bytes);
        if got != *pin {
            mismatches.push(format!("{name}: pinned {pin:#018x}, on-disk {got:#018x}"));
        }
    }
    assert!(
        mismatches.is_empty(),
        ".proto schema changed without regenerating the committed Rust bindings.\n\
         Run sim/trace/regen_pb.sh, commit dynamic_trace.rs, and update PROTO_PINS \
         in the SAME commit:\n{}",
        mismatches.join("\n")
    );
}

/// A NEW .proto added upstream must also be added to the pins (and to the
/// generated bindings) — enumeration catches silent omission.
#[test]
fn no_unpinned_proto_files() {
    let dir = proto_dir();
    let mut on_disk: Vec<String> = std::fs::read_dir(&dir)
        .expect("read proto dir")
        .filter_map(|e| e.ok())
        .map(|e| e.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned())
        .filter(|n| n.ends_with(".proto"))
        .collect();
    on_disk.sort();
    let mut pinned: Vec<String> = PROTO_PINS.iter().map(|(n, _)| n.to_string()).collect();
    pinned.sort();
    assert_eq!(
        on_disk, pinned,
        "proto files on disk diverge from PROTO_PINS — regen + repin in the same commit"
    );
}
```
