```rust
//! Sectored L1 cache core — a lockstep port of the cache state machine in
//! `tools/cache_predictor/l1_warp_pool_walker.py` (`_access_once` +
//! `_apply_fills`), the model whose semantics the Phase-1 L1 predictor
//! validated. The Python module's warp-pool SCHEDULER is deliberately NOT
//! ported: it was a latency-proportional stand-in for warp interleaving,
//! and the sim's SM issue model provides the real interleaving (traced
//! placement + control-bits timing). This module is only the cache.
//!
//! Ported semantics (two-layer, 32 B sector / 128 B line):
//! - hit decision is sector-with-line-allocation: a hit needs the LINE
//!   resident in the (fully-associative, LRU) line pool AND the touched
//!   SECTOR already fetched into it;
//! - two distinguishable in-flight fill kinds, both consuming MSHR
//!   capacity: line-ALLOCATION fills keyed by line (any access to the line
//!   meanwhile MERGES by line — counts as a miss, ready at the fill, and
//!   the fill services every sector the merged accesses touched), and
//!   resident-line SECTOR fills keyed by (line, sector) (only the SAME
//!   missing sector merges; the line's other resident sectors still HIT);
//! - fills apply lazily in CHRONOLOGICAL order (line before sector only at
//!   exactly equal timestamps; same-kind ties in issue order): an in-flight
//!   line is not in the LRU until its fill time, and a sector fill whose
//!   line was evicted mid-flight is DROPPED (sector residency dies with
//!   the line);
//! - when every MSHR entry is busy the access STALLS and retries when the
//!   earliest fill (of either kind) frees an entry;
//! - the miss stream splits into `line_alloc_misses` (fresh allocation +
//!   the eviction it forces) and `sector_resident_misses` (partial-line
//!   sector fetch); invariant: `misses == line_alloc + sector_resident +
//!   merges`.
//!
//! v0 EXTENSIONS beyond the ported model (kept in separate counters so the
//! ported semantics stay auditable): global-class STORE sectors are
//! hit-TESTED against the same state without allocating on miss (NCU's
//! unified `l1tex__t_sector_hit_rate.pct` counts store sectors; the L1 is
//! write-through no-allocate for global stores in this v0 hypothesis), and
//! bypass/untagged sector counting for the unified-denominator emission.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap};

pub const SECTOR_BYTES: u32 = 32;
pub const SECTORS_PER_LINE: u32 = 4;
pub const LINE_BYTES: u32 = SECTOR_BYTES * SECTORS_PER_LINE;

/// Configuration (card-resolved by `pchase_card`; latencies are integer
/// cycles — the caller ceils the card's fractional cycle values).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct L1Config {
    pub line_capacity: u64,
    /// `None` = unlimited (ablation only; the card/documented default is
    /// always finite in production).
    pub mshr_count: Option<u32>,
    pub hit_latency: u64,
    pub miss_latency: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum L1ConfigError {
    #[error("line_capacity must be positive")]
    CapacityZero,
    #[error("mshr_count must be positive when finite")]
    MshrZero,
    #[error("hit latency {hit} must be strictly below miss latency {miss}")]
    LatencyOrderInverted { hit: u64, miss: u64 },
}

/// Outcome of one eligible sector access (after any MSHR stall retries).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AccessOutcome {
    Hit,
    MissLineAlloc,
    MissSectorResident,
    Merge,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct L1Counters {
    /// Ported counters (modeled, manifest-eligible accesses only).
    pub hits: u64,
    pub misses: u64,
    pub merges: u64,
    pub stall_events: u64,
    pub line_fills: u64,
    pub line_alloc_misses: u64,
    pub sector_resident_misses: u64,
    /// Manifest-tagged ineligible sectors (the ported bypass counter).
    pub bypass_sectors: u64,
    /// Subset of `bypass_sectors` whose cache-op token is ATOM (the
    /// write-class bypass stream). Kept as a subset counter so the
    /// emission layer can fold the READ-class bypass stream (LDGSTS)
    /// into the global-load sector surface without pulling atomics in
    /// with it — NCU books those under op_atom/op_red, not op_ld.
    pub bypass_atom_sectors: u64,
    /// v0 extensions for the unified-denominator emission.
    pub untagged_sectors: u64,
    pub store_sectors: u64,
    pub store_hits: u64,
    /// §6.4 write-class rule at the L1 probe: store sectors whose LINE
    /// tag was resident regardless of the sector's valid bit (a
    /// superset of `store_hits`). Counted alongside — the sector-valid
    /// `store_hits` stays the v0 unified diagnostic until l1tex store
    /// accounting is scored against labels and one rule wins.
    pub store_tag_hits: u64,
}

impl L1Counters {
    pub fn add(&mut self, other: &L1Counters) {
        self.hits += other.hits;
        self.misses += other.misses;
        self.merges += other.merges;
        self.stall_events += other.stall_events;
        self.line_fills += other.line_fills;
        self.line_alloc_misses += other.line_alloc_misses;
        self.sector_resident_misses += other.sector_resident_misses;
        self.bypass_sectors += other.bypass_sectors;
        self.bypass_atom_sectors += other.bypass_atom_sectors;
        self.untagged_sectors += other.untagged_sectors;
        self.store_sectors += other.store_sectors;
        self.store_hits += other.store_hits;
        self.store_tag_hits += other.store_tag_hits;
    }
}

enum SingleOutcome {
    Done(AccessOutcome, u64),
    Stall { retry_at: u64 },
}

/// The one shared classification result of [`L1Cache::access_core`];
/// each fill-timing mode maps it to its own public outcome type.
enum CoreAccess {
    Hit,
    /// Merged into an in-flight line allocation; `pending` is the
    /// entry's stored fill time (real in constant mode, the sentinel in
    /// event mode).
    LineMerge {
        pending: u64,
    },
    /// Merged into an in-flight same-sector fetch.
    SectorMerge {
        pending: u64,
    },
    Stalled,
    MissLineAlloc,
    MissSectorResident,
}

/// Which fill-timing discipline an [`L1Cache`] instance runs under —
/// latched on first use so the two families can never mix on one
/// instance (they share the in-flight entry maps).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum FillTiming {
    /// Fill times known at issue (`now + miss_latency`), applied lazily.
    Constant,
    /// Fill times decided by the next level; entries carry `u64::MAX`
    /// until [`L1Cache::complete_fill`].
    Event,
}

/// Identifies one in-flight fill for the event-driven mode: the key the
/// next level's RESPONSE must complete. Line-allocation fills are keyed
/// by line; resident-sector fills by (line, sector) — the same two MSHR
/// kinds as the constant-latency mode.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum FillKey {
    Line(i64),
    Sector(i64, u8),
}

/// Outcome of one eligible sector access in EVENT mode: fill times are
/// unknown at issue (the shared L2 decides them), so misses surface as
/// requests and the caller wires completions back via [`L1Cache::complete_fill`].
/// The fill request fetches the ACCESSED 32 B sector; sectors that merge
/// into an outstanding line allocation are delivered to the L2 exactly
/// once per fill BY THE CALLER (the §6.4 slice-2 machinery in sim-sm:
/// same-batch merges fold into the fill request's sector mask, later
/// merges send one follow-up fetch — the pre-slice-2 undercount is
/// FIXED there, not here). The ported L1 still installs the whole
/// merged mask at one fill event.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EvAccess {
    /// Sector hit: data ready at a known time.
    Hit { ready: u64 },
    /// Fresh miss: send one request to the next level; the response must
    /// call [`L1Cache::complete_fill`] with this key.
    MissRequest { fill: FillKey },
    /// Merged into an ALREADY outstanding fill: no new request; the
    /// merging warp waits on the same key's completion.
    MergedPending { fill: FillKey },
    /// Every MSHR entry is busy: the caller parks the access and retries
    /// after the next completion frees an entry (the event-mode analogue
    /// of the constant mode's retry-at-earliest-fill).
    Stalled,
}

pub struct L1Cache {
    cfg: L1Config,
    /// Fully-associative LRU line pool: monotonic recency stamps.
    by_stamp: BTreeMap<u64, i64>,
    stamp_of: HashMap<i64, u64>,
    next_stamp: u64,
    /// Per-line fetched-sector bitmask (bit = sector index in line, 0..4).
    /// Also accumulates for in-flight line allocations (the fill services
    /// every merged sector).
    sectors: HashMap<i64, u8>,
    /// In-flight fills: value = (fill_time, issue_seq) — the seq keeps
    /// same-timestamp same-kind fills in issue order like the Python
    /// stable sort.
    line_fills: HashMap<i64, (u64, u64)>,
    sector_fills: HashMap<(i64, u8), (u64, u64)>,
    fill_seq: u64,
    /// Lower bound on the earliest in-flight fill time: `apply_fills`
    /// early-outs when `now` has not reached it (the overwhelmingly
    /// common case on the hot path). Maintained as a min on insert and
    /// re-derived after applying.
    min_fill_due: u64,
    /// Latched fill-timing discipline (see [`FillTiming`]).
    fill_timing: Option<FillTiming>,
    pub counters: L1Counters,
}

impl L1Cache {
    pub fn new(cfg: L1Config) -> Result<Self, L1ConfigError> {
        if cfg.line_capacity == 0 {
            return Err(L1ConfigError::CapacityZero);
        }
        if cfg.mshr_count == Some(0) {
            return Err(L1ConfigError::MshrZero);
        }
        if cfg.hit_latency >= cfg.miss_latency {
            return Err(L1ConfigError::LatencyOrderInverted {
                hit: cfg.hit_latency,
                miss: cfg.miss_latency,
            });
        }
        Ok(Self {
            cfg,
            by_stamp: BTreeMap::new(),
            stamp_of: HashMap::new(),
            next_stamp: 0,
            sectors: HashMap::new(),
            line_fills: HashMap::new(),
            sector_fills: HashMap::new(),
            fill_seq: 0,
            min_fill_due: u64::MAX,
            fill_timing: None,
            counters: L1Counters::default(),
        })
    }

    fn mshr_in_use(&self) -> usize {
        self.line_fills.len() + self.sector_fills.len()
    }

    fn earliest_fill(&self) -> u64 {
        self.line_fills
            .values()
            .chain(self.sector_fills.values())
            .map(|&(t, _)| t)
            .min()
            .expect("earliest_fill called with fills in flight")
    }

    fn touch_mru(&mut self, line: i64) {
        if let Some(old) = self.stamp_of.remove(&line) {
            self.by_stamp.remove(&old);
        }
        let stamp = self.next_stamp;
        self.next_stamp += 1;
        self.by_stamp.insert(stamp, line);
        self.stamp_of.insert(line, stamp);
    }

    fn evict_beyond_capacity(&mut self) {
        while self.by_stamp.len() as u64 > self.cfg.line_capacity {
            let (&stamp, &line) = self
                .by_stamp
                .first_key_value()
                .expect("non-empty by capacity check");
            self.by_stamp.remove(&stamp);
            self.stamp_of.remove(&line);
            // Partial-line eviction: sector residency dies with the line.
            self.sectors.remove(&line);
        }
    }

    fn line_resident(&self, line: i64) -> bool {
        self.stamp_of.contains_key(&line)
    }

    /// Replay due fills in CHRONOLOGICAL order; each fill's effect is
    /// decided by the cache state AT ITS OWN FILL TIME (line-before-sector
    /// only at exactly equal timestamps; same-kind ties in issue order).
    ///
    /// Integer-time note (deliberate divergence from the float-timed
    /// Python walker): the sim's clock is integer cycles, so fills whose
    /// float times would differ inside one cycle land on the same
    /// integer timestamp and resolve by the (kind, issue-order) tie rule
    /// instead of sub-cycle chronology. Bit-parity with Python holds
    /// whenever both sides run integer latencies (proven by the gate's
    /// differential); fractional-latency sub-cycle ordering is below the
    /// engine's resolution by design.
    fn apply_fills(&mut self, now: u64) {
        if now < self.min_fill_due {
            return;
        }
        let mut due: Vec<(u64, u8, u64, i64, u8)> = Vec::new();
        for (&line, &(t, seq)) in &self.line_fills {
            if t <= now {
                due.push((t, 0, seq, line, 0));
            }
        }
        for (&(line, sector), &(t, seq)) in &self.sector_fills {
            if t <= now {
                due.push((t, 1, seq, line, sector));
            }
        }
        due.sort_unstable();
        for (_, kind, _, line, sector) in due {
            if kind == 0 {
                self.line_fills.remove(&line);
                self.touch_mru(line);
                self.evict_beyond_capacity();
            } else {
                self.sector_fills.remove(&(line, sector));
                if self.line_resident(line) {
                    // The sector arrives into its (still-resident) line
                    // and re-references it at MRU.
                    *self.sectors.entry(line).or_default() |= 1 << sector;
                    self.touch_mru(line);
                }
                // else: the line was evicted before this fill's own
                // timestamp — the fill is DROPPED.
            }
        }
        self.min_fill_due = self
            .line_fills
            .values()
            .chain(self.sector_fills.values())
            .map(|&(t, _)| t)
            .min()
            .unwrap_or(u64::MAX);
    }

    /// One classification/state step shared by BOTH fill-timing modes —
    /// the single copy of the ported ladder (line-merge → sector-present
    /// hit → sector-merge → MSHR stall → fresh miss), with all counter
    /// accounting inside. `fill_time` is the timestamp a fresh miss's
    /// in-flight entry carries: `now + miss_latency` in constant mode,
    /// the `u64::MAX` sentinel in event mode (the lazy applier ignores
    /// it; `complete_fill` installs at the response event).
    fn access_core(&mut self, sector_id: i64, fill_time: u64) -> CoreAccess {
        let line = sector_id >> 2;
        let sector = (sector_id & 3) as u8;
        if let Some(&(pending, _)) = self.line_fills.get(&line) {
            // Access while the line ALLOCATION is in flight: MERGE by line
            // (the fill will install every merged sector).
            self.counters.merges += 1;
            self.counters.misses += 1;
            *self.sectors.entry(line).or_default() |= 1 << sector;
            return CoreAccess::LineMerge { pending };
        }
        let line_resident = self.line_resident(line);
        // Sector-present HIT testing precedes sector-merge handling.
        let sector_present = line_resident
            && self
                .sectors
                .get(&line)
                .is_some_and(|mask| mask & (1 << sector) != 0);
        if sector_present {
            self.counters.hits += 1;
            self.touch_mru(line);
            return CoreAccess::Hit;
        }
        if line_resident && let Some(&(pending, _)) = self.sector_fills.get(&(line, sector)) {
            // The SAME missing sector is already being fetched: MERGE.
            self.counters.merges += 1;
            self.counters.misses += 1;
            return CoreAccess::SectorMerge { pending };
        }
        // Miss path: needs an MSHR entry (both fill kinds consume capacity).
        if let Some(cap) = self.cfg.mshr_count
            && self.mshr_in_use() >= cap as usize
        {
            self.counters.stall_events += 1;
            return CoreAccess::Stalled;
        }
        self.counters.misses += 1;
        let seq = self.fill_seq;
        self.fill_seq += 1;
        self.min_fill_due = self.min_fill_due.min(fill_time);
        if line_resident {
            // Partial-line sector fetch: no allocation, no eviction; the
            // sector becomes resident at its FILL time (lazy).
            self.counters.sector_resident_misses += 1;
            self.sector_fills.insert((line, sector), (fill_time, seq));
            CoreAccess::MissSectorResident
        } else {
            self.counters.line_alloc_misses += 1;
            self.counters.line_fills += 1;
            self.line_fills.insert(line, (fill_time, seq));
            *self.sectors.entry(line).or_default() |= 1 << sector;
            CoreAccess::MissLineAlloc
        }
    }

    /// Latch the instance to one fill-timing mode on first use; mixing
    /// modes is a programming error (constant-mode entries carry real
    /// times the event mode would complete out of order, and event-mode
    /// sentinels would send the constant retry loop to `u64::MAX`).
    fn latch(&mut self, mode: FillTiming) {
        match self.fill_timing {
            None => self.fill_timing = Some(mode),
            Some(latched) => assert!(
                latched == mode,
                "L1Cache fill-timing modes must not mix on one instance \
                 (latched {latched:?}, called {mode:?})"
            ),
        }
    }

    fn access_single(&mut self, sector_id: i64, now: u64) -> SingleOutcome {
        self.apply_fills(now);
        let fill_time = now + self.cfg.miss_latency;
        match self.access_core(sector_id, fill_time) {
            CoreAccess::Hit => SingleOutcome::Done(AccessOutcome::Hit, now + self.cfg.hit_latency),
            CoreAccess::LineMerge { pending } | CoreAccess::SectorMerge { pending } => {
                SingleOutcome::Done(AccessOutcome::Merge, pending)
            }
            CoreAccess::Stalled => SingleOutcome::Stall {
                retry_at: self.earliest_fill(),
            },
            CoreAccess::MissSectorResident => {
                SingleOutcome::Done(AccessOutcome::MissSectorResident, fill_time)
            }
            CoreAccess::MissLineAlloc => {
                SingleOutcome::Done(AccessOutcome::MissLineAlloc, fill_time)
            }
        }
    }

    /// One modeled (manifest-eligible) sector access at time `now`.
    /// MSHR stalls retry internally at the earliest fill time (the ported
    /// walker's retry contract). Returns the outcome and the data-ready
    /// time.
    pub fn access_eligible(&mut self, sector_id: i64, now: u64) -> (AccessOutcome, u64) {
        self.latch(FillTiming::Constant);
        let mut t = now;
        loop {
            match self.access_single(sector_id, t) {
                SingleOutcome::Done(outcome, ready) => return (outcome, ready),
                SingleOutcome::Stall { retry_at } => t = retry_at.max(t + 1),
            }
        }
    }

    /// One modeled sector access in EVENT mode (shared-L2 integration):
    /// the fill time is decided by the next level, so misses register an
    /// UNTIMED in-flight entry (sentinel time `u64::MAX` — the lazy
    /// applier never applies it; [`Self::complete_fill`] installs it at
    /// the response event). Hit/miss/merge accounting matches
    /// [`Self::access_eligible`]; `stall_events` does NOT — the constant
    /// mode's internal retry-at-earliest-fill always succeeds (one stall
    /// per stalled access), while event-mode parking re-counts a stall
    /// on every failed re-attempt after a completion, so `stall_events`
    /// reads "stall ATTEMPTS" in this mode (deliberate: the retry
    /// discipline is the caller's, and no emitted metric consumes the
    /// counter yet).
    ///
    /// The two modes must not be mixed on one cache instance: constant-
    /// mode entries carry real times the event mode would complete out
    /// of order.
    pub fn access_eligible_ev(&mut self, sector_id: i64, now: u64) -> EvAccess {
        self.latch(FillTiming::Event);
        let line = sector_id >> 2;
        let sector = (sector_id & 3) as u8;
        match self.access_core(sector_id, u64::MAX) {
            CoreAccess::Hit => EvAccess::Hit {
                ready: now + self.cfg.hit_latency,
            },
            CoreAccess::LineMerge { .. } => EvAccess::MergedPending {
                fill: FillKey::Line(line),
            },
            CoreAccess::SectorMerge { .. } => EvAccess::MergedPending {
                fill: FillKey::Sector(line, sector),
            },
            CoreAccess::Stalled => EvAccess::Stalled,
            CoreAccess::MissSectorResident => EvAccess::MissRequest {
                fill: FillKey::Sector(line, sector),
            },
            CoreAccess::MissLineAlloc => EvAccess::MissRequest {
                fill: FillKey::Line(line),
            },
        }
    }

    /// Complete an event-mode fill AT the response event's time. A
    /// sector fill whose line was evicted while it was in flight is
    /// DROPPED, like the lazy applier; returns whether the fill
    /// installed.
    ///
    /// Deliberate divergence from the constant path: `apply_fills`
    /// breaks SAME-TIMESTAMP ties line-before-sector (a batch-applier
    /// artifact the Python lockstep pins), while event mode completes
    /// same-cycle fills in response order — under eviction pressure the
    /// two orders can pick different LRU victims. Sub-cycle completion
    /// order is below the model's resolution either way; the event
    /// order is the shared-L2 system's single source of truth.
    pub fn complete_fill(&mut self, fill: FillKey) -> bool {
        self.latch(FillTiming::Event);
        match fill {
            FillKey::Line(line) => {
                self.line_fills
                    .remove(&line)
                    .expect("completion for a line fill that is not in flight");
                self.touch_mru(line);
                self.evict_beyond_capacity();
                true
            }
            FillKey::Sector(line, sector) => {
                self.sector_fills
                    .remove(&(line, sector))
                    .expect("completion for a sector fill that is not in flight");
                if self.line_resident(line) {
                    *self.sectors.entry(line).or_default() |= 1 << sector;
                    self.touch_mru(line);
                    true
                } else {
                    false
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// v0 extension: hit-TEST a global-class store sector against the
    /// current state without allocating on miss (write-through
    /// no-allocate hypothesis). A store hit re-references the line.
    /// Counts BOTH candidate hit rules — sector-valid (`store_hits`,
    /// the ported-era diagnostic) and the §6.4 write-class line-TAG
    /// rule (`store_tag_hits`) — without changing state behavior (MRU
    /// touch stays on the sector-valid hit only, preserving the L1
    /// state trajectory the scored op_ld exactness was proven on).
    pub fn probe_store(&mut self, sector_id: i64, now: u64) -> bool {
        let line = sector_id >> 2;
        let sector = (sector_id & 3) as u8;
        self.apply_fills(now);
        self.counters.store_sectors += 1;
        let tag_resident = self.line_resident(line);
        if tag_resident {
            self.counters.store_tag_hits += 1;
        }
        let hit = tag_resident
            && self
                .sectors
                .get(&line)
                .is_some_and(|mask| mask & (1 << sector) != 0);
        if hit {
            self.counters.store_hits += 1;
            self.touch_mru(line);
        }
        hit
    }

    /// Manifest-tagged ineligible sectors (the ported bypass counter).
    /// `atom` marks the write-class (ATOM-token) subset — the caller
    /// owns the token, this cache never sees opcodes.
    pub fn count_bypass(&mut self, sectors: u64, atom: bool) {
        self.counters.bypass_sectors += sectors;
        if atom {
            self.counters.bypass_atom_sectors += sectors;
        }
    }

    /// Global-class sectors whose pc the classifier did not tag (v0
    /// unified-denominator extension).
    pub fn count_untagged(&mut self, sectors: u64) {
        self.counters.untagged_sectors += sectors;
    }
}

/// Expand one traced address record's lane vector into UNIQUE global
/// sector ids, in first-seen order (lane-major, ascending sector within a
/// lane) — the `l1_trace_adapter` dedup contract: NCU's sector metric
/// counts unique 32 B sectors per warp INSTRUCTION, and emission order
/// feeds the LRU, so both the SET and the ORDER are ported. `dedup_from`
/// marks where the current instruction's sectors begin in `out`, so a
/// multi-address-record instruction dedups across ALL its records.
pub fn push_unique_sectors(
    lane_vector: &[i64; 32],
    active_lanes: impl Iterator<Item = usize>,
    data_width_bytes: i32,
    out: &mut Vec<i64>,
    dedup_from: usize,
) {
    let width = i64::from(data_width_bytes.max(1));
    for lane in active_lanes {
        let base = lane_vector[lane];
        let first = base >> 5;
        let last = (base + width - 1) >> 5;
        for sector in first..=last {
            if !out[dedup_from..].contains(&sector) {
                out.push(sector);
            }
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
#[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn cache(capacity: u64, mshr: Option<u32>) -> L1Cache {
        L1Cache::new(L1Config {
            line_capacity: capacity,
            mshr_count: mshr,
            hit_latency: 34,
            miss_latency: 244,
        })
        .unwrap()
    }

    fn counters_invariant(c: &L1Counters) {
        assert_eq!(
            c.misses,
            c.line_alloc_misses + c.sector_resident_misses + c.merges,
            "miss == line_alloc + sector_resident + merge"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn sector_with_line_allocation_hit_decision() {
        let mut l1 = cache(8, None);
        // Sector 0 of line 0: line-alloc miss; fills at t=244.
        let (o, ready) = l1.access_eligible(0, 0);
        assert_eq!(o, AccessOutcome::MissLineAlloc);
        assert_eq!(ready, 244);
        // After the fill: same sector hits, but sector 1 of the SAME
        // (now-resident) line is a sector-resident miss, not a hit.
        let (o, _) = l1.access_eligible(0, 300);
        assert_eq!(o, AccessOutcome::Hit);
        let (o, _) = l1.access_eligible(1, 300);
        assert_eq!(o, AccessOutcome::MissSectorResident);
        counters_invariant(&l1.counters);
    }

    #[test]
    fn line_merge_while_allocation_in_flight() {
        let mut l1 = cache(8, None);
        let (_, fill) = l1.access_eligible(0, 0);
        // Different sector of the same line while the allocation is in
        // flight: merge (counts as a miss), ready at the SAME fill time,
        // and the fill services the merged sector too.
        let (o, ready) = l1.access_eligible(1, 10);
        assert_eq!(o, AccessOutcome::Merge);
        assert_eq!(ready, fill);
        let (o, _) = l1.access_eligible(1, 250);
        assert_eq!(
            o,
            AccessOutcome::Hit,
            "merged sector serviced by the line fill"
        );
        counters_invariant(&l1.counters);
    }

    #[test]
    fn lazy_fill_is_not_a_hit_before_fill_time() {
        let mut l1 = cache(8, None);
        l1.access_eligible(0, 0);
        // Same sector before the fill time: merge, never an LRU hit.
        let (o, _) = l1.access_eligible(0, 100);
        assert_eq!(o, AccessOutcome::Merge);
    }

    #[test]
    fn same_missing_sector_on_resident_line_merges() {
        let mut l1 = cache(8, None);
        l1.access_eligible(0, 0);
        l1.apply_fills(244);
        // Sector 1 fetch in flight on the resident line...
        let (o, fill) = l1.access_eligible(1, 250);
        assert_eq!(o, AccessOutcome::MissSectorResident);
        // ...same sector merges; OTHER resident sector still hits.
        let (o, ready) = l1.access_eligible(1, 260);
        assert_eq!(o, AccessOutcome::Merge);
        assert_eq!(ready, fill);
        let (o, _) = l1.access_eligible(0, 260);
        assert_eq!(
            o,
            AccessOutcome::Hit,
            "sector fetch must not shadow its line"
        );
        counters_invariant(&l1.counters);
    }

    #[test]
    fn eviction_drops_sector_residency_and_inflight_sector_fill() {
        let mut l1 = cache(1, None);
        // Line 0 resident.
        l1.access_eligible(0, 0);
        l1.apply_fills(244);
        // Sector 1 of line 0 in flight (fills at 250+244=494)...
        l1.access_eligible(1, 250);
        // ...line 1 allocation evicts line 0 (capacity 1) at its own fill
        // time 251+244=495 > 494. The sector fill applies FIRST (chrono
        // order) into the still-resident line, then the line fill evicts.
        l1.access_eligible(4, 251);
        l1.apply_fills(1000);
        // Line 0 evicted: sector 0 must MISS as a fresh line allocation.
        let (o, _) = l1.access_eligible(0, 1000);
        assert_eq!(o, AccessOutcome::MissLineAlloc);
        counters_invariant(&l1.counters);
    }

    #[test]
    fn sector_fill_dropped_when_line_evicted_before_its_timestamp() {
        let mut l1 = cache(1, None);
        l1.access_eligible(0, 0); // line 0
        l1.apply_fills(244);
        // Line 1 alloc at t=245 → fills 489, evicting line 0 at 489.
        l1.access_eligible(4, 245);
        // Sector fetch into line 0 at t=246 → would fill at 490, AFTER
        // the eviction: must be dropped.
        let (o, _) = l1.access_eligible(1, 246);
        assert_eq!(o, AccessOutcome::MissSectorResident);
        l1.apply_fills(10_000);
        // Line 0 fully gone; re-access = fresh allocation, and the
        // dropped sector never resurrects.
        let (o, _) = l1.access_eligible(1, 10_000);
        assert_eq!(o, AccessOutcome::MissLineAlloc);
        counters_invariant(&l1.counters);
    }

    #[test]
    fn mshr_full_stalls_and_retries() {
        let mut l1 = cache(8, Some(1));
        let (_, fill) = l1.access_eligible(0, 0); // occupies the only MSHR
        // A different line at t=1 stalls until the fill frees the entry,
        // then misses: ready = fill_time + miss_latency.
        let (o, ready) = l1.access_eligible(8, 1);
        assert_eq!(o, AccessOutcome::MissLineAlloc);
        assert_eq!(ready, fill + 244);
        assert_eq!(l1.counters.stall_events, 1);
        counters_invariant(&l1.counters);
    }

    #[test]
    fn lru_eviction_order() {
        let mut l1 = cache(2, None);
        l1.access_eligible(0, 0); // line 0
        l1.access_eligible(4, 1); // line 1
        l1.apply_fills(300);
        l1.access_eligible(0, 300); // touch line 0 → MRU
        // Line 2 evicts the LRU line 1 (not line 0).
        l1.access_eligible(8, 301);
        l1.apply_fills(1000);
        let (o, _) = l1.access_eligible(0, 1000);
        assert_eq!(o, AccessOutcome::Hit);
        let (o, _) = l1.access_eligible(4, 1001);
        assert_eq!(o, AccessOutcome::MissLineAlloc);
        counters_invariant(&l1.counters);
    }

    #[test]
    fn store_probe_tests_without_allocating() {
        let mut l1 = cache(8, None);
        assert!(!l1.probe_store(0, 0), "cold store misses");
        // The store must NOT have allocated: a load still line-alloc
        // misses.
        let (o, _) = l1.access_eligible(0, 10);
        assert_eq!(o, AccessOutcome::MissLineAlloc);
        l1.apply_fills(300);
        assert!(l1.probe_store(0, 300), "store hits the resident sector");
        // A store to a DIFFERENT sector of the resident line: sector-
        // valid rule misses, §6.4 line-tag rule hits.
        assert!(!l1.probe_store(1, 300), "sector-valid rule still misses");
        assert_eq!(l1.counters.store_sectors, 3);
        assert_eq!(l1.counters.store_hits, 1);
        assert_eq!(
            l1.counters.store_tag_hits, 2,
            "tag rule counts the resident-line probes (both post-fill)"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn unique_sector_expansion_dedups_in_first_seen_order() {
        let mut lanes = [i64::MIN; 32];
        // 4 active lanes, 4B apart starting at 0: all in sector 0.
        for (i, l) in lanes.iter_mut().enumerate().take(4) {
            *l = (i * 4) as i64;
        }
        // Lane 4 crosses sectors 3→4 (base 127, width 4).
        lanes[4] = 127;
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        push_unique_sectors(&lanes, 0..5, 4, &mut out, 0);
        assert_eq!(out, vec![0, 3, 4]);
        // A second address record of the SAME instruction dedups against
        // the instruction's whole slice.
        push_unique_sectors(&lanes, 0..5, 4, &mut out, 0);
        assert_eq!(out, vec![0, 3, 4]);
    }

    #[test]
    #[should_panic(expected = "fill-timing modes must not mix")]
    fn mixing_fill_timing_modes_panics() {
        let mut l1 = cache(8, None);
        l1.access_eligible(0, 0); // latches Constant
        l1.access_eligible_ev(4, 1); // Event on the same instance: panic
    }

    #[test]
    fn ev_mode_miss_merge_completion_then_hit() {
        let mut l1 = cache(8, Some(4));
        // Fresh line miss → request keyed by line.
        let a = l1.access_eligible_ev(0, 0);
        assert_eq!(
            a,
            EvAccess::MissRequest {
                fill: FillKey::Line(0)
            }
        );
        // Another sector of the same line merges into the SAME fill.
        let b = l1.access_eligible_ev(1, 5);
        assert_eq!(
            b,
            EvAccess::MergedPending {
                fill: FillKey::Line(0)
            }
        );
        // Response installs line + both merged sectors; hits follow.
        assert!(l1.complete_fill(FillKey::Line(0)));
        assert!(matches!(
            l1.access_eligible_ev(0, 400),
            EvAccess::Hit { ready: 434 }
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            l1.access_eligible_ev(1, 400),
            EvAccess::Hit { .. }
        ));
        // Sector 2 on the now-resident line: sector-resident request, and
        // the same missing sector merges while in flight.
        assert_eq!(
            l1.access_eligible_ev(2, 401),
            EvAccess::MissRequest {
                fill: FillKey::Sector(0, 2)
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            l1.access_eligible_ev(2, 402),
            EvAccess::MergedPending {
                fill: FillKey::Sector(0, 2)
            }
        );
        assert!(l1.complete_fill(FillKey::Sector(0, 2)));
        assert!(matches!(
            l1.access_eligible_ev(2, 900),
            EvAccess::Hit { .. }
        ));
        assert_eq!(l1.counters.hits, 3);
        assert_eq!(l1.counters.misses, 4);
        assert_eq!(l1.counters.merges, 2);
        assert_eq!(l1.counters.line_alloc_misses, 1);
        assert_eq!(l1.counters.sector_resident_misses, 1);
        counters_invariant(&l1.counters);
    }

    #[test]
    fn ev_mode_sector_fill_dropped_when_line_evicted_in_flight() {
        let mut l1 = cache(1, None);
        l1.access_eligible_ev(0, 0); // line 0 alloc
        l1.complete_fill(FillKey::Line(0));
        // Sector fetch in flight on line 0...
        l1.access_eligible_ev(1, 10);
        // ...line 1 allocation completes first and evicts line 0
        // (capacity 1).
        l1.access_eligible_ev(4, 11);
        assert!(l1.complete_fill(FillKey::Line(1)));
        // The sector response then finds its line gone: DROPPED.
        assert!(!l1.complete_fill(FillKey::Sector(0, 1)));
        assert_eq!(
            l1.access_eligible_ev(1, 500),
            EvAccess::MissRequest {
                fill: FillKey::Line(0)
            },
            "dropped sector never resurrects; the line itself was evicted"
        );
        counters_invariant(&l1.counters);
    }

    #[test]
    fn ev_mode_mshr_full_stalls_until_completion_frees_an_entry() {
        let mut l1 = cache(8, Some(1));
        l1.access_eligible_ev(0, 0); // occupies the only MSHR
        assert_eq!(l1.access_eligible_ev(8, 1), EvAccess::Stalled);
        assert_eq!(l1.counters.stall_events, 1);
        l1.complete_fill(FillKey::Line(0));
        assert_eq!(
            l1.access_eligible_ev(8, 2),
            EvAccess::MissRequest {
                fill: FillKey::Line(2)
            }
        );
        counters_invariant(&l1.counters);
    }

    #[test]
    fn bypass_atom_subset_counter_tracks_only_the_atom_stream() {
        let mut l1 = cache(8, None);
        l1.count_bypass(3, false);
        l1.count_bypass(2, true);
        assert_eq!(l1.counters.bypass_sectors, 5);
        assert_eq!(l1.counters.bypass_atom_sectors, 2);
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Shared L2 slice model — a lockstep port of the sectored set-associative
//! replay core in `tools/cache_replay/sector_cache_replay.py`
//! (`replay_access_stream` + `_install_way`), the engine behind the
//! Phase-1 L2 predictor. Like the L1 port, only the CACHE STATE MACHINE
//! is taken: the Python module replayed a timeless trace-order stream,
//! while the sim drives this model with the globally (time, seq)-ordered
//! request stream the event engine produces — the ordering the flat
//! replay stood in for.
//!
//! Ported semantics (32 B sectors in 128 B lines) — these bullets
//! describe the READ class, the rule the Python engine implements; the
//! §6.4 [`L2OpClass::WriteAtomic`] class additionally hits on line-TAG
//! residency alone (same state trajectory, different counting — see
//! `L2OpClass`; the parity corpus pins the Read class only):
//! - a Read-class sector access HITS iff its line tag is resident in
//!   the addressed set AND that sector's valid bit is set;
//! - a resident line whose requested sector is not yet valid is a
//!   sector-fill miss for reads (the bit is set immediately — the
//!   Python replay is occupancy-only, fills are not in-flight at this
//!   level) and a tag-match HIT for writes/atomics;
//! - a non-resident line allocates a way, evicting per policy when the
//!   set is full (LRU / SRRIP 2-bit RRPV / deterministic BIP 1-in-32);
//! - slice/set addressing: `slice = hash(line_id)`,
//!   `set = (line_id // num_slices) % num_sets_per_slice`, with the six
//!   pre-registered slice-hash candidates ported bit-exactly.
//!
//! Rule 1 note: the Phase-1 calibrator SELECTED a config for sm_86 by
//! fitting against local NCU labels (capacity_scale, hash, policy). That
//! selection is a label-fitted artifact and is deliberately NOT consumed
//! here. The sim's geometry comes from the arch card's vendor-documented
//! `l2_geometry` (capacity, line/sector, slice count); associativity,
//! slice hash and replacement policy are DOCUMENTED-DEFAULT hypothesis
//! knobs below (same fail-closed pattern as the L1 MSHR default), to be
//! closed by microbenchmarks — never by label fits.
//!
//! MSHR/fill timing: v0 models L2 occupancy only (no L2-level MSHR or
//! in-flight fill state). The L1's MSHRs already bound the per-SM
//! outstanding stream, and the Python reference has no L2 fill model to
//! port — an L2 MSHR would be an uncarded invention at this point.

/// Number of 32 B sectors per 128 B line (fixed physical granularity;
/// the `u8` way masks below hold exactly these four bits).
pub const L2_SECTORS_PER_LINE: u32 = 4;

/// Documented-default L2 associativity (research gap on every card):
/// 16 ways is the Accel-Sim Ampere config family's value and the common
/// literature assumption for NVIDIA L2s; not microbenched on this
/// project's cards yet. Same contract as the L1 MSHR default: a
/// documented hypothesis knob, never a silent invention.
pub const DOCUMENTED_DEFAULT_L2_ASSOCIATIVITY: u32 = 16;

/// The six pre-registered slice-hash candidates, ported bit-exactly from
/// `SLICE_HASH_REGISTRY`. The card records only the slice COUNT
/// (vendor-documented); which hash the crossbar uses is a research gap.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SliceHash {
    /// Documented-default candidate (v0 approximation).
    LineMod,
    SectorMod,
    XorFolded,
    KnuthMult,
    ShiftMod,
    BitReverse,
}

/// Documented-default slice hash: plain line-interleaving. The Python
/// registry existed to CALIBRATE this unknown; v0 pins the simplest
/// candidate and records it as an approximation.
pub const DOCUMENTED_DEFAULT_L2_SLICE_HASH: SliceHash = SliceHash::LineMod;

impl SliceHash {
    /// `slice_id` for a 128 B line address. Lockstep with the Python
    /// registry functions, INCLUDING negative line ids: Python's `%` is
    /// floored (→ `rem_euclid`), `>>` on negatives is an arithmetic
    /// shift, and `& 0xFFFF…` of a negative yields its two's-complement
    /// low bits — all matched here so a wire-admitted negative address
    /// (a `base_delta` stream summing below zero is structurally legal)
    /// replays identically instead of wrapping through `u64`.
    /// Pinned-value tests below cover both signs.
    pub fn slice_of(self, line_id: i64, num_slices: u32) -> u32 {
        let n = i64::from(num_slices);
        let s = match self {
            SliceHash::LineMod => line_id.rem_euclid(n),
            // (line * 4) % n == ((line %e n) * 4) % n — overflow-free
            // and sign-correct under the euclidean remainder.
            SliceHash::SectorMod => {
                (line_id.rem_euclid(n) * i64::from(L2_SECTORS_PER_LINE)).rem_euclid(n)
            }
            SliceHash::XorFolded => (line_id ^ (line_id >> 5) ^ (line_id >> 11)).rem_euclid(n),
            // Knuth multiplicative hash masked to the low 32 bits — the
            // wrapping product's low bits equal Python's full-precision
            // product masked (two's complement, both signs).
            SliceHash::KnuthMult => {
                (line_id.wrapping_mul(2_654_435_761) & 0xFFFF_FFFF).rem_euclid(n)
            }
            SliceHash::ShiftMod => (line_id >> 1).rem_euclid(n),
            SliceHash::BitReverse => i64::from((line_id as u16).reverse_bits()).rem_euclid(n),
        };
        s as u32
    }
}

/// Replacement policy. LRU is the documented-default approximation (the
/// same status as the L1 pool's LRU); SRRIP/BIP are ported so the
/// lockstep differential covers the full Python surface and calibration
/// can flip the knob later without a re-port.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum L2Replacement {
    Lru,
    Srrip,
    Bip,
}

pub const DOCUMENTED_DEFAULT_L2_REPLACEMENT: L2Replacement = L2Replacement::Lru;

const SRRIP_RRPV_MAX: i64 = 3;
const SRRIP_INSERT_RRPV: i64 = 2;
const BIP_MRU_INSERT_PERIOD: u64 = 32;

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum L2ConfigError {
    #[error("capacity_bytes {capacity} must be >= line_bytes {line}")]
    CapacityBelowLine { capacity: u64, line: u32 },
    #[error(
        "line/sector geometry must be 128/32 (got line={line}, sector={sector}) — the way masks are 4-bit"
    )]
    UnsupportedGranularity { line: u32, sector: u32 },
    #[error("associativity must be >= 1")]
    AssociativityZero,
    #[error("num_slices must be >= 1")]
    SlicesZero,
    #[error(
        "arch {arch:?} has not reviewed the documented-default L2 knobs (assoc 16/LRU/line_mod \
         were reviewed for sm_86 only) — card the fields or extend the reviewed set deliberately"
    )]
    DefaultsUnreviewedForArch { arch: String },
    #[error(
        "card l2_geometry.policy is absent — the model write-allocates stores, and a card \
         without a measured policy must fail closed, never assume write-allocate"
    )]
    WritePolicyGap,
    #[error(
        "card l2_geometry.policy {policy:?} is not a write-allocate token this model implements"
    )]
    WritePolicyUnsupported { policy: String },
}

/// Arches whose documented-default L2 knobs (associativity 16, LRU,
/// line_mod) have been REVIEWED against available public evidence.
/// Same per-arch-set pattern as `cache_op::BARE_LDG_E_DEFAULTS_TO_CA`:
/// an unreviewed arch fails closed instead of inheriting another
/// arch's hypotheses (CLAUDE.md architecture-coupling discipline).
pub const L2_DEFAULTS_REVIEWED_ARCHES: [&str; 1] = ["sm_86"];

/// The one write policy the store path implements (stores allocate in
/// L2 like loads). Cards carrying anything else — or nothing — fail
/// closed at construction.
pub const L2_WRITE_ALLOCATE_POLICY: &str = "write_allocate_non_inclusive";

/// L2 geometry + policy. Construct via [`L2Config::from_carded_geometry`]
/// so the documented-default provenance is explicit at the call site.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct L2Config {
    pub capacity_bytes: u64,
    pub line_bytes: u32,
    pub sector_bytes: u32,
    pub num_slices: u32,
    pub associativity: u32,
    pub replacement: L2Replacement,
    pub slice_hash: SliceHash,
}

impl L2Config {
    /// Config from the arch card's vendor-documented `l2_geometry` block,
    /// with the three research-gap fields taking their DOCUMENTED
    /// defaults (associativity 16 / LRU / line-interleaved slices) —
    /// only on arches that have REVIEWED those defaults, and only when
    /// the card's write `policy` is one the store model implements
    /// (`None` is a typed gap per the sim-calib `L2Geometry.policy`
    /// contract, never an implicit write-allocate).
    pub fn from_carded_geometry(
        arch_token: &str,
        capacity_bytes: u64,
        line_bytes: u32,
        sector_bytes: u32,
        num_slices: u32,
        policy: Option<&str>,
    ) -> Result<Self, L2ConfigError> {
        if !L2_DEFAULTS_REVIEWED_ARCHES.contains(&arch_token) {
            return Err(L2ConfigError::DefaultsUnreviewedForArch {
                arch: arch_token.to_owned(),
            });
        }
        match policy {
            None => return Err(L2ConfigError::WritePolicyGap),
            Some(L2_WRITE_ALLOCATE_POLICY) => {}
            Some(other) => {
                return Err(L2ConfigError::WritePolicyUnsupported {
                    policy: other.to_owned(),
                });
            }
        }
        let cfg = Self {
            capacity_bytes,
            line_bytes,
            sector_bytes,
            num_slices,
            associativity: DOCUMENTED_DEFAULT_L2_ASSOCIATIVITY,
            replacement: DOCUMENTED_DEFAULT_L2_REPLACEMENT,
            slice_hash: DOCUMENTED_DEFAULT_L2_SLICE_HASH,
        };
        cfg.validate()?;
        Ok(cfg)
    }

    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), L2ConfigError> {
        if self.line_bytes != 128 || self.sector_bytes != 32 {
            return Err(L2ConfigError::UnsupportedGranularity {
                line: self.line_bytes,
                sector: self.sector_bytes,
            });
        }
        if self.capacity_bytes < u64::from(self.line_bytes) {
            return Err(L2ConfigError::CapacityBelowLine {
                capacity: self.capacity_bytes,
                line: self.line_bytes,
            });
        }
        if self.associativity == 0 {
            return Err(L2ConfigError::AssociativityZero);
        }
        if self.num_slices == 0 {
            return Err(L2ConfigError::SlicesZero);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// `max(1, capacity // line)` — Python `total_lines`.
    pub fn total_lines(&self) -> u64 {
        (self.capacity_bytes / u64::from(self.line_bytes)).max(1)
    }

    /// `max(1, max(1, total_lines // num_slices) // associativity)` —
    /// Python `num_sets_per_slice`.
    pub fn num_sets_per_slice(&self) -> u64 {
        (self.total_lines() / u64::from(self.num_slices))
            .max(1)
            .checked_div(u64::from(self.associativity))
            .expect("associativity validated nonzero")
            .max(1)
    }
}

/// Who put the sector on the L2 stream. PROVENANCE ONLY: carried on
/// requests for the system layer's emission observer — the cache model
/// itself never consumes it (gate-3 altitude note: emission accounting
/// lives OUTSIDE the models). The BEHAVIORAL per-access dimension is
/// [`L2OpClass`], carried separately: source is 4-way who-sent-it,
/// class is 2-way how-it-hits (an ATOM rides `Bypass` provenance with
/// `WriteAtomic` class).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum L2Source {
    /// An L1 fill request (line-allocation or resident-sector fetch).
    L1Fill,
    /// A manifest-ineligible load sector bypassing the L1 (.cg/.cs/…).
    Bypass,
    /// A global-class sector whose pc the classifier did not tag.
    Untagged,
    /// A global store sector (card policy `write_allocate_non_inclusive`
    /// → stores allocate in L2 exactly like loads).
    Store,
}

/// Behavioral ACCESS CLASS of one L2 sector access — the §6.4
/// per-access-class hit rule. NCU's `lts__t_sectors_lookup_hit`
/// accounting is hypothesized to be per-op-class (gate-3 error
/// attribution, validated on the histogram witness cell): a LOAD needs
/// the sector's DATA, so it hits only when the sector's valid bit is set
/// (the ported Python rule); a WRITE/ATOMIC/REDUCTION carries its own
/// data and coalesces into any resident line, so its lookup hits on
/// line-TAG residency alone. This is a COUNTING rule, not per-cell
/// tuning: the cache state trajectory is identical either way (a
/// write-class access to a resident line validates the sector exactly
/// as the sector-fill-miss path did).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum L2OpClass {
    /// Load-class sector (L1 fills, bypass loads, untagged, LDGSTS):
    /// hit iff the sector's valid bit is set.
    Read,
    /// Store/atomic/reduction sector (STG, RED, ATOM): hit iff the line
    /// TAG is resident, regardless of the sector's valid bit.
    WriteAtomic,
}

/// Outcome of one L2 sector access. `counted_hit` is the observation
/// (per-class NCU accounting, drives [`L2Counters`] and the driver's
/// emission observer); `sector_present` is the physics (the requested
/// sector's data was resident BEFORE this access — the response-pricing
/// arm: a tag-match write COUNTS as a hit but a dependent atomic reply
/// still fetches absent data from DRAM). For `Read` the two coincide.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct L2Outcome {
    pub counted_hit: bool,
    pub sector_present: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct L2Counters {
    pub hits: u64,
    pub misses: u64,
    /// Miss split (state-machine kinds, not the Python 3C diagnostic).
    pub line_misses: u64,
    pub sector_fill_misses: u64,
    /// Of `hits`: write-class hits granted on line-TAG residency while
    /// the sector's valid bit was still clear (the §6.4 rule's whole
    /// contribution — zero when every access is `Read`-class).
    pub write_tag_hits: u64,
}

impl L2Counters {
    pub fn add(&mut self, other: &L2Counters) {
        self.hits += other.hits;
        self.misses += other.misses;
        self.line_misses += other.line_misses;
        self.sector_fill_misses += other.sector_fill_misses;
        self.write_tag_hits += other.write_tag_hits;
    }

    pub fn total(&self) -> u64 {
        self.hits + self.misses
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct Way {
    /// Full line id as the tag (signed: negative wire-admitted ids
    /// replay with Python's floored semantics, never wrapped).
    tag: i64,
    /// Valid-sector bitmask (bit = sector index within the line, 0..4).
    mask: u8,
    /// LRU timestamp (LRU/BIP — BIP inserts can go BELOW the current
    /// minimum, hence signed) or RRPV (SRRIP).
    recency: i64,
}

/// The shared L2: one state machine partitioned into `num_slices ×
/// num_sets_per_slice` sets. Timeless by design — the caller (the event
/// system) presents accesses in the globally ordered request stream.
pub struct L2Model {
    cfg: L2Config,
    num_sets: u64,
    sets: Vec<Vec<Way>>,
    clock: i64,
    bip_counter: u64,
    pub counters: L2Counters,
}

impl L2Model {
    pub fn new(cfg: L2Config) -> Result<Self, L2ConfigError> {
        cfg.validate()?;
        let num_sets = cfg.num_sets_per_slice();
        let n = usize::try_from(u64::from(cfg.num_slices) * num_sets)
            .expect("set count fits usize on 64-bit targets");
        Ok(Self {
            cfg,
            num_sets,
            sets: vec![Vec::new(); n],
            clock: 0,
            bip_counter: 0,
            counters: L2Counters::default(),
        })
    }

    pub fn config(&self) -> &L2Config {
        &self.cfg
    }

    /// One 32 B sector access in global request order. `line_id` is the
    /// global 128 B line address (`sector_id >> 2` in the L1's sector-id
    /// space); negative ids (wire-admissible) take Python's floored
    /// division/remainder. The STATE trajectory is identical for both
    /// [`L2OpClass`]es — the class only changes how a resident-line /
    /// invalid-sector access is COUNTED (Read: sector-fill miss, the
    /// ported Python rule; WriteAtomic: tag-match hit).
    pub fn access(&mut self, line_id: i64, sector: u8, class: L2OpClass) -> L2Outcome {
        debug_assert!(sector < 4);
        let line = line_id;
        let sbit = 1u8 << sector;
        let slice = u64::from(self.cfg.slice_hash.slice_of(line, self.cfg.num_slices));
        let set_idx = line
            .div_euclid(i64::from(self.cfg.num_slices))
            .rem_euclid(self.num_sets as i64) as u64;
        let set_key = usize::try_from(slice * self.num_sets + set_idx)
            .expect("set key fits usize on 64-bit targets");
        self.clock += 1;

        let policy = self.cfg.replacement;
        let ways = &mut self.sets[set_key];
        if let Some(way) = ways.iter_mut().find(|w| w.tag == line) {
            let resident_hit = way.mask & sbit != 0;
            way.recency = match policy {
                L2Replacement::Srrip => 0,
                _ => self.clock,
            };
            if resident_hit {
                self.counters.hits += 1;
                return L2Outcome {
                    counted_hit: true,
                    sector_present: true,
                };
            }
            // Line resident, sector not yet valid: the write-class
            // access supplies its own data → tag-match hit; the read
            // needs the data → sector-fill miss. Both validate the bit.
            way.mask |= sbit;
            return match class {
                L2OpClass::WriteAtomic => {
                    self.counters.hits += 1;
                    self.counters.write_tag_hits += 1;
                    L2Outcome {
                        counted_hit: true,
                        sector_present: false,
                    }
                }
                L2OpClass::Read => {
                    self.counters.misses += 1;
                    self.counters.sector_fill_misses += 1;
                    L2Outcome {
                        counted_hit: false,
                        sector_present: false,
                    }
                }
            };
        }
        // Line miss → allocate (evicting per policy when the set is
        // full). A miss for BOTH classes: no tag to match.
        install_way(
            ways,
            line,
            sbit,
            self.cfg.associativity,
            policy,
            self.clock,
            self.bip_counter,
        );
        if policy == L2Replacement::Bip {
            self.bip_counter += 1;
        }
        self.counters.misses += 1;
        self.counters.line_misses += 1;
        L2Outcome {
            counted_hit: false,
            sector_present: false,
        }
    }
}

/// `_install_way` port: insert a freshly-fetched line, evicting per
/// policy when the set is full.
fn install_way(
    ways: &mut Vec<Way>,
    tag: i64,
    sbit: u8,
    assoc: u32,
    policy: L2Replacement,
    clock: i64,
    bip_counter: u64,
) {
    if ways.len() < assoc as usize {
        let recency = match policy {
            L2Replacement::Srrip => SRRIP_INSERT_RRPV,
            L2Replacement::Bip => {
                let mru = bip_counter.is_multiple_of(BIP_MRU_INSERT_PERIOD);
                if mru || ways.is_empty() {
                    clock
                } else {
                    min_recency(ways) - 1
                }
            }
            L2Replacement::Lru => clock,
        };
        ways.push(Way {
            tag,
            mask: sbit,
            recency,
        });
        return;
    }

    if policy == L2Replacement::Srrip {
        // Find a way at RRPV max; if none, age all until one reaches it.
        loop {
            if let Some(w) = ways.iter_mut().find(|w| w.recency >= SRRIP_RRPV_MAX) {
                *w = Way {
                    tag,
                    mask: sbit,
                    recency: SRRIP_INSERT_RRPV,
                };
                return;
            }
            for w in ways.iter_mut() {
                w.recency += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    // LRU / BIP eviction: least recency wins (first index on ties, like
    // the Python strict `<` scan).
    let victim = ways
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .min_by_key(|(ix, w)| (w.recency, *ix))
        .map(|(ix, _)| ix)
        .expect("set is full, hence non-empty");
    let recency = match policy {
        L2Replacement::Bip => {
            let mru = bip_counter.is_multiple_of(BIP_MRU_INSERT_PERIOD);
            if mru { clock } else { min_recency(ways) - 1 }
        }
        _ => clock,
    };
    ways[victim] = Way {
        tag,
        mask: sbit,
        recency,
    };
}

fn min_recency(ways: &[Way]) -> i64 {
    ways.iter()
        .map(|w| w.recency)
        .min()
        .expect("min_recency on non-empty ways")
}

#[cfg(test)]
#[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Read-class access sugar: the ported Python rule, where the
    /// counted hit and the physical sector presence coincide.
    fn rd(l2: &mut L2Model, line: i64, sector: u8) -> bool {
        l2.access(line, sector, L2OpClass::Read).counted_hit
    }

    /// Write-class access sugar (STG/RED/ATOM): counted hit under the
    /// §6.4 tag-match rule.
    fn wr(l2: &mut L2Model, line: i64, sector: u8) -> bool {
        l2.access(line, sector, L2OpClass::WriteAtomic).counted_hit
    }

    fn cfg(capacity: u64, assoc: u32, slices: u32) -> L2Config {
        L2Config {
            capacity_bytes: capacity,
            line_bytes: 128,
            sector_bytes: 32,
            num_slices: slices,
            associativity: assoc,
            replacement: L2Replacement::Lru,
            slice_hash: SliceHash::LineMod,
        }
    }

    /// Pinned against the Python registry (`SLICE_HASH_REGISTRY`) for
    /// lines {0, 1, 5, 12345, 987654321, 2^40+7, 2^56+123} at 6 and 7
    /// slices — regenerated verbatim from `sector_cache_replay.py`.
    #[test]
    fn slice_hashes_match_python_pins() {
        let lines: [i64; 7] = [0, 1, 5, 12345, 987_654_321, (1 << 40) + 7, (1 << 56) + 123];
        let cases: [(SliceHash, [u32; 7], [u32; 7]); 6] = [
            (
                SliceHash::LineMod,
                [0, 1, 5, 3, 3, 5, 1],
                [0, 1, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1],
            ),
            (
                SliceHash::SectorMod,
                [0, 4, 2, 0, 0, 2, 4],
                [0, 4, 6, 2, 5, 1, 4],
            ),
            (
                SliceHash::XorFolded,
                [0, 1, 5, 2, 5, 3, 2],
                [0, 1, 5, 1, 4, 3, 0],
            ),
            (
                SliceHash::KnuthMult,
                [0, 1, 5, 3, 3, 3, 5],
                [0, 5, 6, 3, 3, 5, 3],
            ),
            (
                SliceHash::ShiftMod,
                [0, 0, 2, 4, 4, 5, 3],
                [0, 0, 2, 5, 1, 4, 0],
            ),
            (
                SliceHash::BitReverse,
                [0, 2, 4, 0, 4, 2, 0],
                [0, 1, 3, 6, 5, 0, 6],
            ),
        ];
        for (hash, at6, at7) in cases {
            for (i, &line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
                assert_eq!(hash.slice_of(line, 6), at6[i], "{hash:?}({line}, 6)");
                assert_eq!(hash.slice_of(line, 7), at7[i], "{hash:?}({line}, 7)");
            }
        }
    }

    /// NEGATIVE line ids (wire-admissible via base_delta streams summing
    /// below zero) must replay with Python's floored semantics, never a
    /// u64 wrap — pins regenerated from `sector_cache_replay.py` for
    /// lines {-1, -93, -12345, -(2^40)-7}.
    #[test]
    fn negative_line_ids_match_python_floored_semantics() {
        let lines: [i64; 4] = [-1, -93, -12345, -(1 << 40) - 7];
        let cases: [(SliceHash, [u32; 4], [u32; 4]); 6] = [
            (SliceHash::LineMod, [5, 3, 3, 1], [6, 5, 3, 5]),
            (SliceHash::SectorMod, [2, 0, 0, 4], [3, 6, 5, 6]),
            (SliceHash::XorFolded, [5, 1, 2, 3], [6, 3, 4, 4]),
            (SliceHash::KnuthMult, [3, 1, 1, 1], [6, 5, 1, 6]),
            (SliceHash::ShiftMod, [5, 1, 1, 0], [6, 2, 1, 2]),
            (SliceHash::BitReverse, [3, 5, 5, 3], [1, 0, 3, 2]),
        ];
        for (hash, at6, at7) in cases {
            for (i, &line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
                assert_eq!(hash.slice_of(line, 6), at6[i], "{hash:?}({line}, 6)");
                assert_eq!(hash.slice_of(line, 7), at7[i], "{hash:?}({line}, 7)");
            }
        }
        // Set mapping floors too: Python (-93 // 6) % 512 == 496.
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(cfg(6_291_456, 16, 6)).unwrap();
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, -93, 1), "cold negative line");
        assert!(rd(&mut l2, -93, 1), "tagged and re-hit, no wrap");
    }

    /// Pinned against Python `CacheReplayConfig` derived properties.
    #[test]
    fn geometry_derivation_matches_python() {
        let c = cfg(6_291_456, 16, 6);
        assert_eq!(c.total_lines(), 49_152);
        assert_eq!(c.num_sets_per_slice(), 512);
        // Tiny degenerate config exercises both max(1, ·) clamps.
        let tiny = cfg(1024, 16, 6);
        assert_eq!(tiny.total_lines(), 8);
        assert_eq!(tiny.num_sets_per_slice(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn carded_constructor_applies_documented_defaults() {
        let policy = Some(L2_WRITE_ALLOCATE_POLICY);
        let c = L2Config::from_carded_geometry("sm_86", 6_291_456, 128, 32, 6, policy).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.associativity, DOCUMENTED_DEFAULT_L2_ASSOCIATIVITY);
        assert_eq!(c.replacement, L2Replacement::Lru);
        assert_eq!(c.slice_hash, SliceHash::LineMod);
        assert!(matches!(
            L2Config::from_carded_geometry("sm_86", 6_291_456, 256, 32, 6, policy),
            Err(L2ConfigError::UnsupportedGranularity { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            L2Config::from_carded_geometry("sm_86", 64, 128, 32, 6, policy),
            Err(L2ConfigError::CapacityBelowLine { .. })
        ));
    }

    /// Fail-closed gates on the carded constructor: an arch that never
    /// reviewed the documented defaults, and a card whose write policy
    /// is a gap (sm_120-laptop ships `policy: null`) or an unknown
    /// token, must all be typed errors — the store path write-allocates
    /// and must never assume it.
    #[test]
    fn carded_constructor_fails_closed_on_arch_and_policy() {
        let policy = Some(L2_WRITE_ALLOCATE_POLICY);
        assert!(matches!(
            L2Config::from_carded_geometry("sm_120", 33_554_432, 128, 32, 12, policy),
            Err(L2ConfigError::DefaultsUnreviewedForArch { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            L2Config::from_carded_geometry("sm_86", 6_291_456, 128, 32, 6, None),
            Err(L2ConfigError::WritePolicyGap)
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            L2Config::from_carded_geometry("sm_86", 6_291_456, 128, 32, 6, Some("write_back")),
            Err(L2ConfigError::WritePolicyUnsupported { .. })
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn sector_hit_requires_line_and_sector() {
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(cfg(1024, 2, 1)).unwrap();
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, 0, 0), "cold line miss");
        assert!(rd(&mut l2, 0, 0), "sector now valid");
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, 0, 1), "resident line, new sector");
        assert!(rd(&mut l2, 0, 1));
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.line_misses, 1);
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.sector_fill_misses, 1);
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.hits, 2);
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.total(), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn lru_evicts_least_recent_line() {
        // 1 slice, 1 set (capacity 256 B / 128 B line / assoc 2), LRU.
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(cfg(256, 2, 1)).unwrap();
        rd(&mut l2, 0, 0);
        rd(&mut l2, 1, 0);
        rd(&mut l2, 0, 0); // line 0 → MRU
        rd(&mut l2, 2, 0); // evicts line 1
        assert!(rd(&mut l2, 0, 0), "line 0 survived");
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, 1, 0), "line 1 was evicted");
    }

    #[test]
    fn eviction_drops_sector_residency_with_the_line() {
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(cfg(128, 1, 1)).unwrap();
        rd(&mut l2, 0, 0);
        rd(&mut l2, 0, 1);
        rd(&mut l2, 9, 0); // same set (1 set total) → evict
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, 0, 1), "sector died with the line");
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.line_misses, 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn set_mapping_matches_python_form() {
        // 1 slice, 2 sets, assoc 1 (capacity 256, line 128, assoc 1):
        // lines 0 and 2 share set 0; line 1 lives in set 1.
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(cfg(256, 1, 1)).unwrap();
        rd(&mut l2, 0, 0);
        rd(&mut l2, 1, 0);
        rd(&mut l2, 2, 0); // evicts line 0, not line 1
        assert!(rd(&mut l2, 1, 0), "set 1 undisturbed");
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, 0, 0), "conflict-evicted");
    }

    #[test]
    fn srrip_ages_and_reinserts_at_long_interval() {
        let mut c = cfg(256, 2, 1);
        c.replacement = L2Replacement::Srrip;
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(c).unwrap();
        rd(&mut l2, 0, 0); // insert rrpv=2
        rd(&mut l2, 2, 0); // insert rrpv=2 (same set)
        rd(&mut l2, 0, 0); // hit → rrpv=0
        // New line: no way at max → age all (0→1, 2→3), evict line 2.
        rd(&mut l2, 4, 0);
        assert!(rd(&mut l2, 0, 0), "recently-hit line survives");
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, 2, 0), "aged line evicted");
    }

    #[test]
    fn bip_inserts_below_lru_except_periodically() {
        let mut c = cfg(256, 2, 1);
        c.replacement = L2Replacement::Bip;
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(c).unwrap();
        // bip_counter=0 → first install at MRU; the next 31 at LRU-1.
        rd(&mut l2, 0, 0); // MRU insert (counter 0)
        rd(&mut l2, 2, 0); // below line 0 (counter 1)
        rd(&mut l2, 4, 0); // evicts line 2 (lowest recency)
        assert!(rd(&mut l2, 0, 0), "MRU-inserted line survives");
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, 2, 0), "LRU-inserted line evicted");
    }

    /// Cross-language lockstep corpus (BL-20260507 pattern): the SAME
    /// deterministic LCG streams, replayed through the canonical Python
    /// engine, produce these (hits, total) pins —
    /// `tools/cache_replay/test_l2_rust_parity.py` asserts the Python
    /// side AND that these rows exist here. Regenerate BOTH files in
    /// one commit.
    #[test]
    fn python_parity_corpus_pins() {
        // (policy, hash, seed, capacity, assoc, slices, n, line_space,
        //  signed, hits, total)
        type Row = (
            L2Replacement,
            SliceHash,
            u64,
            u64,
            u32,
            u32,
            u64,
            i64,
            bool,
            u64,
            u64,
        );
        #[rustfmt::skip]
        let corpus: [Row; 7] = [
            (L2Replacement::Lru, SliceHash::LineMod, 1, 16384, 4, 3, 500, 128, false, 159, 500),
            (L2Replacement::Lru, SliceHash::KnuthMult, 2, 16384, 4, 3, 500, 128, false, 164, 500),
            (L2Replacement::Srrip, SliceHash::XorFolded, 3, 16384, 4, 3, 500, 128, false, 150, 500),
            (L2Replacement::Srrip, SliceHash::BitReverse, 4, 4096, 2, 2, 500, 256, false, 6, 500),
            (L2Replacement::Bip, SliceHash::SectorMod, 5, 16384, 4, 3, 500, 128, false, 181, 500),
            (L2Replacement::Bip, SliceHash::ShiftMod, 6, 4096, 2, 2, 500, 256, false, 11, 500),
            (L2Replacement::Lru, SliceHash::LineMod, 7, 4096, 2, 3, 400, 96, true, 14, 400),
        ];
        for (policy, hash, seed, cap, assoc, slices, n, space, signed, hits, total) in corpus {
            let mut l2 = L2Model::new(L2Config {
                capacity_bytes: cap,
                line_bytes: 128,
                sector_bytes: 32,
                num_slices: slices,
                associativity: assoc,
                replacement: policy,
                slice_hash: hash,
            })
            .unwrap();
            let mut x: u64 = seed;
            for _ in 0..n {
                x = x
                    .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                    .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
                let mut line = ((x >> 20) % space as u64) as i64;
                if signed && (x & 1) == 1 {
                    line = -line;
                }
                rd(&mut l2, line, ((x >> 10) & 3) as u8);
            }
            assert_eq!(
                (l2.counters.hits, l2.counters.total()),
                (hits, total),
                "corpus row seed={seed} ({policy:?}, {hash:?})"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn stores_allocate_like_loads() {
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(cfg(1024, 2, 1)).unwrap();
        assert!(!wr(&mut l2, 3, 2), "cold store misses (no tag to match)");
        assert!(
            rd(&mut l2, 3, 2),
            "write-allocate: the store's line services a later load"
        );
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.line_misses, 1);
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.write_tag_hits, 0, "cold path grants no tag hit");
    }

    /// The §6.4 per-access-class rule: a write-class access to a
    /// RESIDENT line hits on the tag alone, even when the sector's
    /// valid bit is clear — and validates the sector (the write carries
    /// its own data), so a later read of that sector hits too. The same
    /// interleaving under Read class stays a sector-fill miss: the STATE
    /// trajectory is identical, only the counting differs.
    #[test]
    fn write_class_hits_on_tag_match_and_validates_the_sector() {
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(cfg(1024, 2, 1)).unwrap();
        assert!(!wr(&mut l2, 3, 0), "cold write line-misses");
        assert!(
            wr(&mut l2, 3, 2),
            "write to a NEW sector of the resident line: tag-match hit"
        );
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.write_tag_hits, 1);
        assert_eq!(
            l2.counters.sector_fill_misses, 0,
            "the tag-match hit is not double-counted as a fill miss"
        );
        assert!(
            rd(&mut l2, 3, 2),
            "the write validated the sector — a later read hits"
        );
        // Physics stays honest for pricing: a tag-match hit to a fresh
        // sector reports it ABSENT before the access (an atomic reply
        // would still fetch from DRAM), while a re-read finds it present.
        let out = l2.access(3, 3, L2OpClass::WriteAtomic);
        assert!(out.counted_hit && !out.sector_present);
        let out = l2.access(3, 3, L2OpClass::Read);
        assert!(out.counted_hit && out.sector_present);
        // Mirror stream under Read class: same state, different counts.
        let mut r = L2Model::new(cfg(1024, 2, 1)).unwrap();
        assert!(!rd(&mut r, 3, 0));
        assert!(!rd(&mut r, 3, 2), "read of the invalid sector fill-misses");
        assert_eq!(r.counters.sector_fill_misses, 1);
        assert_eq!(r.counters.write_tag_hits, 0);
        assert!(rd(&mut r, 3, 2));
    }

    /// Tag-match never crosses an eviction: once the line is gone the
    /// write-class access line-misses like everyone else.
    #[test]
    fn write_class_tag_hit_dies_with_the_line() {
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(cfg(128, 1, 1)).unwrap();
        assert!(!wr(&mut l2, 0, 0));
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, 9, 0), "same single set → evicts line 0");
        assert!(!wr(&mut l2, 0, 1), "no resident tag, no write hit");
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.write_tag_hits, 0);
    }
}
```
