```rust
//! sim-engine: the discrete-event core (design §6.1).
//!
//! v0 is a binary-heap min-queue over the current event tuple
//! `(time, seq, target, kind)` with a strict deterministic total order on
//! `(time, seq)`, where `seq` is the insertion sequence number. Payload data
//! belongs in the caller's typed `kind`; there is no separate FFI payload
//! handle. Two runs over the same inputs therefore produce bit-identical
//! schedules — a prerequisite for the M2 accuracy gates (a simulator whose
//! outputs wobble run-to-run cannot be compared against deterministic-class
//! NCU counts).
//!
//! The planned hybrid timing-wheel front-end and per-SM actor batching are
//! performance work layered behind this same API once profiles justify them
//! (throughput target 3–10 M events/s v0 → 10–30 M optimized).

use std::cmp::Reverse;
use std::collections::BinaryHeap;

/// Simulation time in cycles of the modeled clock domain.
pub type Time = u64;

/// Opaque component id (SM index, L2 slice index, DRAM channel, ...).
/// The engine never interprets it; dispatch tables live in the callers.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct TargetId(pub u32);

/// A scheduled event. `kind` is the caller's tagged enum (no virtual
/// dispatch on the hot path); the engine orders only by `(time, seq)`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Event<K> {
    pub time: Time,
    /// Insertion sequence number: unique, monotonically increasing, and the
    /// deterministic tie-breaker for same-cycle events (FIFO within a cycle).
    pub seq: u64,
    pub target: TargetId,
    pub kind: K,
}

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EngineError {
    #[error(
        "cannot schedule event at t={requested} — the clock already advanced to {now} (time travel would silently corrupt causality)"
    )]
    SchedulePast { requested: Time, now: Time },
    #[error("delay {delay} from now={now} overflows the u64 cycle domain")]
    TimeOverflow { now: Time, delay: Time },
}

/// Heap entry ordered by `(time, seq)` only; `kind` deliberately carries no
/// ordering obligation.
struct HeapEntry<K>(Event<K>);

impl<K> PartialEq for HeapEntry<K> {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.0.time == other.0.time && self.0.seq == other.0.seq
    }
}
impl<K> Eq for HeapEntry<K> {}
impl<K> PartialOrd for HeapEntry<K> {
    fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<std::cmp::Ordering> {
        Some(self.cmp(other))
    }
}
impl<K> Ord for HeapEntry<K> {
    fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> std::cmp::Ordering {
        (self.0.time, self.0.seq).cmp(&(other.0.time, other.0.seq))
    }
}

/// Deterministic discrete-event queue with pure next-event clock advance.
pub struct EventQueue<K> {
    heap: BinaryHeap<Reverse<HeapEntry<K>>>,
    now: Time,
    next_seq: u64,
}

impl<K> Default for EventQueue<K> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl<K> EventQueue<K> {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            heap: BinaryHeap::new(),
            now: 0,
            next_seq: 0,
        }
    }

    /// Current simulation time: the timestamp of the last popped event.
    pub fn now(&self) -> Time {
        self.now
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.heap.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.heap.is_empty()
    }

    /// Schedule at absolute time `at` (>= now, or a typed error).
    pub fn schedule_at(&mut self, at: Time, target: TargetId, kind: K) -> Result<u64, EngineError> {
        if at < self.now {
            return Err(EngineError::SchedulePast {
                requested: at,
                now: self.now,
            });
        }
        let seq = self.next_seq;
        self.next_seq += 1;
        self.heap.push(Reverse(HeapEntry(Event {
            time: at,
            seq,
            target,
            kind,
        })));
        Ok(seq)
    }

    /// Schedule `delay` cycles after the current time. Overflowing the
    /// cycle domain is a typed error, never a silent clamp.
    pub fn schedule_in(
        &mut self,
        delay: Time,
        target: TargetId,
        kind: K,
    ) -> Result<u64, EngineError> {
        let at = self
            .now
            .checked_add(delay)
            .ok_or(EngineError::TimeOverflow {
                now: self.now,
                delay,
            })?;
        self.schedule_at(at, target, kind)
    }

    /// Timestamp of the next event without popping it.
    pub fn peek_time(&self) -> Option<Time> {
        self.heap.peek().map(|Reverse(HeapEntry(e))| e.time)
    }

    /// Pop the next event and advance the clock to its timestamp.
    pub fn pop(&mut self) -> Option<Event<K>> {
        let Reverse(HeapEntry(event)) = self.heap.pop()?;
        debug_assert!(event.time >= self.now, "heap yielded an event in the past");
        self.now = event.time;
        Some(event)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
#[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)] // unwrap in tests is an assertion, not error handling
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
    enum Kind {
        IssueBatch,
        MemResponse,
        Drain,
    }

    #[test]
    fn orders_by_time_then_insertion_seq() {
        let mut q = EventQueue::new();
        q.schedule_at(10, TargetId(0), Kind::MemResponse).unwrap();
        q.schedule_at(5, TargetId(1), Kind::IssueBatch).unwrap();
        q.schedule_at(10, TargetId(2), Kind::IssueBatch).unwrap();
        q.schedule_at(5, TargetId(3), Kind::Drain).unwrap();

        let order: Vec<(Time, u32)> = std::iter::from_fn(|| q.pop())
            .map(|e| (e.time, e.target.0))
            .collect();
        // t=5 first (FIFO: target 1 before 3), then t=10 (FIFO: 0 before 2).
        assert_eq!(order, vec![(5, 1), (5, 3), (10, 0), (10, 2)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn same_cycle_fifo_is_stable_across_many_events() {
        let mut q = EventQueue::new();
        for i in 0..1000u32 {
            q.schedule_at(42, TargetId(i), Kind::IssueBatch).unwrap();
        }
        let targets: Vec<u32> = std::iter::from_fn(|| q.pop()).map(|e| e.target.0).collect();
        assert_eq!(targets, (0..1000).collect::<Vec<_>>());
    }

    #[test]
    fn clock_advances_monotonically_and_rejects_time_travel() {
        let mut q = EventQueue::new();
        q.schedule_at(100, TargetId(0), Kind::Drain).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(q.pop().unwrap().time, 100);
        assert_eq!(q.now(), 100);
        assert_eq!(
            q.schedule_at(99, TargetId(0), Kind::Drain),
            Err(EngineError::SchedulePast {
                requested: 99,
                now: 100
            })
        );
        // Scheduling exactly at `now` is legal (zero-latency follow-up).
        q.schedule_at(100, TargetId(0), Kind::IssueBatch).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(q.pop().unwrap().time, 100);
    }

    #[test]
    fn deterministic_against_reference_sort() {
        // Deterministic pseudo-random schedule (LCG — no external RNG dep,
        // and no wall-clock seeding: runs must be reproducible).
        let mut q = EventQueue::new();
        let mut expected: Vec<(Time, u64)> = Vec::new();
        let mut x: u64 = 0x2545_f491_4f6c_dd1d;
        for _ in 0..10_000 {
            x = x
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            let t = x >> 40; // ~24-bit times → plenty of same-time collisions
            let seq = q
                .schedule_at(t, TargetId((x & 0xff) as u32), Kind::MemResponse)
                .unwrap();
            expected.push((t, seq));
        }
        expected.sort();
        let popped: Vec<(Time, u64)> = std::iter::from_fn(|| q.pop())
            .map(|e| (e.time, e.seq))
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(popped, expected);
    }

    #[test]
    fn interleaved_schedule_and_pop() {
        let mut q = EventQueue::new();
        q.schedule_at(1, TargetId(0), Kind::IssueBatch).unwrap();
        q.schedule_at(3, TargetId(0), Kind::MemResponse).unwrap();
        let e = q.pop().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(e.time, 1);
        // React to the event by scheduling a follow-up before the t=3 one.
        q.schedule_in(1, TargetId(1), Kind::Drain).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            q.pop().unwrap(),
            Event {
                time: 2,
                seq: 2,
                target: TargetId(1),
                kind: Kind::Drain
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(q.pop().unwrap().time, 3);
        assert!(q.pop().is_none());
        assert_eq!(q.now(), 3);
    }
}
```

```rust
//! sim-emit: the NCU-metric emission layer (design §6.4).
//!
//! Takes a completed kernel replay's counter snapshot and produces a typed
//! vector of NCU metric PREDICTIONS, one per registry observation contract
//! (`tools/local_labels/metric_registry.json`). It is the ONLY sim crate that
//! names label-pipeline contracts: metric NAMES are the output contract and
//! are allowed here; label VALUES still never enter (Rule 1, enforced by
//! `eval/guards/test_targets_not_features_guard.py`).
//!
//! Shape (design proposal P3, "descriptor-table hybrid"): a compiled
//! [`DESCRIPTORS`] table is the single source of truth — one row per emitted
//! metric binds a registry key + NCU metric string + [`Unit`] + [`MetricKind`]
//! to a pure emit fn over the raw counters. A registry-lockstep test walks the
//! table against `metric_registry.json` so a descriptor can never drift from
//! the contract it claims to implement. Rate accounting lives HERE, never in
//! the cache counter structs (gate-2 altitude note c): `L1Counters`/
//! `L2Counters` hold raw counts; the emit fns compose them.
//!
//! Three states are kept distinct, never conflated into a silent zero:
//!   * a real zero — `Exact(0)` / `Fraction { value: Some(0.0), .. }`
//!     (accesses happened, none hit);
//!   * not-applicable — `Fraction { value: None, denominator: 0, .. }`
//!     (no accesses; NCU reports n/a — a legitimate scorable prediction);
//!   * not-produced-by-this-run — [`EmitOutcome::Unavailable`] (the replay's
//!     mem-mode lacks the counting unit, e.g. no L2 under `L1Const`).
//!
//! LDGSTS folding (the §6.4 op_ld surface): NCU books LDGSTS (cp.async) global
//! loads under `op_ld` on the frozen sm_86 bundle — verified against the
//! bundle's own captured counts, NOT the metric-name taxonomy (a witness
//! kernel with only LDGSTS loads and no ordinary loads shows all of its
//! `op_ld` requests attributed to the async copies, with the total-request
//! rollup balancing exactly against `op_ld` + `op_st`). So the op_ld surface
//! folds the READ-class bypass stream (`bypass_sectors - bypass_atom_sectors`,
//! the async-copy loads) into its denominator; the ATOM write-class subset
//! stays out (NCU books it under op_atom/op_red). The sim models LDGSTS as
//! pure bypass with no L1 residency, so those sectors contribute to the
//! denominator but never to the hit numerator — an honest v0 under-prediction
//! whose residual localizes the un-modeled LDGSTS-L1-residency effect.

use sim_mem::{L1Counters, L2Counters};
use sim_sm::{DramStats, KernelReplayResult};

/// The exact counter fields the emission layer reads, borrowed. Decouples
/// emission from the full `KernelReplayResult` so a cell's counters — summed
/// across its kernel launches — can be emitted directly (rates compose from
/// summed numerators/denominators; they cannot be averaged post-hoc).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct CounterSnapshot<'a> {
    /// `smsp__inst_executed.sum` source — total warp-instructions issued.
    pub instructions_issued: u64,
    /// L1TEX counters, present iff the replay attached an L1 (not `Flat`).
    pub l1: Option<&'a L1Counters>,
    /// L2 counters, present only on the shared-L2 path.
    pub l2: Option<&'a L2Counters>,
    /// DRAM read observer, present only on the shared-L2 path.
    pub dram: Option<&'a DramStats>,
}

impl<'a> CounterSnapshot<'a> {
    /// Borrow the emission-relevant counters out of one completed replay.
    pub fn from_replay(r: &'a KernelReplayResult) -> Self {
        Self {
            instructions_issued: r.instructions_issued,
            l1: r.l1.as_ref(),
            l2: r.l2.as_ref(),
            dram: r.dram.as_ref(),
        }
    }
}

/// A predicted metric value, shaped to its NCU contract. The numeric payload
/// carries num/den so a `None` rate is auditable in-band (None IFF den == 0).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub enum MetricValue {
    /// An exact non-negative integer count (sectors, requests, instructions).
    Exact(u64),
    /// A `[0, 1]` fraction. `value` is `None` iff `denominator == 0` (NCU
    /// reports the metric as n/a — never a fabricated 0.0).
    Fraction {
        value: Option<f64>,
        numerator: u64,
        denominator: u64,
    },
}

impl MetricValue {
    /// Fail-closed `[0, 1]` fraction constructor. `value` is `None` iff
    /// `den == 0`; a `num > den` fraction is a counter-arithmetic bug and is
    /// surfaced typed, never clamped into range.
    fn fraction(key: &'static str, num: u64, den: u64) -> Result<Self, EmitError> {
        if num > den {
            return Err(EmitError::RateExceedsUnity { key, num, den });
        }
        Ok(Self::Fraction {
            value: (den != 0).then(|| num as f64 / den as f64),
            numerator: num,
            denominator: den,
        })
    }
}

/// The NCU-facing unit of a metric (the registry `unit` field). Only the
/// variants v0 uses are declared; cycles/ns/ratio arrive with their metrics.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Unit {
    /// A raw non-negative count.
    Count,
    /// A percentage in NCU's own rendering; stored as a `[0, 1]` fraction
    /// (registry `parser_transform = percent_to_fraction`).
    Pct,
}

/// The numeric shape a descriptor promises to emit — asserted against the
/// returned [`MetricValue`] so a wrong-variant slip fails loudly, and pinned
/// against the registry `metric_class`/`valid_max` by the lockstep test.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MetricKind {
    /// Emits [`MetricValue::Exact`].
    Count,
    /// Emits [`MetricValue::Fraction`].
    Fraction,
}

/// A hardware counting unit a metric needs to be predictable at all.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MemUnit {
    /// The L1TEX cache (`KernelReplayResult.l1`).
    L1Tex,
    /// The L2 slices (`KernelReplayResult.l2`).
    Lts,
    /// The DRAM read observer (`KernelReplayResult.dram`).
    Dram,
}

/// Typed reason a metric was NOT predicted by THIS run — distinct from a
/// value-level `None` (which means "predicted n/a: no accesses"). The harness
/// excludes such a cell with a reason rather than scoring a null.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Unavailable {
    /// The replay's mem-mode did not attach the counting unit this metric
    /// reads (e.g. no L2 counters under `Flat`/`L1Const`).
    MemModeLacksUnit { needs: MemUnit },
}

/// Per-metric outcome: a genuine prediction, or a typed not-produced reason.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub enum EmitOutcome {
    Predicted(MetricValue),
    Unavailable(Unavailable),
}

/// One emitted metric, carrying its registry key + NCU identifier so the eval
/// join (downstream, outside `sim/`) can match against frozen labels by key.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub struct MetricPrediction {
    /// The registry key — the eval JOIN key.
    pub key: &'static str,
    /// The NCU metric identifier this predicts.
    pub ncu_metric: &'static str,
    pub unit: Unit,
    pub outcome: EmitOutcome,
}

/// A compiled row of the emission table: the binding from a sim quantity to
/// its registry contract. [`DESCRIPTORS`] is the single source of truth the
/// lockstep test pins against `metric_registry.json`.
pub struct MetricDescriptor {
    pub key: &'static str,
    pub ncu_metric: &'static str,
    pub unit: Unit,
    pub kind: MetricKind,
    pub emit: fn(&CounterSnapshot) -> Result<EmitOutcome, EmitError>,
}

/// Fail-closed emission faults. Benign "this run's mem-mode lacks the unit" is
/// NOT an error — it is an [`Unavailable`] outcome inside the vector, so a
/// Flat-mode run still emits the instruction count while marking the cache
/// rates typed-unavailable (the Carded::Gap / unsupported_memory_path idiom).
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EmitError {
    #[error(
        "metric {key}: rate numerator {num} exceeds denominator {den} — a >1.0 fraction is a \
         counter bug, never clamped into range"
    )]
    RateExceedsUnity {
        key: &'static str,
        num: u64,
        den: u64,
    },
    #[error("counter invariant broken for {key}: {detail}")]
    CounterInvariant {
        key: &'static str,
        detail: &'static str,
    },
}

/// READ-class bypass sectors = all bypass sectors minus the ATOM write-class
/// subset. This is the LDGSTS/bypass-LOAD stream that folds into the `op_ld`
/// surface; the ATOM subset (booked under op_atom/op_red by NCU) stays out.
fn bypass_read_sectors(key: &'static str, l1: &L1Counters) -> Result<u64, EmitError> {
    l1.bypass_sectors
        .checked_sub(l1.bypass_atom_sectors)
        .ok_or(EmitError::CounterInvariant {
            key,
            detail: "bypass_atom_sectors exceeds bypass_sectors (subset invariant broken)",
        })
}

// ---- per-metric emit fns (the rate accounting, moved out of the counters) ----

/// `smsp__inst_executed.sum` — total warp-instructions issued. One issue per
/// traced record across every SM; always available (no mem unit needed).
fn emit_smsp_inst_executed(snap: &CounterSnapshot) -> Result<EmitOutcome, EmitError> {
    Ok(EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(
        snap.instructions_issued,
    )))
}

/// `l1tex__t_sectors_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_ld.sum` — global-load sectors:
/// modeled eligible loads plus the READ-class bypass (LDGSTS) stream.
fn emit_gmem_ld_sectors(snap: &CounterSnapshot) -> Result<EmitOutcome, EmitError> {
    let key = "traffic_gmem_ld_sectors";
    let Some(l1) = snap.l1 else {
        return Ok(EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
            needs: MemUnit::L1Tex,
        }));
    };
    let sectors = l1.hits + l1.misses + bypass_read_sectors(key, l1)?;
    Ok(EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(sectors)))
}

/// `l1tex__t_sectors_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_st.sum` — global-store sectors.
fn emit_gmem_st_sectors(snap: &CounterSnapshot) -> Result<EmitOutcome, EmitError> {
    let Some(l1) = snap.l1 else {
        return Ok(EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
            needs: MemUnit::L1Tex,
        }));
    };
    Ok(EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(l1.store_sectors)))
}

/// `l1tex__t_sector_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_ld_hit_rate.pct` — the op_ld sector
/// hit rate. Numerator = modeled eligible hits; denominator folds the
/// READ-class bypass (LDGSTS) sectors in (they miss L1 structurally in v0, so
/// they enter the denominator but contribute no hits — the honest residual).
fn emit_l1tex_read_hit_rate(snap: &CounterSnapshot) -> Result<EmitOutcome, EmitError> {
    let key = "cache_hit_rate_l1tex_read_sector";
    let Some(l1) = snap.l1 else {
        return Ok(EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
            needs: MemUnit::L1Tex,
        }));
    };
    let num = l1.hits;
    let den = l1.hits + l1.misses + bypass_read_sectors(key, l1)?;
    Ok(EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::fraction(
        key, num, den,
    )?))
}

/// `l1tex__t_sector_hit_rate.pct` — the unified L1TEX sector hit rate over all
/// op classes. v0 numerator uses the sector-valid store rule (`store_hits`);
/// the §6.4 line-TAG rule (`store_tag_hits`) is the carried alternative,
/// unresolved until l1tex store accounting is scored. The full bypass stream
/// (atom included) is in the denominator — the unified metric covers
/// global_atomic/global_reduction, so `bypass_atom_sectors` must NOT be added
/// on top (it is already a subset of `bypass_sectors`).
fn emit_l1tex_unified_hit_rate(snap: &CounterSnapshot) -> Result<EmitOutcome, EmitError> {
    let key = "cache_hit_rate_l1tex_sector";
    let Some(l1) = snap.l1 else {
        return Ok(EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
            needs: MemUnit::L1Tex,
        }));
    };
    let num = l1.hits + l1.store_hits;
    let den = l1.hits + l1.misses + l1.store_sectors + l1.bypass_sectors + l1.untagged_sectors;
    Ok(EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::fraction(
        key, num, den,
    )?))
}

/// `lts__t_sector_hit_rate.pct` — the unified L2 sector hit rate. Every LTS
/// access from all four L2 source lanes is in `l2.hits`/`l2.misses`;
/// `write_tag_hits` is already a subset of `hits` (do not add it).
fn emit_l2_hit_rate(snap: &CounterSnapshot) -> Result<EmitOutcome, EmitError> {
    let key = "cache_hit_rate_l2_sector";
    let Some(l2) = snap.l2 else {
        return Ok(EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
            needs: MemUnit::Lts,
        }));
    };
    Ok(EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::fraction(
        key,
        l2.hits,
        l2.total(),
    )?))
}

/// `dram__sectors_read.sum` — DRAM read sectors (v0 read-only demand proxy).
fn emit_dram_read_sectors(snap: &CounterSnapshot) -> Result<EmitOutcome, EmitError> {
    let Some(dram) = snap.dram else {
        return Ok(EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
            needs: MemUnit::Dram,
        }));
    };
    Ok(EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(
        dram.read_sectors,
    )))
}

/// The v0 emission table — one row per registry contract this layer predicts.
/// Adding a metric is a one-row append plus its emit fn; the lockstep test and
/// the eval join need no edits.
pub const DESCRIPTORS: &[MetricDescriptor] = &[
    MetricDescriptor {
        key: "smsp_inst_executed_sum",
        ncu_metric: "smsp__inst_executed.sum",
        unit: Unit::Count,
        kind: MetricKind::Count,
        emit: emit_smsp_inst_executed,
    },
    MetricDescriptor {
        key: "traffic_gmem_ld_sectors",
        ncu_metric: "l1tex__t_sectors_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_ld.sum",
        unit: Unit::Count,
        kind: MetricKind::Count,
        emit: emit_gmem_ld_sectors,
    },
    MetricDescriptor {
        key: "traffic_gmem_st_sectors",
        ncu_metric: "l1tex__t_sectors_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_st.sum",
        unit: Unit::Count,
        kind: MetricKind::Count,
        emit: emit_gmem_st_sectors,
    },
    MetricDescriptor {
        key: "cache_hit_rate_l1tex_read_sector",
        ncu_metric: "l1tex__t_sector_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_ld_hit_rate.pct",
        unit: Unit::Pct,
        kind: MetricKind::Fraction,
        emit: emit_l1tex_read_hit_rate,
    },
    MetricDescriptor {
        key: "cache_hit_rate_l1tex_sector",
        ncu_metric: "l1tex__t_sector_hit_rate.pct",
        unit: Unit::Pct,
        kind: MetricKind::Fraction,
        emit: emit_l1tex_unified_hit_rate,
    },
    MetricDescriptor {
        key: "cache_hit_rate_l2_sector",
        ncu_metric: "lts__t_sector_hit_rate.pct",
        unit: Unit::Pct,
        kind: MetricKind::Fraction,
        emit: emit_l2_hit_rate,
    },
    MetricDescriptor {
        key: "traffic_dram_read_sectors",
        ncu_metric: "dram__sectors_read.sum",
        unit: Unit::Count,
        kind: MetricKind::Count,
        emit: emit_dram_read_sectors,
    },
];

/// Assert an emit fn returned the numeric shape its descriptor promised.
fn shape_matches(kind: MetricKind, value: &MetricValue) -> bool {
    matches!(
        (kind, value),
        (MetricKind::Count, MetricValue::Exact(_))
            | (MetricKind::Fraction, MetricValue::Fraction { .. })
    )
}

/// Emit every descriptor over one completed replay, in registry-table order.
/// Genuine faults (a rate above unity, a broken subset invariant) return
/// [`EmitError`]; benign missing-unit cases ride the [`Unavailable`] arm.
pub fn emit_all(snap: &CounterSnapshot) -> Result<Vec<MetricPrediction>, EmitError> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(DESCRIPTORS.len());
    for d in DESCRIPTORS {
        let outcome = (d.emit)(snap)?;
        if let EmitOutcome::Predicted(v) = &outcome {
            debug_assert!(
                shape_matches(d.kind, v),
                "emit fn for {} returned a value shape inconsistent with its declared kind",
                d.key
            );
        }
        out.push(MetricPrediction {
            key: d.key,
            ncu_metric: d.ncu_metric,
            unit: d.unit,
            outcome,
        });
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// A by-key view of a prediction vector for the eval join.
pub fn index_by_key(
    preds: &[MetricPrediction],
) -> std::collections::BTreeMap<&'static str, &MetricPrediction> {
    preds.iter().map(|p| (p.key, p)).collect()
}

#[cfg(test)]
#[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use sim_mem::{L1Counters, L2Counters};
    use sim_sm::DramStats;

    /// A replay result carrying just the counters the emit fns read.
    fn replay(
        instructions_issued: u64,
        l1: Option<L1Counters>,
        l2: Option<L2Counters>,
        dram: Option<DramStats>,
    ) -> KernelReplayResult {
        KernelReplayResult {
            instructions_issued,
            records_seen: instructions_issued,
            per_sm: Default::default(),
            max_cycles: 1,
            l1,
            l2,
            l2_by_source: None,
            dram,
        }
    }

    fn predicted<'a>(preds: &'a [MetricPrediction], key: &str) -> &'a EmitOutcome {
        &preds
            .iter()
            .find(|p| p.key == key)
            .expect("key present")
            .outcome
    }

    /// Emit from owned counters (the `KernelReplayResult` temporary lives
    /// through the `emit_all` call within this expression).
    fn emit(
        instructions_issued: u64,
        l1: Option<L1Counters>,
        l2: Option<L2Counters>,
        dram: Option<DramStats>,
    ) -> Result<Vec<MetricPrediction>, EmitError> {
        emit_all(&CounterSnapshot::from_replay(&replay(
            instructions_issued,
            l1,
            l2,
            dram,
        )))
    }

    #[test]
    fn fraction_is_none_at_zero_denominator_never_zero() {
        let v = MetricValue::fraction("k", 0, 0).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            v,
            MetricValue::Fraction {
                value: None,
                numerator: 0,
                denominator: 0
            }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn fraction_real_zero_is_some_zero() {
        let MetricValue::Fraction { value, .. } = MetricValue::fraction("k", 0, 10).unwrap() else {
            panic!("expected fraction");
        };
        assert_eq!(value, Some(0.0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rate_above_unity_is_a_typed_error_not_a_clamp() {
        assert_eq!(
            MetricValue::fraction("k", 11, 10),
            Err(EmitError::RateExceedsUnity {
                key: "k",
                num: 11,
                den: 10
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn op_ld_surface_folds_read_class_bypass_ldgsts_into_the_denominator() {
        // Witness shape: a kernel of ONLY LDGSTS loads (all bypass, none
        // eligible, no atoms) — mirrors gemm_hmma_bf16. The op_ld sector
        // count is the bypass-read stream, and the modeled hit rate is 0
        // (v0 has no L1 residency for bypass) — the honest under-prediction.
        let l1 = L1Counters {
            bypass_sectors: 196_608,
            bypass_atom_sectors: 0,
            store_sectors: 16_384,
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let preds = emit(197_120, Some(l1), None, None).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "traffic_gmem_ld_sectors"),
            &EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(196_608))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "cache_hit_rate_l1tex_read_sector"),
            &EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Fraction {
                value: Some(0.0),
                numerator: 0,
                denominator: 196_608
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "traffic_gmem_st_sectors"),
            &EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(16_384))
        );
        // The instruction count needs no mem unit and is always emitted.
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "smsp_inst_executed_sum"),
            &EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(197_120))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn op_ld_denominator_excludes_the_atom_write_class_bypass_subset() {
        // 100 bypass sectors, 40 of them ATOM (write-class -> op_atom/op_red,
        // NOT op_ld). The op_ld surface sees only the 60 READ-class sectors.
        let l1 = L1Counters {
            hits: 10,
            misses: 5,
            bypass_sectors: 100,
            bypass_atom_sectors: 40,
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let preds = emit(1, Some(l1), None, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "traffic_gmem_ld_sectors"),
            &EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(10 + 5 + 60))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn atom_subset_exceeding_bypass_is_a_typed_counter_invariant() {
        let l1 = L1Counters {
            bypass_sectors: 3,
            bypass_atom_sectors: 4,
            ..Default::default()
        };
        assert_eq!(
            emit(1, Some(l1), None, None),
            Err(EmitError::CounterInvariant {
                key: "traffic_gmem_ld_sectors",
                detail: "bypass_atom_sectors exceeds bypass_sectors (subset invariant broken)",
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_mem_unit_is_unavailable_not_an_error_or_a_zero() {
        // Flat mode: no L1/L2/DRAM. Only the instruction count is produced;
        // every cache metric is typed-unavailable with its needed unit.
        let preds = emit(42, None, None, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "smsp_inst_executed_sum"),
            &EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(42))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "cache_hit_rate_l1tex_read_sector"),
            &EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
                needs: MemUnit::L1Tex
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "cache_hit_rate_l2_sector"),
            &EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
                needs: MemUnit::Lts
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "traffic_dram_read_sectors"),
            &EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
                needs: MemUnit::Dram
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn l2_and_dram_metrics_predict_when_their_units_are_present() {
        let l2 = L2Counters {
            hits: 3,
            misses: 1,
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let dram = DramStats {
            read_sectors: 8415,
            bw_delayed_responses: 0,
        };
        let preds = emit(1, None, Some(l2), Some(dram)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "cache_hit_rate_l2_sector"),
            &EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Fraction {
                value: Some(0.75),
                numerator: 3,
                denominator: 4
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "traffic_dram_read_sectors"),
            &EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(8415))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn index_by_key_covers_every_descriptor() {
        let preds = emit(1, None, None, None).unwrap();
        let idx = index_by_key(&preds);
        assert_eq!(idx.len(), DESCRIPTORS.len());
        for d in DESCRIPTORS {
            assert!(
                idx.contains_key(d.key),
                "descriptor {} missing from index",
                d.key
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn descriptor_keys_are_unique() {
        let mut keys: Vec<&str> = DESCRIPTORS.iter().map(|d| d.key).collect();
        keys.sort_unstable();
        let n = keys.len();
        keys.dedup();
        assert_eq!(keys.len(), n, "duplicate descriptor keys");
    }
}
```

#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used)] // test binary: unwrap is an assertion
//! Machine-local replay smoke: join a real captured trace with its
//! control-bits sidecar and replay it end-to-end under the issue model
//! with the sim-mem L1 attached (cache-op roles come from the sidecar's
//! own opcode text; geometry from the committed pchase static card).
//!
//! The M1 evidence is gitignored machine-local data, so inputs come from
//! the environment (Rule-1 guard: no annex/label path literals inside
//! sim/):
//!
//! ```sh
//! SIM_TRACE_SMOKE_DIR=<trace_<shape> dir> \
//! SIM_CONTROL_BITS_DIR=<control-bits sidecar dir> \
//!   cargo test --release -p sim-sm --test machine_local_replay \
//!   real_trace_replays_under_issue_model -- --ignored --exact --nocapture
//! ```
//!
//! The control-bits sidecar is located from the trace's own metadata (the
//! exec info's `benchmark_name` minus a trailing `_run` +
//! `.control_bits.json`). The ordinary workspace suite ignores this test; the
//! authoritative hardware gate supplies both environment values and executes
//! it nonvacuously. Missing values on a direct ignored-test invocation fail.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use sim_calib::ArchCard;
use sim_mem::{L2Config, PchaseCard};
use sim_sm::{ControlSidecar, IssueModelParams, ReplayMemMode, build_schedules, replay_kernel};
use sim_trace::{ExecInfo, TraceDir};

fn sm86_card() -> ArchCard {
    // The card is COMMITTED repo data (not machine-local evidence), so an
    // in-repo path is fine here. The M1 traces are sm_86 captures.
    let path =
        PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../arch_profiles/cards/sm_86.json");
    ArchCard::load(&path).expect("committed sm_86 card loads")
}

fn sm86_pchase_card() -> PchaseCard {
    // Committed P-chase static card: the L1 geometry source the Phase-1
    // walker resolves from (capacity has no default; MSHR documented
    // default when typed).
    let path =
        PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../data/pchase/sm_86_static_card.json");
    PchaseCard::load(&path).expect("committed pchase card loads")
}

#[test]
#[ignore = "requires machine-local M1 evidence; run tools/dev/hw_evidence_gate.sh"]
fn real_trace_replays_under_issue_model() {
    let trace_dir = std::env::var("SIM_TRACE_SMOKE_DIR")
        .expect("SIM_TRACE_SMOKE_DIR must be set by tools/dev/hw_evidence_gate.sh");
    let cb_dir = std::env::var("SIM_CONTROL_BITS_DIR")
        .expect("SIM_CONTROL_BITS_DIR must be set by tools/dev/hw_evidence_gate.sh");

    let td = TraceDir::open(&trace_dir).expect("open trace dir");
    let exec = ExecInfo::load_from_trace_dir(td.root()).expect("exec info loads");
    let stem = exec
        .benchmark_name
        .strip_suffix("_run")
        .unwrap_or(&exec.benchmark_name);
    let sidecar_path = Path::new(&cb_dir).join(format!("{stem}.control_bits.json"));
    let sidecar = ControlSidecar::load(&sidecar_path, "sm_86").expect("sidecar loads");

    let schedules = build_schedules(&exec, &sidecar).expect("(function, pc) join");

    let lat = sm86_card()
        .required_latencies()
        .expect("sm_86 card has no latency gaps");
    let params =
        IssueModelParams::v0_sm86_from_card_latencies(lat.l1_hit, lat.l2_hit, lat.dram, lat.shared);

    // L1 mode: geometry (capacity + MSHR) from the committed pchase
    // static card's fail-closed resolvers; the hit/miss LATENCIES come
    // from `params` — one source, so the pair can never drift. The
    // resolvers' own latency audit (hit strictly below miss) still runs
    // as part of geometry resolution. SIM_L1_DISABLE=1 exercises the
    // flat-latency ablation path end-to-end (the owner runner runs one
    // cell in this mode so `classify_flat` never goes machine-untested).
    // Typed mode selection: flat (SIM_L1_DISABLE=1) → L1-const
    // (SIM_L2_DISABLE=1, the pre-L2 lockstep surface) → default full
    // hierarchy (shared L2 from the arch card's vendor-documented
    // `l2_geometry`; assoc/hash/policy documented defaults).
    let mode = if std::env::var("SIM_L1_DISABLE").is_ok() {
        ReplayMemMode::Flat
    } else {
        let geometry = sm86_pchase_card()
            .resolve_walk_geometry(None)
            .expect("pchase geometry resolves");
        let l1 = params.l1_config(geometry.capacity.line_capacity, geometry.mshr.count);
        if std::env::var("SIM_L2_DISABLE").is_ok() {
            ReplayMemMode::L1Const(l1)
        } else {
            let card = sm86_card();
            let g = card
                .l2_geometry
                .require("sm_86", "l2_geometry")
                .expect("sm_86 card l2_geometry present");
            let l2 = L2Config::from_carded_geometry(
                "sm_86",
                g.capacity_bytes,
                g.line_bytes,
                g.sector_bytes,
                g.num_slices,
                g.policy.as_deref(),
            )
            .expect("carded L2 geometry valid");
            // DRAM read-bandwidth covariate from the card's locked
            // operating point (fail-closed: a card without the block
            // cannot run the full hierarchy). SIM_DRAM_BW_DISABLE=1 is
            // the latency-only ablation (the pre-covariate model).
            let dram = if std::env::var("SIM_DRAM_BW_DISABLE").is_ok() {
                sim_sm::DramBw::Unmodeled
            } else {
                let bw = card
                    .dram_bandwidth
                    .require("sm_86", "dram_bandwidth")
                    .expect("sm_86 card dram_bandwidth present");
                sim_sm::DramBw::Carded {
                    bytes_per_sec: bw
                        .validated_peak_bytes_per_second()
                        .expect("carded peak rate valid"),
                    sm_clock_hz: bw.locked_sm_clock_hz().expect("carded SM clock valid"),
                }
            };
            ReplayMemMode::L1SharedL2 { l1, l2, dram }
        }
    };

    let mut kernels = 0usize;
    let mut records: u64 = 0;
    let mut issued: u64 = 0;
    let mut max_cycles: u64 = 0;
    let mut sms = 0usize;
    let mut l1_totals: Option<sim_mem::L1Counters> = None;
    let mut l2_totals: Option<sim_mem::L2Counters> = None;
    let mut split_totals = sim_sm::L2SourceSplit::default();
    let mut dram_totals: Option<sim_sm::DramStats> = None;
    for loc in td.kernels().collect::<Vec<_>>() {
        let result = replay_kernel(&td, &loc, &schedules, &params, mode).expect("replay");
        kernels += 1;
        records += result.records_seen;
        issued += result.instructions_issued;
        max_cycles = max_cycles.max(result.max_cycles);
        sms = sms.max(result.per_sm.len());
        assert_eq!(result.instructions_issued, result.records_seen);
        if let Some(c) = &result.l1 {
            l1_totals.get_or_insert_with(Default::default).add(c);
        }
        if let Some(c) = &result.l2 {
            l2_totals
                .get_or_insert_with(sim_mem::L2Counters::default)
                .add(c);
        }
        if let Some(split) = &result.l2_by_source {
            split_totals.add(split);
        }
        if let Some(d) = &result.dram {
            dram_totals.get_or_insert_with(Default::default).add(d);
        }
    }
    eprintln!(
        "smoke: replay kernels={kernels} records={records} issued={issued} \
         max_cycles={max_cycles} sms={sms}"
    );
    if let Some(c) = &l1_totals {
        eprintln!(
            "smoke: l1 hits={} misses={} merges={} stalls={} line_alloc={} sector_res={} \
             bypass={} bypass_atom={} untagged={} store={} store_hits={} store_tag_hits={}",
            c.hits,
            c.misses,
            c.merges,
            c.stall_events,
            c.line_alloc_misses,
            c.sector_resident_misses,
            c.bypass_sectors,
            c.bypass_atom_sectors,
            c.untagged_sectors,
            c.store_sectors,
            c.store_hits,
            c.store_tag_hits,
        );
    }
    if let Some(c) = &l2_totals {
        let s = split_totals;
        eprintln!(
            "smoke: l2 hits={} misses={} line_misses={} sector_fill_misses={} write_tag_hits={} \
             fill=({},{}) bypass=({},{}) untagged=({},{}) store=({},{})",
            c.hits,
            c.misses,
            c.line_misses,
            c.sector_fill_misses,
            c.write_tag_hits,
            s.sectors[0],
            s.hits[0],
            s.sectors[1],
            s.hits[1],
            s.sectors[2],
            s.hits[2],
            s.sectors[3],
            s.hits[3],
        );
    }
    if let Some(d) = &dram_totals {
        eprintln!(
            "smoke: dram read_sectors={} bw_delayed_responses={}",
            d.read_sectors, d.bw_delayed_responses
        );
    }

    // NCU-metric emission over the cell's summed counters (sim-emit contract
    // layer). Rates compose from summed numerators/denominators — so emission
    // runs on the AGGREGATE, never on per-kernel rates. One machine-parseable
    // line per metric drives the accuracy sweep (labels stay outside sim/).
    let snap = sim_emit::CounterSnapshot {
        instructions_issued: issued,
        l1: l1_totals.as_ref(),
        l2: l2_totals.as_ref(),
        dram: dram_totals.as_ref(),
    };
    for p in sim_emit::emit_all(&snap).expect("emission contracts hold") {
        use sim_emit::{EmitOutcome, MetricValue};
        let payload = match p.outcome {
            EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(v)) => format!("count:{v}"),
            EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Fraction {
                value,
                numerator,
                denominator,
            }) => match value {
                Some(x) => format!("frac:{x}:{numerator}/{denominator}"),
                None => format!("frac:na:{numerator}/{denominator}"),
            },
            EmitOutcome::Unavailable(u) => format!("unavailable:{u:?}"),
        };
        eprintln!("smoke: emit {} = {}", p.key, payload);
    }

    assert!(kernels > 0 && issued > 0 && max_cycles > 0 && sms > 0);
}

{"excerpt_sha256":"abbb1759cb6f8183e5898f8fe0384a5ee958a314b407a9a324edd5d83982d0df","file_sha256":"abbb1759cb6f8183e5898f8fe0384a5ee958a314b407a9a324edd5d83982d0df","file_total_lines":91,"final_newline":true,"full_required_justification":"The compact test's loading, matching, and assertions completely define the currently enforced direction and its gaps.","id":"E1036","kind":"file_full","lines":[1,91],"non_operational":true,"path":"sim/emit/tests/registry_lockstep.rs","revision":"WORKTREE","role":"decision","selection_reason":"The complete current lockstep test exposes its one-way descriptor-to-registry scope and the missing registry-to-descriptor or typed-exclusion direction.","supports":["B1014"]}

```rust
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used)] // test binary: unwrap is an assertion
//! Registry lockstep: every `sim_emit::DESCRIPTORS` row must bind to a real
//! `tools/local_labels/metric_registry.json` v2 entry with a matching NCU
//! metric string, unit, and numeric shape. This closes the drift surface —
//! a descriptor cannot name a metric that does not exist or misdeclare its
//! contract without failing here.
//!
//! Rule-1 note: this reads the registry (metric NAMES / contract shapes — the
//! output contract, allowed in the emit tree), never a label VALUE artifact
//! from the gitignored machine-local evidence trees.

use std::path::PathBuf;

use serde_json::Value;
use sim_emit::{DESCRIPTORS, MetricKind, Unit};

fn registry() -> Value {
    let path = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
        .join("../../tools/local_labels/metric_registry.json");
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("read registry {}: {e}", path.display()));
    serde_json::from_str(&text).expect("registry parses")
}

#[test]
fn every_descriptor_matches_its_registry_contract() {
    let reg = registry();
    let metrics = reg["metrics"].as_array().expect("metrics is an array");

    let mut failures: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for d in DESCRIPTORS {
        let Some(entry) = metrics.iter().find(|m| m["key"].as_str() == Some(d.key)) else {
            failures.push(format!("{}: no registry entry with this key", d.key));
            continue;
        };

        let ncu = entry["ncu_metric"].as_str().unwrap_or("<none>");
        if ncu != d.ncu_metric {
            failures.push(format!(
                "{}: ncu_metric mismatch — descriptor {:?} vs registry {:?}",
                d.key, d.ncu_metric, ncu
            ));
        }

        let unit = entry["unit"].as_str().unwrap_or("<none>");
        let unit_ok = match d.unit {
            Unit::Count => unit == "count",
            Unit::Pct => unit == "pct",
        };
        if !unit_ok {
            failures.push(format!(
                "{}: unit mismatch — descriptor {:?} vs registry {:?}",
                d.key, d.unit, unit
            ));
        }

        // Numeric shape must agree with the registry's bound + parser:
        // a Count is unbounded above (valid_max null); a Fraction is a
        // percent stored as a [0,1] value (valid_max 1.0, percent_to_fraction).
        let valid_max = &entry["valid_max"];
        let parser = entry["parser_transform"].as_str().unwrap_or("<none>");
        let kind_ok = match d.kind {
            MetricKind::Count => valid_max.is_null(),
            MetricKind::Fraction => {
                valid_max.as_f64() == Some(1.0) && parser == "percent_to_fraction"
            }
        };
        if !kind_ok {
            failures.push(format!(
                "{}: kind {:?} inconsistent with registry valid_max={} parser_transform={:?}",
                d.key, d.kind, valid_max, parser
            ));
        }

        // A metric we EMIT as a prediction must be a target, not an input
        // (Rule 1's model_io_role field; the guard's role assertion).
        let role = entry["model_io_role"].as_str().unwrap_or("<none>");
        if role != "target" {
            failures.push(format!(
                "{}: model_io_role is {:?}, expected \"target\" for an emitted prediction",
                d.key, role
            ));
        }
    }

    assert!(
        failures.is_empty(),
        "descriptor/registry lockstep failures:\n{}",
        failures.join("\n")
    );
}
```

````markdown
**Inherited operator decisions (still binding, from the 2026-07-02 founding plan):**
- **Hardware:** 3 GPUs / 2 arches / 3 SKUs — RTX 3090 Ti (GA102, sm_86) · RTX 5060 laptop (GB206, sm_120) · cloud RTX PRO 6000 (GB202, sm_120). No B200/sm_100 in paper 1.
- **Full root + NCU on ALL three targets** (reaffirmed 2026-07-06): clock/memory-clock locking (`nvidia-smi -lgc/-lmc`), persistence mode, and counter-permission setup are **allowed and preferred**, local *and* cloud. The old non-root/counter-less deployment thesis, the cloud-NCU ban, the NCU quarantine, and "no simulator revival" are all **retired**.
- **The one surviving prohibition — targets-never-features.** NCU / hardware-counter values are prediction *targets and validation references only*; they must never enter simulator inputs, trace features, or calibration constants fitted on the *same cell* being scored. Enforced by the repurposed leakage guard (`deployability` → `model_io_role: target | input | either`).
- **Execution order — sm_86 first, to completion.** The current dev host **is the RTX 3090 Ti**. The repo does not migrate to the 5060 laptop or cloud GB202 until M-SIM-1 passes and the operator explicitly approves migration.
- **Accuracy bar — cycle-accurate *outputs*, not cycle-ticking *implementation*.** The sole publication-binding target is `gpc__cycles_elapsed.max`; it remains bound to the captured operating state and is not assumed DVFS-stable. Registry-governed metrics and the seven current simulator descriptors are reported secondary outputs, not substitute headlines. The event-driven engine retains the 100–1000× cycle-simulator speed objective.

## 1. Thesis and novelty (MICRO 2027 framing)

**Thesis.** An open, event-driven, trace-driven simulator of Ampere/Blackwell SMs and memory hierarchy,
calibrated per architecture from non-NCU microbenchmarks or vendor documentation and validated against
NCU on silicon, can predict the sole binding cycle target while reporting a typed set of supported
NCU-shaped secondary descriptors at **100–1000×** the speed of cycle-level simulators — a practical
replacement for Accel-Sim-class tools on modern AI kernels, and the first such tool that reaches
consumer/workstation Blackwell. The 61-entry registry remains capture and metric-identity authority;
it is not a claim that every registry metric is a simulator output or publication gate.

**Relevant open gaps** (from the 2026-07-02 adversarial SOTA survey; provenance retained there). Under ADR 0002, vector, cache, and SOL gaps motivate secondary reporting only; they are not co-headlines or fallback gates:
1. **No open simulator has a validated timing model past sm_86.** Accel-Sim tops out at SM80_A100 / SM86_RTX3070 (~25–32% Ampere error, ~12.5 KIPS → days/workload); GPGPU-Sim 4.x is in maintenance.
2. **No published work predicts full NCU metric *vectors*.** Nearest neighbor is Omniwise (AMD-only, source-only, 10–12 metrics, random splits).
3. **No model targets NCU *sector hit-rate* metrics.** Best NCU-validated cache model: profiner (CGF'22; L1 3.73% / L2 15.81% MAPE, one Turing GPU). The frozen sm_86 v5 L2 head's **6.4% geomean** is retained as an external historical comparator only; it is not an in-simulator calibration layer or architecture input.
4. **No sm_120 (consumer/workstation Blackwell) performance model exists at all** — only microbench dissections (RTX 5080 arXiv:2507.10789; B200 arXiv:2512.02189; Chips&Cheese GB202).
5. **No academic work predicts NCU Speed-of-Light percentages.**
6. **No GPU analog of the Weaver/McKee counter-determinism studies** — an NCU counter-repeatability characterization is free, load-bearing novelty (§6).

**Competitors to engage head-on:** PipeWeave (ISCA'26; hybrid, 6.1% latency, 11 GPUs — *latency-only, operator-level*; we differ on event-driven what-if capability + arbitrary-SASS generality + Blackwell); UPC "Modeling Modern GPU Cores" (MICRO'25; 13.45% Ampere / 17.41% Blackwell cycle MAPE *inside cycle-level Accel-Sim, slow* — their reverse-engineered facts are **inputs to our SM model**); NVArchSim (HPCA'21; the design template, proprietary — we are the open, Blackwell-capable instantiation); the GPUMech→MDM→GCoM→AMALI cascade (mechanistic models calibrated to one generation explode on the next: GCoM 10%→127% on A100 LLM kernels — our per-arch microbench calibration + silicon-only validation is the answer).

**Paper's one-sentence positioning:** *a measurement instrument and design-iteration tool — it predicts the binding cycle target and supported NCU-shaped secondary descriptors on real hardware in seconds instead of days, and, unlike black-box predictors, its event-driven core retains what-if capability.* The **what-if / variable-fidelity** capability is the primary differentiator vs. the hybrid-ML competitors (PipeWeave, NeuSight, SynPerf) and the reason D1 chose simulator-primary.

---

## 6. Simulator design (grounded in the design note + the F1–F10 fix list)

From `references/papers/notes/draft_new_gpu_simulator.md` (NVArchSim-inspired) + the UPC MICRO'25
reverse-engineered facts + the repo's own failure→fix map (`plans/research/sota_…dossier.md` §3):

- **6.1 Engine.** Rust. Binary-heap event queue → hybrid timing-wheel + min-heap; **tagged-enum event dispatch** (no virtual dispatch on the hot path); compact POD event record `{time, seq, target_id, kind, payload_ref}`; pure next-event clock advance. **Per-SM actor mini-loop** batches several issue cycles per wake (NOT one event per warp pick) to avoid queue flooding. Throughput target **3–10 M events/s → 10–30 M optimized.**
- **6.2 SM model** (fidelity MEDIUM). 4 sub-cores; CGGTY issue; **dependence stalls read from SASS control bits (Phase 1E), not simulated scoreboards** — the 13–17% cycles-MAPE lever [F6]. Unified INT32/FP32 pipe for sm_120 (verified GB202 fact); tensor path = HMMA (sm_86) / block-scaled `mma.sync` + FP8/FP6/FP4 (sm_120). **No tcgen05/TMEM** (sm_100-only; out of scope).
- **6.3 Memory hierarchy.** L1 = sectored + **finite MSHR** + **warp-pool FIFO interleaving** + **carveout-aware capacity** [F1–F3, Nugteren HPCA'14 warp-pool 6.4–8.3% L1 MAE; HRD(32,128) two-granularity reuse distance]; geometry from the per-arch cards [F2, Mei&Chu p-chase]. L2 = slice actors ported from `tools/cache_replay/sector_cache_replay.py` semantics (32 B sector fills, hashed slice mapping — **widen the IPOLY-style hash for GB202's large L2**; note the L40/5090 non-uniform-L2-latency finding). DRAM = GDDR6X/GDDR7 bandwidth-latency (fidelity HIGH only if error attribution demands it).
- **6.4 NCU-emission layer** (`sim/emit`). Every supported emitted descriptor implements its registry-v2 observation contract, **including NCU's sector-accounting semantics** (the ~15 pp hazard Accel-Sim's authors attribute to profiler accounting) and NCU's **isolated-execution / per-pass cache-flush** assumption → simulate **cold-cache per kernel by default**, matching `--cache-control all` labels. The seven current descriptors remain secondary and ungated. `gpc__cycles_elapsed.max` remains `required_unimplemented` until the checked-in aggregation-semantics study admits its mapping.
- **6.5 Calibration layer** (`sim/calib`). Per-architecture latencies and throughputs come only from dedicated non-NCU microbenchmarks and vendor documentation. Historical NCU-fitted isotonic/residual heads remain external evaluation comparators; they do not calibrate simulator state, architecture cards, or emitted predictions [F5].
- **6.6 Fidelity knobs** (per component, the what-if differentiator): frontend LOW · warp-scheduler MEDIUM · exec-units MEDIUM · tensor MEDIUM · L1 MEDIUM · interconnect LOW · L2 MEDIUM · DRAM HIGH. Codex-flagged **hypotheses-not-spec** (RF cache, uniform unit, L0 icache stream-buffer): keep behind knobs, validate before claiming.

## 8. Novelty / paper contributions (MICRO 2027)

1. **The first open, fast, event-driven simulator with a silicon-validated cycles headline on Ampere *and* consumer/workstation Blackwell** — reaching sm_120, where no open simulator has a config.
2. **A typed NCU-shaped observation and emission layer:** `gpc__cycles_elapsed.max` is the sole binding output; the seven current simulator descriptors and any future capability-gated additions are reported secondary outputs, not co-headlines.
3. **A GPU NCU counter-repeatability / determinism study** (the missing Weaver/McKee analog) — noise floors supporting interpretation of the sole cycles accuracy gate and the ungated secondary diagnostics; includes the Blackwell `lts` 115–217% anomaly.
4. **Same-ISA / cross-SKU generalization** (GB206 vs GB202: only card inputs change) — a controlled test mechanistic models historically fail.
5. **Speed:** 100–1000× over Accel-Sim/UPC with retained **what-if / variable-fidelity** capability — the black-box predictors cannot do what-if.
6. **A dataset release:** NCU-profiled FlashInfer-Bench + SOL-ExecBench across 3 SKUs / 2 arches.

## 9. Risk register

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation (already in plan) |
|---|---|---|
| Cycles bar ≤10% (D5) is *below* the ~13–17% literature floor | **High** | Report >10% through ≤15% honestly as floor-only. A result >15% is publication failure and cannot be replaced by a metric-vector or hybrid-head headline. Heavier control-bit (§1E) + latency (§1D) calibration is the primary accuracy lever. |
| NVBit Blackwell TMA-tracing bugs (#162–164) | Med | Typed-exclude TMA-heavy cells; track upstream; consumer sm_120 avoids tcgen05/TMA-heavy paths. |
| Laptop clock instability (lock → limit under thermals) | Med→Low | Root clock locking controls but does not eliminate operating-state and thermal risk; keep nvbench-style noise gates (≥10 samples, 0.5% rel-stddev stop, ≥20 µs kernels). |
| Blackwell classifier fix doesn't meet the L2 engineering diagnostic | Med | It's now a *measurement* task (NCU+root); if other error sources (coalescing/prefetch/compression/ECC) dominate, report that finding honestly. L2 remains nonbinding and cannot affect the cycles publication verdict. |
| MICRO 2027 CFP shifts | Low | Re-confirm monthly; HPCA 2028 (≈Aug 2027) then ISCA 2028 fallbacks. |
| A competitor ships an sm_120 timing model first | Low | Differentiators hold: event-driven speed + what-if capability + arbitrary-SASS scope + 3-SKU silicon validation. Secondary NCU-shaped descriptors remain supporting evidence, not a replacement headline. |
| Schedule slip (9 mo is tight for a from-scratch sim) | Med | Preserve dependency order, keep the ~3-week buffer, and narrow nonbinding scope if needed. Do not front-load Blackwell work or substitute any hybrid/secondary headline for failed cycles. |

## 10. Resolutions to prior open questions (merge dossier Q1–Q10, re-adjudicated under the new charter)

Full-NCU + simulator-primary changes most answers:
- **Q1 (canonical metric registry):** registry v2 / label schema v5 (**61 entries** with observation contracts) is the canonical capture ceiling and metric-identity authority; it already includes the current stall-reason and throughput/SOL surface. Future tensor-pipe or other entries are additive and capability-gated. `model_io_role` governs targets-never-features; registry membership does not imply simulator implementation or publication binding.
- **Q2 (timing labels):** `gpc__cycles_elapsed.max` is the sole publication headline and `gpu__time_duration.sum` is a reported secondary timing label. Active timing is NCU-only. Retained CUPTI dual-source evidence is frozen, historical, and non-authoritative; its producer must not be reactivated.
- **Q3 (wall-clock predictor target):** the legacy wall-clock predictor and direct `duration_ns` model are retired. The simulator's binding output is cycles; any future cycles-to-time mapping must use admitted per-architecture operating-state semantics and remains secondary.
- **Q4 (label authority):** active labels use the authoritative v5 unit-tagged schema and 61-entry registry. Do not re-admit or rewrite historical rows from this founding plan; canonical historical runnability v1 remains restored, while the frozen sm_86 v5 head and 30-cell sm_120 cohort (b1646ef7) remain byte-stable external regression fixtures only.
- **Q5 (sm_90a build vs deploy ban):** already resolved — `build_arch_families.json` separates build-arch from deploy `arch_id`; sm_90a is a compile-only fatbin slice.
- **Q6 (Blackwell classifier fix in scope?):** **YES, conditionally after M-SIM-1 and explicit operator approval** — gated Phase 3 uses cuobjdump inventory + cache-op microbench + NCU differential on the 5060 to set `bare_ldg_e_default` empirically; no Phase-1 sm_120 execution is authorized.
- **Q7 (comparison_runner cohort model):** one arch-parameterized per-(kernel,metric,arch) harness (§3B).
- **Q8 (L1 contract):** L1 remains a reported engineering diagnostic. Coverage records whether the diagnostic is interpretable; it is not an accuracy/publication gate. The warp-pool/MSHR rebuild (§6.3) may improve L1 reporting, but no hard L1 accuracy gate is added under the current cycles-only contract without a later explicit ADR.
- **Q9 (Blackwell key + token vocab):** `resolve_arch_id` already canonicalizes the 8 spellings; add `cards/sm_120-gb202.json` with SKU disambiguation; the 5060-laptop label does **not** silently transfer to GB202 — that's the cross-SKU experiment.
- **Q10 (provenance slug bug):** cosmetic (gitignored, never joins the runner); fix `build.py` `KERNEL_SLUG` wiring as a bounded Phase-0 tidy.

**Remaining genuine research gaps:** sm_120 L1/L2 geometry, the Blackwell L2 diagnostic target, sm_120 L1 reporting, the sm_120 NVML clock anchor, and cross-arch transfer. They are gated Phase-3 tasks and remain untouched until M-SIM-1 passes and the operator explicitly approves migration.
````

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Authoritative, read-only machine-local evidence gate for the sim workspace.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd -P)
ROOT=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd -P)
PY="$ROOT/.venv/bin/python"
OWNER="$ROOT/tools/nvbit_tracer/test_sim_rust_machine_local.py"
PREFLIGHT_OWNER="$ROOT/tools/local_labels/test_campaign_preflight.py"
PREFLIGHT_NODE="$PREFLIGHT_OWNER::test_environment_probes_ok_on_reference_host"
M1_BUILDER="$ROOT/tools/nvbit_tracer/build_m1_payload_authority.py"
ALIASES="$ROOT/evidence/path_aliases.v2.json"

missing() {
    printf 'hardware_evidence_prerequisite_missing: %s\n' "$1" >&2
    exit 2
}

fail() {
    printf 'hardware_evidence_gate_failed: %s\n' "$1" >&2
    exit 1
}

test -x "$PY" || missing "$PY"
command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing "cargo on PATH"
command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing "nvidia-smi on PATH"
command -v ncu >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing "ncu on PATH"
test -f "$OWNER" || missing "$OWNER"
test -f "$PREFLIGHT_OWNER" || missing "$PREFLIGHT_OWNER"
test -f "$M1_BUILDER" || missing "$M1_BUILDER"
test -f "$ALIASES" || missing "$ALIASES"

TMP_ROOT=$(mktemp -d /tmp/gpu-sim-hw-evidence.XXXXXX) || missing "/tmp"
cleanup() {
    rm -rf -- "$TMP_ROOT"
}
trap cleanup EXIT HUP INT TERM
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$TMP_ROOT/cargo-target"
export CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1

# The builder verifies the source pin, all 17 current mappings, and all 5,033
# payloads without writing.  Preserve its missing-vs-mismatch taxonomy.
set +e
"$PY" "$M1_BUILDER" --verify-only
verify_rc=$?
set -e
case "$verify_rc" in
    0) ;;
    2) missing "M1 payload-authority verification input" ;;
    *) fail "M1 payload-authority verification" ;;
esac

# Parse only current_root values. Historical absolute roots are never emitted
# into the gate environment or a Rust command.
"$PY" - "$ALIASES" <<'PY'
import json
import sys
from pathlib import PurePosixPath

path = sys.argv[1]
doc = json.load(open(path, encoding="utf-8"))
rows = doc.get("rows")
if not isinstance(rows, list) or len(rows) != 17:
    raise SystemExit("path_aliases.v2.json must contain exactly 17 rows")
slugs = []
roots = []
prefixes = ("data/annex/m1_trace_capture_direct/", "workloads/portable_lcd/results/")
for row in rows:
    if not isinstance(row, dict) or set(row) != {"slug", "historical_root", "current_root"}:
        raise SystemExit("path-alias row shape mismatch")
    slug = row["slug"]
    root = row["current_root"]
    if not isinstance(slug, str) or not slug or not isinstance(root, str):
        raise SystemExit("path-alias row scalar mismatch")
    pure = PurePosixPath(root)
    if pure.is_absolute() or "\\" in root or any(p in ("", ".", "..") for p in pure.parts):
        raise SystemExit("unsafe current M1 root")
    if not root.startswith(prefixes):
        raise SystemExit("current M1 root outside declared prefixes")
    slugs.append(slug)
    roots.append(root)
if slugs != sorted(slugs) or len(set(slugs)) != 17 or len(set(roots)) != 17:
    raise SystemExit("path-alias rows are not 17 unique sorted current roots")
print("M1_CURRENT_ROOTS=17")
PY

    "real_trace_replays_under_issue_model: test",

    for line in Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    if line.strip().endswith(": test")

    raise SystemExit(f"ignored Rust test set mismatch: expected={expected!r} actual={actual!r}")
print("RUST_IGNORED_NAME_SET=3")
PY

)

    raise SystemExit(f"hardware owner output is vacuous; missing {missing!r}")
```

## 11. Required response format

Return one consolidated ruling and answer every actual Q ID in ascending order. For protocol purposes, answer every Q with task-specific deliverables and a mechanical acceptance predicate; there are no serial remands. A disposition judges the contract literally requested by that Q ID against the embedded evidence and controlling constraints:

- `ACCEPT`: the requested contract is sufficient and may be implemented unchanged.
- `AMEND`: the requested contract is directionally valid but incomplete or defective; provide one complete replacement contract in the same answer.
- `REJECT`: implementing the requested contract would conflict with controlling authority or preserve an unsafe premise; state the authoritative replacement or typed prohibited/no-op result.
- `STOP`: the ruling depends on a genuinely user-owned choice or unavailable external hardware fact that cannot honestly be represented as a typed pending state. Missing repository evidence is a prompt defect, not permission to fabricate facts or request another message.

For each actual Q ID, emit exactly one standalone disposition line containing only one of these four literal forms, with the prompt's actual numeric identifier substituted for Qnnn:

Qnnn: ACCEPT
Qnnn: AMEND
Qnnn: REJECT
Qnnn: STOP

Choose exactly one form per actual Q ID; the four lines above specify the grammar and are not alternatives to reproduce together. Immediately after that Q ID's standalone line, and before the next Q ID's line, provide its rationale, complete ruling, exact invariants, states, identities, failure codes, implementation order, and positive/negative tests requested by that question. Do not repeat a Q ID, combine dispositions, defer rationale, cite a sibling response, or invent semantics for an unembedded dependency.

After all Q rulings, emit exactly one `Local blocker ledger` table with exactly one row for each blocker ID embedded in section 6 and no other rows. Required columns are: `blocker_id`, `question_ids`, `question_dispositions`, `blocker_disposition`, `severity`, `predecessor_blocker_ids`, `evidence_ids`, `producer_owner`, `validator_owner`, `schema_owner`, `test_owner`, `current_state`, `required_action`, `positive_predicate_ids`, `negative_control_ids`, `typed_failure_or_stop`, `offline_ready`, and `hardware_done`. IDs in every list must be sorted and must name only local IDs. `current_state` must be one of `implemented_verified`, `implemented_unverified`, `prototype`, `missing`, `external_pending`, or `prohibited`. Owners must be an embedded repository-relative path, `future:<repository-relative-path>`, `future_operator`, or `none`. The blocker disposition is derived mechanically from its Q dispositions with precedence `STOP > REJECT > AMEND > ACCEPT`; no other aggregation is allowed.

End with exactly one fenced `json` object named by the preceding literal line `Mechanical acceptance record`. It must contain: `schema_version` equal to 1; exact sorted `expected_question_ids`, `observed_disposition_ids`, `expected_blocker_ids`, and `ledger_blocker_ids`; a `checks` array in which each unique `Pnnn` check is defined once with `scope` (`response`, `offline`, or `hardware`), `owner`, `condition`, `evidence_or_command`, `expected`, and `result` (`pass`, `fail`, `pending`, or `prohibited`); and `response_complete_predicate_ids`, `offline_ready_predicate_ids`, and `hardware_done_predicate_ids` arrays. Each scope is the conjunction of its named checks. Also include Boolean results `response_complete`, `offline_implementation_ready`, and `hardware_done`, plus sorted `unsatisfied_predicate_ids`. A Boolean may be true only when every named check in its scope has result `pass`. Hardware-dependent checks without embedded admitted hardware evidence must be `pending` or `prohibited`, and `hardware_done` must be false. `authorized_for_handoff` must be false because this draft is not itself authorization.

Use no placeholders, pseudocode deferrals, truncated hashes, undefined helpers, requests for additional repository facts, or serial remands. Every branch must have an exact predicate. Distinguish repository-verifiable facts, offline implementation readiness, and future hardware completion.

For this bounded consultation, return only artifacts, transitions, ownership, schemas, tests, and predicates supported by the local blockers, questions, and decision evidence. The local blocker ledger is the sole integration artifact for this prompt and has no cross-prompt authority. Every conclusion must be decidable from this prompt alone; do not refer to, await, or condition an answer on another consultation.
